defects.reproduction: Read VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §7 and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md §5.6 against PaletteSlugBar.vue:2, :54-59, and the absent rotation/secret-retention affordances.
defects.proposedCure: Deletion (D-1). The composition W23 owns replaces it; remounting would install a shape the constitution has already superseded.

defects.defect: RETRACTED FINDING, recorded because the retraction is evidence. I flagged `border-muted-foreground` (:65) as a dead Tailwind class — both live siblings pointedly avoid it with inline styles, which reads exactly like a routed-around broken idiom. Measurement disproved it. The surviving design observation is that the admin state renders grey here while the ratified successor gives admin the gold identity.
defects.evidence: Live measurement in the running document: withBothClasses → border rgb(124,102,80) / color rgb(124,102,80); onlyTextMuted → border rgb(198,180,159); onlyBorderMuted → border rgb(124,102,80) / color rgb(28,25,23). The class resolves — RETRACTED. Surviving observation: PaletteSlugBar.vue:63-68 renders admin as `text-muted-foreground border-muted-foreground` (grey), while ProfileSection.vue:96 renders it `class="slug-pill cursor-default whitespace-nowrap gold-shimmer" style="border-color: var(--color-gold); color: var(--color-gold)"` — the ratified gold identity (owner feedback: "golden shimmer pill"). Two admin identities in one codebase; the orphan has the un-designed one.
defects.mechanism: divergent state treatment between an orphan and its successor — and, for the retracted arm, inference-from-siblings standing in for measurement
defects.reproduction: Inject the three class combinations into a .app-layout host on http://localhost:9000 and read getComputedStyle().borderTopColor — values above. The retraction is fully reproducible.
defects.proposedCure: None for the retracted arm. For the surviving arm: the admin identity is one composition (gold-shimmer, --color-gold) owned at the root, not two per-surface improvisations — D-1's deletion resolves it.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the application's ONLY login-failure copy is imperatively pushed into this never-mounted orphan through a template ref (`slugBarRef`) that is never bound to any element, so a wrong slug in the live dock fails completely silently: no message, no announcement, no state. Four links, each verified by file:line and exhaustive grep — useSlugMigration.ts:83-87 writes into `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`; the ref is created at :30 and returned at :121 but usePalettePorts.ts:257's only consumer (App.vue:153-156) reads three unrelated keys, so it is never bound; SlugEditLayer.vue:54 calls onSlugSwitch un-awaited and onSlugSwitch never rethrows, making SlugEditLayer's own catch unreachable; and SlugEditLayer declares `slugError` at :13 yet never renders it (template :75-119) while :56 tears the form down synchronously. The design defect is not staleness — it is that an error surface was made a private child capability (defineExpose + parent-held instance ref) instead of a property of the auth composition, so deleting the host silently deleted the app's failure affordance with zero type, test, or e2e signal. D-1 (the orphan itself) is the enabling condition; D-2 is the shipped, user-facing hole.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. Recorded for balance, since this seat was instructed not to hunt for reasons the component is fine: two things genuinely pass and are stated as such in the report. (1) Owner edict 6 (animations are never deleted) — the component consumes the global `vj-morph` family rather than hand-rolling a fourth transition name, and reduced motion is honoured for free by the global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:80 ("The global prefers-reduced-motion guard below neutralises all three"); no per-site work, no violation. (2) Owner edict 8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) — PaletteSlugBar.vue:131-145 are all runtime imports with no type-only import mis-declared. Edict 1 (no god modules) also passes at 243 focused lines. One further negative is recorded honestly as a RETRACTION (D-16): I inferred that `border-muted-foreground` was a dead class because both live siblings avoid it with inline styles; live measurement showed it resolves correctly (border rgb(124,102,80) with the class, rgb(198,180,159) without), and I retracted it. The evidence law earned its keep there — the inference was strong, plausible, and wrong.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) for demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m]) — declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 — the Tags filter is inert: SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55 binds `:checked` / `@update:checked`, but glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox has props ["modelValue","defaultValue","disabled","value","id","class","asChild","as","name","required"] and emits exactly ["update:modelValue"] (measured from the shipped bundle; `grep -rl "update:checked" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns nothing). A real mount+click emits only ["update:modelValue"], so `toggleTag` is unreachable and `update:selectedTags` never fires — the tag filter never reaches `currentFilterOpts()`. Because `modelValue` is unbound the control is UNCONTROLLED: it ticks visually, never reports, and never resets when "Clear all filters" empties `pm.selectedTags` — so the UI desynchronises permanently. The identical break sits on the tag WRITE path at TagEditPopover.vue:27-30; these are the demo's only two Checkbox usages, so no correct example exists to have caught it. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exits 0.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Recorded soundness, §5 of the report: every one of the 11 import specifiers at SearchFilterBar.vue:127-145 resolves within or below its own layer — no feature→shell, component→boot, or demo→src-internal edge exists. The library reach is HONEST and my "stale self-installed tarball" hypothesis was refuted by `tsc --traceResolution`: `@mkbabb/value.js/css` resolves through the repo's own package.json#exports self-name resolution to dist/subpaths/css.d.ts — the same edge a real npm consumer traverses. verbatimModuleSyntax clean (one type-only import, correctly marked). Vue 3.5 idioms correct (reactive props destructure, useTemplateRef in the sibling). My "dead CSS token" hypothesis was refuted by live measurement — --type-small/--leading-small/--radius-md/--duration-fast/--ease-standard/--font-serif/--accent all resolve. Every glass-ui prop OTHER than `variant` and Checkbox's `checked` was verified correct against measured props/emits. No console or page errors from this component in any of the four browse captures.)

defects.defect: The Tags filter is inert — the component binds `:checked` / `@update:checked`, an API glass-ui 7.0.0's Checkbox does not have. The control is left uncontrolled: it ticks visually, never emits anything the parent listens for, and never resets when the filter state is cleared.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:51-55. Spec: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/checkbox/Checkbox.vue.d.ts:4-12,19 declares `modelValue?: CheckedState | null` and `"update:modelValue": (value: CheckedState) => any`. Measured runtime: props=["modelValue","defaultValue","disabled","value","id","class","asChild","as","name","required"] emits=["update:modelValue"]. `grep -rl "update:checked" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` → no matches. Mount probe output: EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"] · DOM: <button data-slot="checkbox" … checked="false" role="checkbox" … data-state="checked"> (the `checked` prop landed as a raw fallthrough attribute; data-state flipped from the control's own internal state). `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → EXIT=0. Identical defect at demo/palettes/browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:27-30 (the tag WRITE path) — the demo's only other Checkbox usage.
defects.mechanism: Consumer speaks a retired design-system API; Vue admits unknown attrs as fallthrough and unknown on* handlers as native listeners, so the prop/emit rename is silent at both runtime and typecheck.
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config <scratch cfg pointing root at repo>; probe file mounts glass-ui Checkbox with {checked:false, 'onUpdate:checked', 'onUpdate:modelValue'}, clicks [role=checkbox], asserts the emit ledger → EMITTED: ["update:modelValue"]. In-app: open /#/browse ⋮ → Tags, tick a tag; the badge stays 0 and the wall does not change; then Clear all filters and the tick remains.
defects.proposedCure: Controlled v-model shape: `<Checkbox :model-value="selectedTags.includes(tag.name)" @update:model-value="() => toggleTag(tag.name)" />`, same at TagEditPopover.vue:27-30. Architecturally: make the class of defect impossible — FilterMenu becomes stateless over one `v-model:query` object (see L-4 cure), so no local/uncontrolled state can desynchronise from the wall; and close the gate that let glass-ui 7 land un-migrated (a vue/no-undef-properties-class rule for glass-ui components, since vue-tsc exits 0 on all of these today).

defects.defect: `variant="ghost"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7's Button — the string lands as a raw DOM attribute and the button renders at the default `emphasis="secondary"`. 51 sites across 20 demo files.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:5 and :111-115. Spec: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:3-9 — `export type ButtonEmphasis = "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"; interface ButtonProps { emphasis?: ButtonEmphasis; tone?: Tone; … }` — no `variant`. Live DOM at localhost:9000/#/browse: {hasVariantAttr:"ghost", dataEmphasis:"secondary", dataTone:"neutral", bg:"oklab(0.915626 0.00551148 0.0130686 / 0.52)", class:"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule …", size:"32x40"}. Button.props.emphasis.default === "secondary" (measured from the bundle). Visual confirmation: audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/browse.png — the ⋮ trigger is a filled chip, and BrowsePane.vue:69-76 `variant="outline"` Retry renders as a solid filled pill. Census: 51 `<Button variant=…>` sites — outline 28, ghost 19, primary-audacious 2, destructive 1, default 1.
defects.mechanism: Same as L-1: consumer speaks a retired design-system axis. glass-ui 7 replaced shadcn's single `variant` with orthogonal `emphasis` × `tone`; the demo was never migrated, and per-instance Tailwind size overrides were added to compensate.
defects.reproduction: node -e 'const m=await import("./node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js"); console.log(Object.keys(m.Button.props))' → no "variant". Then in the live app: document.querySelector('button[aria-label="Filters"]').getAttribute('variant') === "ghost" while .dataset.emphasis === "secondary"; getBoundingClientRect() === 32x40 despite class="h-8 w-8".
defects.proposedCure: Migrate the axis, no compat map (edict 2): ghost→emphasis="quiet", outline→emphasis="secondary", default→emphasis="primary", destructive→emphasis="primary" tone="danger". Delete the per-instance `h-8 w-8` / `h-7 w-full` overrides in favour of `size` (edict 5 — the measured 32x40 shows the override half-loses anyway). Wire a lint rule so a glass-ui prop rename fails loud instead of exiting 0.

defects.defect: The colour filter is the only one of five that never reaches the wire; BrowsePane re-implements the API's own OKLab matcher client-side over a single 50-row page, while the transport for the server-side filter is built, wired, and dead.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:336-349 (`colorSearchParams`, `displayedBrowse`, `const radius = 0.15`, `Math.hypot(c.L-L, c.a-a, c.b-b) <= radius`) vs api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-180 (`colorMatcherFor`, `query.colorRadius ?? 0.15`, `Math.sqrt(dL*dL+da*da+db*db) <= radius`) — same predicate, same default, same empty-array rule, same .some(). Transport exists: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-31 declares colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius, :50-53 serialises them; api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:89-92 validates them. Never set: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-60 `currentFilterOpts()` emits limit/sort/q/tier/tags only; `grep -rn "colorL" demo/` → 2 hits, both the declaration and the serialiser. BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts:19). Comment at BrowsePane.vue:353-354: "API also supports server-side via colorL/colorA/colorB params, but client-side is instant".
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership across the client/server boundary; an optimisation note became the only implementation, so the concept has two homes and the canonical one is unreachable.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'colorL' demo/ → only api/palettes.ts:27,50. Read useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-60 — no color* key. Therefore any colour search narrows only the loaded page: a matching palette on keyset page 2 of the commons is invisible and the wall reports empty.
defects.proposedCure: Delete colorSearchParams and displayedBrowse. Put `color: { L, a, b, radius } | null` in the shared filter state next to tier/tags and add three lines to currentFilterOpts(). crud-list.ts becomes the single home for OKLab distance; Math.hypot leaves the demo entirely. Pair with publishing `deltaE(a,b)` from @mkbabb/value.js/color so the API stops hand-rolling it too (`grep -rn "deltaE\|colorDistance" src/` → zero hits in a colour library).

defects.defect: The five filters this one component emits have four different owners, and three of them are homed in the *dialog* sub-feature. There is no filter-state module; useBrowsePalettes is a 240-line god module holding filter state + keyset pagination + CRUD.
defects.evidence: sort → useBrowsePalettes.ts:116; tier/selectedTags/clearFilters → demo/palettes/browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts:91-100 (imported by BrowsePane.vue:255-265 from './browser/dialog'); colorSearch → BrowsePane.vue:351 (pane-local); text → useBrowsePalettes.ts:43 AND :57. That file's own header at :17-18 documents the mismatch: "Browse filter handlers (onTierChange / onTagsChange / onClearFilters): mutate pm.tierFilter / pm.selectedTags and reload." activeFilterCount (SearchFilterBar.vue:189-195) reads tier+selectedTags from PROPS but colorSearchActive from a LOCAL ref (:171); onClearAll (:227-232) must fire TWO events to reset one concept, caught by BrowsePane.vue:328-332 and :357-359. `wc -l demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts` = 240.
defects.mechanism: No unique semantic home for the 'browse query' concept, so each filter landed wherever its handler was first written; the god module had no room for it.
defects.reproduction: Read the six emit sites in SearchFilterBar.vue:154-161 and follow each binding in BrowsePane.vue:15-26 to its handler. Four distinct modules, two of them (dialog composables, pane-local) semantically wrong.
defects.proposedCure: NEW demo/palettes/browse/useBrowseQuery.ts owning { text, sort, tier, tags, color, radius } + toListOptions(): ListPalettesOptions + activeCount + clear(). useBrowsePalettes becomes useBrowsePage (paging + fetch only); vote/rename/delete/visibility/fork lift into usePaletteMutations.ts; useDialogBrowseActions.ts is DELETED. SearchFilterBar becomes a stateless FilterMenu over one `v-model:query` — which also makes L-1's desync arithmetically impossible and collapses the double-fired clear.

defects.defect: A hand-rolled 6-digit-hex regex gates the field one line in front of the full CSS Color Level 4 parser it already imports; rejected input is silently replaced by the swatch colour, and the field's own placeholder advertises a syntax the regex refuses.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:218 `const hex = text.startsWith("#") && /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i.test(text) ? text : pickerHex.value;` — with hexToOklab (:205-211) calling parseColorIn, and placeholder="#hex, hsl(...)" at :92, pickerHex default "#4488cc" at :170. Measured library capability: parseCssColor+convertColor resolve all of `hsl(210 60% 50%)` → oklab 0.5883 -0.0443 -0.1319, `oklch(0.7 0.15 250)` → 0.7000 -0.0513 -0.1410, `rebeccapurple` → 0.4403 0.0882 -0.1339, `#48c` → 0.6136 -0.0415 -0.1175, `color(display-p3 0.2 0.4 0.8)` → 0.5340 -0.0363 -0.1775. The regex accepts one of the five. The `"none"` guard at :207-209 is unreachable given the gate — it defends the impossible while the possible failure is silenced.
defects.mechanism: A second, narrower, incompatible parser placed in front of the canonical total parser; failure masked by a fallback instead of surfaced (edict 2: masking fallbacks).
defects.reproduction: Type `rebeccapurple` (or `hsl(210 60% 50%)`, or `#48c`) into the Find-by-Colour field and press Search. The emitted colorSearch triple is that of #4488cc, not the typed colour. No error, no visual difference from success — colorSearchActive goes true and the badge increments.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the regex. `parseColorIn(text, "oklab")` inside a try, surfacing PickerColorError as field-invalid state via glass-ui Input's existing `invalid` prop (measured present). The library is a total parser; stop putting a partial one in front of it.

defects.defect: One component carries two colour engines: SearchFilterBar reaches the library for colour while its only child, MiniColorPicker, hand-rolls the full HSV↔RGB↔hex conversion — inside the demo of a colour library.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:132 imports ./MiniColorPicker.vue, rendered :66-81. MiniColorPicker.vue imports only vue + ../../../ui/popover + ../../../ui/button — no value.js. Its :88-114 is an HSV→RGB sextant switch + toHex padder; :118-134 the RGB→HSV inverse, carrying its own hue hack at :126 `if (d === 0) return; // keep existing hue`. @mkbabb/value.js/color publishes hsv, rgb, convertColor, toRgba8 (src/subpaths/color.ts); demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:56 already declares HSV channel metadata. MEMORY records the hue-drift lesson at library level (stableHue in useColorModel). The two engines meet via a watch→emit→prop→watch round trip (MiniColorPicker.vue:116,118 ↔ SearchFilterBar.vue:175-178).
defects.mechanism: Duplicate ownership of a concept the library exists to own; a library-level lesson re-learned badly at component level.
defects.reproduction: grep -n '^import' demo/palettes/browser/search/MiniColorPicker.vue → vue + two ui shims, no @mkbabb/value.js. Then read :88-134.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both conversion blocks. `convertPickerColor(color, "hsv")` and `colorToCss(color)` from demo/color-session/ do all of it; the SV canvas becomes a thin h/s/v view over one AnyColor (ColorField.vue in the proposed lattice). One colour engine per demo.

defects.defect: Text search composes two incompatible matchers in series — a MongoDB $text search on the server and a substring filter on the client — producing three distinct behavioural regimes for one field.
defects.evidence: Server: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:95-96 `const q = query.q?.trim(); if (q) f.$text = { $search: q };` (stemmed, whole-word, index-driven). Client: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:43-45 `useFilteredList(remotePalettes, deps.searchQuery, (p,q) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q))` (substring). Gate: useBrowsePalettes.ts:57 `...(q.length >= 2 ? { q } : {})`. Regimes: 0 chars → neither; 1 char → client substring only; ≥2 → server $text THEN client substring.
defects.mechanism: Two homes for one concept across the client/server boundary, composed serially rather than one being canonical.
defects.reproduction: Search `blu` on a commons containing "Blue Ridge": $text has no whole-word token `blu`, the server returns nothing, the wall is empty. Search `ocean sunset`: $text OR-matches and returns rows, then the client requires the literal contiguous string in name/slug and discards nearly all of them.
defects.proposedCure: One matcher. The API owns the text index — delete filteredBrowse from the browse path and lower the q gate to 1 character. useFilteredList survives for PalettesPane's genuinely local list.

defects.defect: The library type `Channel = number | "none"` forces every consumer to invent its own policy; four demo sites do so and none agree. The library publishes no projection off it.
defects.evidence: SearchFilterBar.vue:205-211 → THROW ("Hex color produced missing OKLab channels"); demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:127-128 → return null; demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownColors.ts:39-42,52 → THROW on L/C with a different message, COERCE H→0; demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useImageSampler.ts:39-41 → pass "none" through as display text. src/subpaths/color.ts exports the `Channel` type and no resolver. Related: `grep -rn "deltaE\|colorDistance" src/` → zero hits.
defects.mechanism: Missing library-level projection → four ad-hoc homes for one policy.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'channels' demo/ | grep '"none"' — four call sites, four disciplines.

Since every showConfirm caller lives in this one file, extract the whole 33-line confirm engine (254-286) — it removes a concern from a 391-line SFC rather than adding to one (edict 1).

defects.defect: NEW. User search is a client-side filter over a hard-coded 50-row window. The server's `q` parameter is declared and wired but NEVER sent, so searching for a user who exists beyond row 50 renders "No users found." — a false negative in the admin lookup that gates destruction.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:21-32 declares listUsers(token, limit=20, offset=0, q?) and forwards q. `grep -rn 'listUsers(' demo/` returns exactly ONE call site: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:59 `const res = await listUsers(token, 50);` — no offset, no q, ever. The filter is client-side at useAdminUsers.ts:29-34. MEASURED (probe-C2-implementation.json N4_search, chromium and webkit identical), server holding 60 users with 10 named `zed-offpage-user-*` outside the first 50: {listRequests:["GET /admin/users?limit=50&offset=0"], qParamSent:false, requestsAfterTyping:0, afterSearch:{rows:0, emptyPlate:true, countLine:"50 users"}}. Witness frames-C2/N4-webkit-search-false-negative.png shows, simultaneously on one screen: header badge [50], "50 users", "· ROSTER CLEAR · No users found.", and a DISABLED `Prune empty` while three empty users exist server-side.
defects.mechanism: A — a value is sourced from a different authority than the one that acts on it. The search authority is the client's 50-row cache; the corpus is the server's. Two search authorities for one concern.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N4 leg) — stubs a 60-user roster, types `zed-offpage`, records 0 rows / emptyPlate true / 0 requests issued.
defects.proposedCure: The parameters already exist. Debounce searchQuery into `listUsers(token, limit, offset, q)`, consume `res.total` (which useAdminUsers.ts:60 currently discards), and mount the `PaginationBar.vue` that already sits UNUSED in this component's own directory — the sibling audit and flagged panels already do exactly this (useAdminAudit.ts:62, AdminAuditPanel.vue:83). Deleting the client-side filter at useAdminUsers.ts:32-34 is part of the cure, not a casualty of it. No new component, no new directory (edict 3).

defects.defect: NEW. With no admin token the roster renders the success-with-no-data plate — "· roster clear · No users found." — with no mention of authentication anywhere on the page, and a fully enabled Refresh button that issues ZERO requests forever.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:54-57 — `const token = getAdminToken(); if (!token) return;` returns BEFORE loadingUsers and BEFORE usersLoadError are touched, so the panel's state ladder (AdminUsersPanel.vue:46 loading -> :51 loadError -> :63 users.length===0) falls through to the third arm. MEASURED (probe-C2-implementation.json N5_noToken, chromium and webkit identical): {mainText:"Users 0 Manage accounts and permissions. 0 users Prune empty Refresh · ROSTER CLEAR · No users found. …", rows:0, hasUnreachable:false, hasSignIn:false, refreshDisabled:false, adminRequestsBefore:10, adminRequestsAfterRefresh:10}. Witness frames-C2/N5-{chromium,webkit}-no-token-roster-clear.png.
defects.mechanism: B — failure, absence and emptiness are the same value. `void` is being used as an error channel: a function that can fail three ways (no credential / request failed / succeeded) returns void for two of them.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N5 leg). Manually: clear localStorage key `palette-admin-token`, load http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users.
defects.proposedCure: Add `unauthenticated` as a member of the discriminated union the composable should return (the same union that cures the prior seat's C-5 count-over-error contradiction): `unauthenticated | loading | error | resolved`. The panel's arm for it is a sign-in affordance, not the clear-roster plate. AdminPane.vue already gates on `pm.isAdminAuthenticated` elsewhere, so the affordance has a home.

defects.defect: NEW. An open disclosure is never invalidated by Refresh. The admin presses Refresh precisely because they suspect the screen is stale, and the one region they are actively reading is the one region the button does not touch.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 — toggleUserExpand is the ONLY writer of `userPalettes`; nothing watches the `users` prop, nothing watches `loading`. MEASURED (probe-C2-implementation.json N3_staleAcrossRefresh, both engines): expand alpha at server generation 1, flip the server to generation 2, press Refresh -> {paletteFetches:["GET /admin/users/alpha-keeper-0001/palettes"] (exactly one, ever), afterRefresh:{stillExpanded:true, showsGen1:true, showsGen2:false}}. CONTROL (probe-C2b-controls.json K3_reexpandControl, both engines): {afterFirstExpand:"GEN-1", afterRefresh:"GEN-1", afterCollapseReexpand:"GEN-2", paletteFetches:[2 requests]} — collapsing and re-expanding DOES pull GEN-2, proving the server truth genuinely changed and the transport is healthy. This is staleness, not caching.
defects.mechanism: A — the disclosure's authority is one gesture, the roster's is another; two independent cells joined by nothing. "Refresh" means two different things on two halves of the same pane.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N3 leg) then `probe-C2b-controls.mjs` (K3 control).
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of the C-1 cure. Once the disclosure is a keyed resource — a colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` returning {palettes, loading, error} driven by watch(slugRef) with an AbortController — invalidation is a watch on the roster's fetch generation, and Refresh means one thing on the whole pane.

defects.defect: NEW trigger for the carried C-1 mechanism, with a strictly worse signature: after the operator EXPLICITLY COLLAPSES a row mid-flight, that cancelled fetch later overwrites a different row's already-settled, correct disclosure — silently, with no loading state in between.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-357 — the collapse arm returns early, does NOT reset loadingUserPalettes, and does not cancel the in-flight request whose row it is collapsing. MEASURED (probe-C2-implementation.json N6_collapseMidflight, chromium and webkit identical) with alpha delayed 1500ms and beta 40ms; expand alpha -> wait 250ms -> COLLAPSE alpha -> wait 100ms -> expand beta: midway = {openRow:"beta-drifte r-0002 2 Palettes", region:"BETA-DRIFTER-0002-PALETTE 2 0"} (correct); settled = {openRow:"beta-drifte r-0002 2 Palettes", region:"ALPHA-KEEPER-0001-PALETTE 2 0"} (alpha's data inside beta's row). AdminUsersPanel.vue:150 then binds the card's admin delete to `user.slug` — beta — so the prior seat's measured wrong-owner destruction is reachable from this gesture too.
defects.mechanism: A — the response's key is not the row's key; `expandedUserSlug` and `userPalettes` are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order. Also mechanism C: an in-flight request with no termination path.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N6 leg).
defects.proposedCure: The same AbortController-keyed resource as C-1, with one addition the prior cure must not forget: a sequence counter placed only on the fetch path does NOT close this variant, because the collapse arm must also cancel. Making a response for a non-current key unrepresentable — rather than policed — closes both triggers at once and removes userPalettes/removeUserPalette/updatePaletteTier/clearUserPalettes from defineExpose as a side effect.

defects.defect: A FAILED prune is reported to the operator as the reassuring "No empty users to prune". Three distinct outcomes — the server refused / the credential is gone / there was genuinely nothing to prune — collapse into one sentence, with no role=alert anywhere.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:186-199 — `if (!token) return 0;` (path 2, NEW this seat) and `catch (e:any) { console.warn(...); return 0; }` (path 1, the D seat's). AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-309 maps 0 to "No empty users to prune". MEASURED by the D seat's probe-D2d-prune-failure.mjs with the prune endpoint fulfilled 500 application/problem+json: `[warn] Failed to prune empty users: Internal Server Error` / PRUNE-FAILURE: {message:"No empty users to prune", anyErrorRole:false} while the toolbar simultaneously reads "· 2 empty", ~220px away in the same type register. Frame frames-D2/G-prune-FAILED-desktop-light.png.
defects.mechanism: B — failure, absence and emptiness are the same value. `0` is being used as an error channel. `onPruneDone(count: number)` is the signature defect: a number cannot express failure, so no downstream code can.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-D2d-prune-failure.mjs` (D seat's, re-runnable against live :9000). Cross-seat corroboration: filed independently on the design axis in challenge-D-design.md; re-filed here because the mechanism is a code defect, and because the no-token path into the same string is new.
defects.proposedCure: The result channel must carry the three outcomes the action actually has — pruned N / nothing to prune / failed with the machine reason — in the error register already ratified at AdminUsersPanel.vue:51-62. Change the signature before the copy: `onPruneDone(result: {ok:true, pruned:number} | {ok:false, reason:string})`.

defects.defect: NEW. The `aria-label` on both loading containers is discarded by BOTH engines (ARIA prohibits naming role=generic), so what is actually announced is three identical "Loading" live regions and never "Loading users".
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:46 `<div v-if="loading" class="grid gap-3" aria-label="Loading users">` and :135 `aria-label="Loading palettes"` — a div with no role maps to ARIA `generic`; ARIA 1.2 §5.2.8.4 ("Roles which cannot be named") lists generic among the roles for which aria-label is PROHIBITED. MEASURED (probe-C2-implementation.json N1_loadingAria, chromium and webkit identical). DOM: [{tag:"div", role:null, ariaLabel:"Loading users", childRoles:["status","status","status"]}, then 3x {tag:"div", role:"status", ariaLabel:"Loading"}]. Accessible tree: ariaSnapshotLoadingLines = ['  - status "Loading"', '  - status "Loading"', '  - status "Loading"'], snapshotMentionsLoadingUsers = FALSE. Source of the triplication: AdminListSkeleton.vue:10-11 carries role="status" aria-label="Loading" and is rendered `v-for="i in 3"`.
defects.mechanism: B-adjacent (announcement): the name the author wrote is dead, and the announcement that survives is decoration repeated N times. Paired with the prior seat's C-7 (the RESULT of destroying users is announced ZERO times) the panel's announcement budget is exactly inverted.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminUsersPanel/probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N1 leg) — holds the roster in `loading` for 6s and reads both the DOM and Playwright's ARIA snapshot in both engines.
defects.proposedCure: role="status" belongs on the CONTAINER, once, carrying the name; the repeated skeletons are decoration and should be aria-hidden="true" rather than three competing live regions. Since AdminListSkeleton.vue is consumed by five admin panels, moving the announcement off the atom and onto the container is one edit that corrects five surfaces (edict 1: fix at the shared atom, not per instance).

defects.defect: NEW. An unchecked cast asserts a server-supplied `string` into a three-member union, twice, on the same value.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:371-380 — `function updatePaletteTier(paletteSlug: string, tier: string)` then `tier: tier as "standard" | "featured" | "archived"`. Caller demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:92 casts `result.tier` identically. A server returning any fourth tier value lands an off-union string in Palette.tier, which PaletteCard then branches on.
defects.mechanism: The type system being told to stop looking at a trust boundary. Not a runtime defect against today's constrained server.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static. Labelled a type-safety observation, not a reproduced failure; today's server is constrained to the three values.
defects.proposedCure: Type the parameter as the union at the boundary and narrow once where the server's response is decoded, not at two consumption sites. If the response really is unconstrained, validate it once in the api/ layer.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat, re-corroborated by my C-19). The concurrent-expand race renders one user's palettes inside another user's open disclosure and then routes the admin delete against the WRONG owner.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:352-365 — `userPalettes.value = await pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)` with no generation guard; `finally` clears loading for whichever request settles first. Line 150 binds the card's admin delete to the ROW's slug, never the palette's owner: `@admin-delete="emit('adminDeleteUserPalette', $event, user.slug)"`. Prior probe-impl-c3.json (chromium and webkit identical): t_alphaLanded = {openRow:"beta-drifter-00022Pale", disclosure:"ALPHA-PALETTE-AAA 2 0"}, RACE_REPRODUCED true. Prior probe-impl-c3b.json: deleteRequests = ["http://localhost:9077/admin/palettes/alpha-p-1"] issued from beta's row; betaBadge 2->1, alphaBadge 4->4 (both numbers now wrong, in opposite directions). Re-corroborated at this HEAD by probe-C2-implementation.json N6 via a different gesture.
defects.mechanism: A — a value is sourced from a different authority than the one that acts on it; expandedUserSlug and userPalettes are two independent cells joined only by wall-clock order.
defects.reproduction: `VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:9077 npx vite --port 9077` then `node .../probe-impl-c3.mjs` and `.../probe-impl-c3b.mjs`. Cheaper route at this HEAD: `node .../probe-C2-implementation.mjs` (N6 leg) against live :9000, no second server needed.
defects.proposedCure: A colocated `useAdminUserPalettes(slugRef)` keyed resource: watch(slugRef, {flush:'post'}) + AbortController cancelled on key change, returning {palettes, loading, error} bound to the key it was fetched for. The race becomes unrepresentable rather than policed; it also supplies C-4's missing error cell and dissolves the defineExpose imperative surface.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). The prune confirmation quotes a SEARCH-FILTERED count for a GLOBALLY SCOPED destruction: the number that describes and gates the action comes from a client-side view filter; the number destroyed is whatever the server finds.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 emptyCount over the `users` prop; AdminPane.vue:28 `:users="pm.filteredAdminUsers.value"` (filtered, useAdminUsers.ts:29-34); demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69 pruneEmptyUsers(token) — POST /admin/users/prune-empty takes no filter, no body, no slug list. Prior probe-impl.json C2 (both engines): unfiltered "· 3 empty"; filtered on `gamma` -> "· 1 empty", dialog "Prune 1 empty users? This will permanently delete 1 user…" while the server deletes 3. defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl.mjs` (C2 leg, requires :9077); the disabled inverse arm reproduces on live :9000 via `node .../probe-C2c-window.mjs` (W2b frame).

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). The roster prints a total it never measured and offers no second page — 87 of 137 users unreachable.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). A FAILED disclosure fetch costumes as "No palettes." — in the file whose own comment forbids exactly that.

The row's badge still reads the true count two lines above. Indictment: AdminUsersPanel.vue:49-50 "error != empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster."
defects.mechanism: B — failure, absence and emptiness are the same value.
defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl.mjs` (C4 leg, requires :9077).

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). "0 users" is printed above "The roster is unreachable." — the file's own A-3 invariant, guarded for `loading` and not for `loadError`.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:5-10 — the comment names the contradiction ("a '0 users' line above three loading skeletons is a self-contradiction") and the guard is `v-if="!loading"` only. Prior probe-impl.json C1 with the users endpoint at 500, both engines byte-identical: mainText "Users 0 Manage accounts and permissions. 0 users Prune empty Refresh The roster is unreachable. Internal Server Error Retry"; countLine "0 users"; hasUnreachable true. AdminPane.vue:118-121 repeats it in the header badge (guards adminCount on pm.loadingUsers only).
defects.mechanism: B — four states (unresolved/loading/error/resolved) modelled as three independent booleans plus a nullable string, which is what lets "count" exist inside "error".
defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl.mjs` (C1 leg, requires :9077).
defects.proposedCure: Not `&& !loadError` in two places. A discriminated union returned by the composable makes the count a member of the RESOLVED variant only, and the contradiction becomes unrepresentable in both consumers at once. Same union that absorbs my C-17.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). Every interactive row is a role="button" that CONTAINS two focusable descendants, has no aria-controls, and computes its accessible name from its contents — absorbing the label of the destructive button inside it.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-131 — the row div takes role="button" + tabindex=0 + aria-expanded and contains the action cluster at :106-131. Prior probe-impl.json C5_a11y, both engines identical: [{ariaExpanded:"false", ariaControls:null, focusableDescendants:2, descendantLabels:["Palettes","Delete user beta-drifter-0002"], accName:"beta-drifte r-0002 2 Palettes"}, …]. WAI-ARIA forbids focusable descendants inside role=button (axe rule nested-interactive, WCAG 4.1.2). The disclosure region at :134 has no id and is never associated with the control that toggles it. Two-engine, DOM-structural, wholly independent of macOS Full Keyboard Access — MT-F022 does not absorb it.
defects.mechanism: The row was made the affordance because "there is NO other keyboard path to a user's palettes" (comment at :70-77) — that premise is the thing to fix, not to build on.
defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl.mjs` (C5 leg, requires :9077).
defects.proposedCure: Hoist the disclosure into a real sibling <button> (a chevron carrying aria-expanded + aria-controls and its own name), leaving the row a plain container. This is exactly the `interactive` prop the adjudicated MT-AU1 scope already moves into AdminListItem.vue — it should carry the corrected shape, not the current one.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). The destructive action's only receipt is un-announced (no live region) AND is truncated ~1s early by the previous beat's uncancelled timer. My C-15 makes the double-beat reachable from a single gesture.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:16-20 — a bare <span> inside a Transition; no role, no aria-live, no live ancestor. Prior probe-impl.json: C5_beatLiveRegion = [] (zero live regions contain the beat text) while C5_a11y.liveRegions within <main> = 1 (the OTHER pane's empty plate). WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA). Contrast inside this one directory: the LOADING state is announced three times over (AdminListSkeleton.vue:10 role=status, v-for i in 3) while the result of destroying users is announced zero times. Truncation: AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-309 `setTimeout(..., 3000)` with no handle, never cleared — prior C5_doubleBeat, chromium beat2 armed t0+2332ms yet gone by t0+4300ms (entitled to t0+5332ms); webkit beat2 armed t0+2045ms, same outcome. `grep -c onUnmounted` on the file -> 0, so the closure writes to a dead ref after unmount.
defects.mechanism: C — work that is started is never given a way to be finished or cancelled.
defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl.mjs` (C5 leg, requires :9077). The single-gesture double-beat reproduces on live :9000 via `node .../probe-C2b-controls.mjs` (K2b: two prunes, one receipt).
defects.proposedCure: The existing ActionFeedback.vue atom already does clearTimeout-before-re-arm correctly and is the right home — but it must gain the onUnmounted teardown it lacks (grep -c onUnmounted on it -> 0) and a role="status" before twelve consumers inherit the hole.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). One malformed row denies the entire admin console — the panel has zero row-level tolerance, so ErrorBoundary catches a raw JS engine string and the whole roster, Prune, Refresh and every delete disappear.

Prior probe-impl-c10 with one row `slug: null` (the exact contract violation e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:100-135 documents): chromium alert=True rows=0 bodyLen=125 "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length') Try again"; webkit alert=True rows=0 bodyLen=118 "null is not an object (evaluating 'slug.length')". deleteLabels [] — every control gone.

defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl-c10.mjs` (requires :9077).
defects.proposedCure: The crash belongs to the component, not the boundary. A row whose slug is not a string is a row the panel should not render, or should render as a flagged non-actionable row. The boundary is the last resort, not the design.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat). An empty slug produces a destructive control whose accessible name is "Delete user " — a trailing space — and a confirmation dialog whose slug pill renders empty.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:126 `:aria-label="`Delete user ${user.slug}`"`; the pill at :97-101 renders empty (slugHead("") -> "", slugTail("") -> "") and the dialog pill at :165-169 likewise. Prior probe-impl-c10 with slug "": rows=1 interactive=1 alert=False, deleteLabels ["Sort users","Delete user "]. Invisible to the accessible-name battery leg, which tests for EMPTINESS, not for identifying content.
defects.mechanism: B — an empty slug is a valid render; a destructive control whose name does not identify its target, and a confirmation that confirms nothing nameable.
defects.reproduction: `node .../probe-impl-c10.mjs` (requires :9077).
defects.proposedCure: Same as C-8 — reject or flag rows that violate the slug contract at the boundary rather than rendering an unnamed destructive control.

defects.defect: CARRIED (prior seat), RE-MEASURED AT THIS HEAD. The vitest tier cannot mount any component at all, and the e2e gate stays green through nearly every finding in this report — seven of my eight new rows included.
defects.evidence: Re-run at HEAD 7cae8bd0: `grep -c 'plugin-vue\|plugins' vitest.config.ts` -> 0; `grep -rn 'from ".*\.vue"' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` -> 0; `grep -rln '@vue/test-utils' test/ demo/test/ e2e/ | wc -l` -> 0; `grep -rln 'AdminUsers\|prune' test/ demo/test/ | wc -l` -> 0. vitest.config.ts declares no `plugins` key, so .vue is untransformable; @vue/test-utils and jsdom are devDependencies with zero importers. Coverage is four e2e specs (admin-walk, admin-populated, a11y-authed-admin, flows/user-status). NAMED MUTATIONS THAT STAY GREEN — prior seat's: replace line 241 with `users.length` (prune scope becomes the whole roster, every spec still passes). MINE: C-15 delete `confirmOpen.value=false` and close on a 400ms timer (specs assert a DELETE fires, and it does); C-16 make the client filter `filter(() => true)` (no spec asserts a filtered row count); C-17 `if (!token) { adminUsers.value = []; return; }` (identical render, no spec is unauthenticated); C-18 make emit('refresh') a no-op panel-side (no spec presses Refresh with a row expanded); C-19 any change to the collapse arm is invisible (no spec expands a row twice); C-20 delete both aria-labels (the battery asserts nameless==[] over BUTTONS, not containers); C-21 `return 0` unconditionally (the POST still fires, which is all user-status.spec.ts checks). Also `expect(report.controlsChecked).toBeGreaterThan(0)` — the spec's own guard against an empty-scope false green — is satisfied by the toolbar's Prune/Refresh/Sort buttons with ZERO user rows present.
defects.mechanism: A vacuous gate: the assertions are about whether a request fires, never about whether the right thing was described, scoped, or shown.
defects.reproduction: Run the four greps above from the repo root; then apply any mutation in the table and run `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/admin`.
defects.proposedCure: Add `@vitejs/plugin-vue` to vitest.config.ts and mount this component with @vue/test-utils (already a devDependency, zero importers) — the scope questions above (which count is quoted, which key the response belongs to, which state renders) are unit questions and do not need a browser. The e2e tier should assert the DESCRIPTION the operator accepted, not merely that a request left.

The subject imports value.js not at all. No false proof of the public API. (2) `Badge variant="secondary"` (`:102`) is VALID — glass-ui's Badge does declare `variant` (`dist/components/badge/Badge.vue.d.ts:4`), unlike Button; L-4 is scoped to Button and a mechanical sweep touching Badge would be a regression. Only the dialog binding (L-18) is mis-rung. (4) `vj-celebrate` degrades correctly without geometry vars — all four custom properties carry fallbacks (`animations.css:156-165`); no animation deleted or inlined (edict 6 clean). (5) The three-parallel-`useDark` suspect named in the brief is CURED — all 10 live sites import the single `useGlobalDark` from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dark`; only two stale COMMENTS survive (incl. adjacent to the cited `useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:76`). defects.defect: The state layer imports the view and drives it through a template ref. `useAdminUsers.ts:14` imports the SFC type; `:27` holds its instance; `:95/117/132/146` + `usePalettePorts.ts:123` mutate component-private state through a 5-member `defineExpose` (`AdminUsersPanel.vue:389`). The handle is published on the app-wide ADMIN port (`usePalettePorts.ts:197`) and the mount site BORROWS it (`AdminPane.vue:134`). Type cycle: useAdminUsers -> browser/admin/index.ts -> AdminUsersPanel.vue -> usePalettePorts -> useAdminUsers. Consequence: `onAdminDeleteUserPalette` (`useAdminUsers.ts:112-125`) updates the panel copy and the server but NEVER `deps.remotePalettes` — while its sibling `onAdminDeletePalette` (`:101-110`) does — so Browse renders a deleted palette until reload.

Structural half: grep -c 'if (!token) return' demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts -> 11; across demo/palettes/*.ts -> 22; grep -rn 'requiresAdmin|adminOnly|guard' demo/shell/ -> nothing.
defects.mechanism: Authorization is a ROUTE precondition modelled as a per-method silent early return. The precondition has no home, so it is re-asserted 22 times, and the one place it matters (the panel's state model) never learns about it — the panel models 3 states (loading/error/empty) where the domain has 4.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED end to end: (1) ensure localStorage has no 'palette-admin-token'; (2) navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users; (3) network log filtered users|/api/ is EMPTY — no request was ever issued; (4) DOM contains 'No users found' and the toolbar reads '0 users'. The app knows it is logged out (the dock says 'Login') while the panel asserts the roster is clear.
defects.proposedCure: One gate at the composition boundary: an `auth: "admin"` flag in demo/shell/viewSchema.ts honoured once in useViewManager, or an <AdminGate> in AdminPane.vue, rendering an authentication plate when !isAdminAuthenticated. Inside the gate getAdminToken() is a non-null contract — construct useAdminUsers WITH a token rather than letting it re-ask — and all 22 guards delete. The panel then never needs an 'unauthorized' state because it never mounts unauthorized.

defects.defect: 51 dead `variant` props on `<Button>` across 22 demo files (5 in the subject). glass-ui 7.0.0 ButtonProps declares emphasis/tone/size/iconOnly/loading — there is NO `variant`. Every such button renders at the default emphasis and the prop falls through onto the DOM as an inert HTML attribute. The subject speaks BOTH vocabularies 40 lines apart: dead `variant` at :22,33,58,114,123 and correct Glass 7 `emphasis`/`tone` at :174,175. Concretely damaging: the W5-12/F-8 intent documented at :107-111 ('the per-row destructive is quieted to ink-at-rest — red arrives on hover/focus, never as 5 resting beacons down the list') was expressed as variant="ghost" and is therefore SILENTLY REVERTED — the row delete renders at the same emphasis as the 'Palettes' button beside it.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 (no `variant` member). LIVE DOM measurement, http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users: {"text":"Prune empty","attrs":["data-slot=\"button\"","data-emphasis=\"secondary\"","data-tone=\"neutral\"","data-size=\"sm\"",…,"variant=\"outline\"",…]} and the same for "Refresh" — data-emphasis="secondary" is glass-ui's DEFAULT, and variant="outline" is a fallthrough attribute styling nothing. Fleet count (own python regex over every `<Button …>` tag-open in demo/**/*.vue): 51 sites across 22 files; 5 in AdminUsersPanel.vue at lines 22,33,58,114,123.
defects.mechanism: The design-system public surface changed at the 6->7 upgrade and this component was only half-migrated. Nothing can catch it: Vue treats an undeclared attribute on a component as a fallthrough attr, so vue-tsc does not flag it, and eslint.config.js has no rule in this space — CI is documented fully green at HEAD (db77dbd8) while all 51 sites ship.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED: navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users and evaluate `[...document.querySelectorAll('button')].filter(b=>/Prune|Refresh/i.test(b.textContent)).map(b=>[...b.attributes].map(a=>a.name+'='+a.value))` — both buttons show data-emphasis="secondary" alongside a stray variant="outline".
defects.proposedCure: Mechanical rewrite: outline->emphasis="secondary", ghost->emphasis="quiet", destructive->tone="destructive", default->emphasis="primary" (row delete becomes emphasis="quiet" tone="destructive", which also retires its two per-instance hover:text-destructive utilities). Structural: wire the installed, unused `vue/no-restricted-static-attribute` ({key:'variant', element:'Button'}) so the drift cannot recur. Relay to glass-ui BH: the rename shipped with no consumer trap — request `variant?: never` or inheritAttrs:false + an explicit allowlist so an unrecognised design-token prop is a VISIBLE no-op.

defects.defect: Injection keys live in the module that wires them, so importing one Symbol drags 26 modules into a leaf panel. AdminUsersPanel.vue:200 imports ADMIN_PORT_KEY from a 275-line module that imports 15 composables, the API client, auth, session tokens and storage. Systemic: of the 22 modules importing usePalettePorts, 21 import ONLY a key symbol; exactly one imports providePalettePorts, the module's actual product. Five of the 21 are SHELL files reaching into the palettes FEATURE for an identity key assembled entirely out of demo/platform/auth/*.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (275 L, imports at :1-23); demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:200. Shell->feature edges: demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13. The 26-module closure figure is r2's measurement (scratchpad closure.py), not re-run this pass; the module shape is re-confirmed by reading.
defects.mechanism: Keys have no home. The correct shape already exists in this repo and this very component consumes it correctly at :187 — demo/color-session/keys.ts, 27 lines, six InjectionKeys, type-only imports, zero runtime weight.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis-free structural claim confirmed by file:line and import counts; the 26-module weight figure is carried from r2's closure script and was not independently re-measured this pass.
defects.proposedCure: Add demo/palettes/keys.ts (5 InjectionKeys + the 5 port interfaces, type-only imports) — the twin of a file already in the tree, so no new directory and no new concept (edict 3 satisfied). usePalettePorts.ts then imports the keys in order to provide them and nothing else imports it at all. Move session/identity keys one step further to demo/platform/auth/keys.ts and the shell->feature edge dissolves. 21 import lines change.

defects.defect: The ADMIN 'port' is the retired god facade renamed: a 34-member object injected to call exactly one method, spanning five unrelated sub-domains (users, colour-name queue, audit, flagged, tags) plus search and card expansion. And the panel receives its data by a SECOND mechanism from the SAME source — of AdminPane.vue's 6 props, 5 are pure `pm.*` reads and 7 of 7 emits bind straight to `pm.*` handlers, while the child already injects that port ten lines away.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:195-231 (34 members); demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:234 (inject) with a single use at :361 (`pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)`). Passthrough traced from AdminPane.vue:26-39: :users=pm.filteredAdminUsers.value, :loading=pm.loadingUsers.value, :load-error=pm.usersLoadError.value, :expanded-id=pm.expandedId.value, :total-users=pm.adminUsers.value.length, :css-color=inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY); all 7 emits -> pm.onDeleteUserPalettes/onDeleteUser/toggleExpand/onFeaturePalette/onAdminDeleteUserPalette/onPrune/loadAdminUsers. The module's own header (usePalettePorts.ts:20-30) states the intent it failed: dissolving 'the old usePaletteManager god facade (153 L, ONE cross-everything injected blob) into FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports'.
defects.mechanism: The facade was renamed, not dissolved (edict 1). No consumer of this port can be reasoned about without reading all 34 members. Simultaneously the parent/child pair runs two data paths from one source — 13 declarations of ceremony that add zero information, each a place a rename can silently drift.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by member count and call-site trace.
defects.proposedCure: With L-1 applied the inject at :234 deletes outright and the panel becomes purely prop/emit driven — mountable in a test with props alone, no provider. Structurally: split adminPort along its five existing sub-composable seams, which already own their slices; the port's only work today is re-aggregating them into one blob.

defects.defect: demo/ui/ is 19 pure alias barrels of glass-ui with zero added surface, and the subject uses BOTH the alias and the real subpath in one import block: Button/Badge via ../../../ui/* at :188-189, Dialog* via @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog at :190-197 — while demo/ui/dialog exists and exports the identical eight symbols. Two names for one design system, in one file. The shims also import glass-ui's ROOT barrel, so every shimmed import forfeits the per-component subpath splitting glass-ui publishes 74 export entries to provide.
defects.evidence: $ find demo/ui -type f | wc -l -> 19; $ find demo/ui -type f ! -name index.ts | wc -l -> 0 (every file is a one-line re-export). $ grep -rEl 'from "(\.\./)+ui/' demo --include='*.vue' --include='*.ts' | wc -l -> 48 importers. Subject: AdminUsersPanel.vue:188,189 vs :190-197. demo/ui/dialog/index.ts exports the same 8 Dialog symbols. Provenance in the tree: demo/ui/alert/index.ts's own comment records that the barrel once held a local shadcn re-implementation and was converted to a re-export with the husk kept so consumers' import lines would not change — a back-compat shim by definition.
defects.mechanism: An alias layer the no-legacy edict forbids (edict 2), plus a dual path to the design system (edict 4). SELF-CORRECTION recorded in the report: I first counted 20 barrels from a directory listing; `find` says 19 and the prior r2 pass is correct.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by find/grep counts above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely (19 files); every consumer names the glass-ui subpath directly (@mkbabb/glass-ui/button, /badge, /dialog, …). This REMOVES a directory rather than adding one, so it satisfies edict 3 rather than straining it — 48 files, mechanical. It also makes L-4-class drift visible, because the import line then names the real package.

defects.defect: The confirmation concept lost its home at the Glass 7 upgrade and two demo consumers independently re-grew it. The subject carries a 35-line hand-rolled confirm state machine (7 refs + showConfirm + onConfirm, ~9% of the file) plus 24 lines of Dialog markup; demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:101-122 is a second copy driven by a DIFFERENT mechanism (a boolean republished on the library port). Meanwhile the two sibling destructive admin panels confirm NOTHING.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:157-181 (markup) + :254-286 (machine); demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:101-122 (second copy, same apologetic comment 'Glass 7: ConfirmDialog folded onto the Dialog family'). glass-ui 7.0.0 package.json#exports has ./dialog and NO confirm entry. Unconfirmed destructive siblings: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:99, AdminTagsPanel.vue:101. Family evidence (carried from r2's `git show f2c8f565`): the same commit also produced ActionBarLayer.vue's local successor for the removed glass-ui useLayerTransition.
defects.mechanism: When glass-ui removes a primitive this demo grows a private copy instead of relaying the need upstream — against the design-system edict and against the standing glass-ui BH/BI relay law. Two implementations of 'confirm a destructive palette action', neither reusable by the other.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by reading both call sites and the glass-ui exports map.
defects.proposedCure: One useConfirm() returning {confirm(opts): Promise<boolean>} plus one <ConfirmDialog> composed from the Glass 7 Dialog family. Because there are 3+ call sites in this repo alone, the composition belongs BACK IN glass-ui (/dialog already ships dialogStageContext, the natural home) — this is a BH-relay item, not a new demo wrapper (edict 3). Net: -35 lines here, -20 in PalettesPane, +2 confirmations where there are none today.

defects.defect: The admin row grammar has three homes and the declared atom serves one of three. AdminListItem.vue is the cluster's row primitive exposing exactly the three slots this row needs (swatch/content/actions); AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-132 transcribes it by hand; AdminListSkeleton.vue transcribes it again. `grep -rln AdminListItem demo` returns two files and one of them matches only in a COMMENT — the tell that the atom is being transcribed, not used. A change to the row rhythm must land in three files, two of which are not the atom.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:12-23 (the atom; classes `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge min-w-0`); AdminUsersPanel.vue:80 (`flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 transition-colors`, border on the wrapper at :68); AdminListSkeleton.vue:12 + its comment at :4 ('shaped as the AdminListItem row grammar'). Real consumers: grep -rn AdminListItem demo -> AdminNamesPanel.vue:44,71,94,116,128 only.
defects.mechanism: Unique semantic ownership violated for 'an admin list row'. Same species one level up: EmptyState.vue (12 consumers) and AdminListSkeleton.vue are design-system atoms with no home in the design system — glass-ui 7.0.0's 74 subpaths contain no empty-state and no skeleton entry.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural. Its RENDERED consequence is filed separately and is reproducible: see L-17.
defects.proposedCure: AdminUsersPanel's row becomes <AdminListItem> with the disclosure semantics (role, tabindex, aria-expanded, keydown) hoisted INTO the atom behind an `interactive` prop — the atom is the right home for 'an admin list row', disclosure included. AdminListSkeleton becomes <AdminListItem> with <Skeleton> in its slots: one home, three consumers, and the skeleton cannot diverge from the row again. EmptyState and a list-row Skeleton variant are BH-relay candidates for glass-ui, reusing existing component-type names.

defects.defect: The transient action-result beat has THREE homes and the newest is the only one that leaks. glass-ui ships ./toast and the demo uses it zero times; ActionFeedback.vue owns the concept correctly INCLUDING a clearTimeout on re-trigger, but is buried four levels deep in one card's private folder; AdminUsersPanel.vue:301-309 rebuilds it inline with a bare setTimeout(…, 3000) — no handle, no clearTimeout, no onUnmounted.
defects.evidence: glass-ui package.json#exports has './toast'; grep -rn 'glass-ui/toast|useToast|Toaster' demo -> 0 hits. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue (props {message,variant,visible,autoDismissMs=2500}; watch clears its timer before re-arming). demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:16-20 (Transition) + :301-309 (the uncancelled timer); grep -n setTimeout on the subject -> exactly one hit, line 308.
defects.mechanism: Three implementations of one concept. ActionFeedback's wrong home — a generic feedback atom inside browser/card/PaletteCard/ — is WHY the admin panel could not find it; nothing about the concept is card-specific.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS (mechanically certain from the code; not executed — an admin token is required and the action is destructive): two prunes inside 3 s and the first timer nulls pruneResult while the second message is young. Separately, a prune followed by a sub-view switch (AdminPane.vue:26 v-if) leaves a live timer writing to an unmounted component's ref.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt glass-ui's Toast (edict 4: the design system owns this) and retire both demo copies; if Toast's API cannot express the in-flow 'unfurl beside the toolbar' placement, that is a glass-ui-side variant request (BH relay), not a demo re-implementation. Interim minimum: move ActionFeedback.vue beside EmptyState.vue in demo/shared/ui/ (existing directory, no new dir) and use it here — pruneResult becomes message + v-model:visible and the raw setTimeout deletes.

defects.defect: The `.slug-pill` recipe institutionalises per-instance overrides — its own comment says so — and the copy-paste it was created to kill is still alive inside a component this panel renders. Five consumers use four different mechanisms to apply tone: injected Vue value (subject :99,:168), static CSS var inline (ProfileSection.vue:96, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:67), Tailwind utilities (PaletteSlugBar.vue:65), bare class (ProfileSection.vue:73, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:48).
defects.evidence: demo/styles/foundation.css:583-587 — comment: 'Consumers set `color` / `border-color` per-instance via :style'; rule: `.slug-pill { @apply text-mono-small font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full border; }`. Surviving literal copy-paste: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue:9 — `class="text-mono-small font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full border truncate max-w-tooltip"` reproduces all six @apply utilities in order, and PaletteCard is rendered BY the subject at :140. Subject overrides at :99 and :168.
defects.mechanism: The concept 'identity pill' has no component home, so it exists as a CSS class plus four hand-written tone applications plus one literal duplicate. Edict 5 (root-level styling, never per-instance overrides) is violated by construction: the class REQUIRES every consumer to override it inline.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by grep across the four consumer files and the foundation.css rule.
defects.proposedCure: glass-ui already ships ./chip (dist/components/chip/{Chip.vue.d.ts,chipVariants.d.ts,types.d.ts}). The slug pill IS a Chip. Promote it — <Chip tone="accent"|"muted"|"gold"|"destructive">, tones resolving at the root component level — and the .slug-pill class, all four mechanisms, the PaletteCardSwatches copy, and this component's SAFE_ACCENT_KEY inject retire together. BH-relay item: Chip needs a tone axis.

defects.defect: The wire contract has two declarations and the divergence is paid in masking guards. demo/palettes/types.ts:88 declares `User` with `paletteCount?: number` (OPTIONAL); api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:24 declares `UserListEntry` with `paletteCount: number` (REQUIRED). demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:26 types the response against the demo's hand-mirrored copy, never the server's. The optionality lie is paid for at five sites in the subject and two in the composable.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/types.ts:88-94 vs api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:24-30. Guard sites in the subject: :81, :87-89, :103 (`?? 0`), :113, :241 (`?? 0`); in the composable: useAdminUsers.ts:120, :136. (createdAt: Date -> string is JSON-honest and correct; USER_STATUSES matches exactly today at api/src/modules/session/model.ts:96 — and nothing keeps it matched tomorrow.)
defects.mechanism: Two homes for one concept (the admin-user wire shape), with no shared source and no generation step. Each `??` is a masking fallback for a field the server always sends — forbidden by edict 2.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by side-by-side type declarations and guard-site enumeration.
defects.proposedCure: One declaration. Either the api package publishes its DTO types and the demo imports them, or demo/palettes/model/wire.ts is generated from the api contracts at build time. Minimum immediate fix: `paletteCount: number` (required) in the demo type, deleting all seven guards.

defects.defect: The loading skeleton draws a 32 px leading swatch the real row does not have, so every roster load ends in a horizontal reflow — defeating the 'ONE loading grammar' invariant the subject annotates itself with. AdminListSkeleton is shaped to AdminListItem (whose first slot is a w-8 h-8 anchor); the subject renders that skeleton but its own hand-rolled row opens straight into flex-1 min-w-0 with no leading element.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListSkeleton.vue:15 — `<Skeleton surface="glass" variant="breath" class="w-8 h-8 rounded-full shrink-0" />`, plus its comment at :4 ('shaped as the AdminListItem row grammar'). demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:14-16 (the w-8 h-8 swatch slot it mirrors). Subject: renders the skeleton at :47 and :136; its row at :78-132 has no leading element (`:91 <div class="flex-1 min-w-0 …">` is the first child). Invariant claimed at :44-45. Border placement also diverges: AdminListItem carries `rounded-md border border-card-edge min-w-0` on the row; the subject puts it on an outer wrapper (:68) and leaves the row bare, so AdminListItem's documented S.W5-12/F-1 min-w-0 fix was never inherited.
defects.mechanism: The rendered consequence of L-7's three-transcription structure: the skeleton tells the truth about AdminListItem and a lie about this panel, because they are different rows.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS at runtime (needs an admin token and a populated roster to observe the transition; this seat is read-only and the roster is empty). The SHAPE mismatch itself is CONFIRMED by file:line — a w-8 h-8 leading circle exists in the skeleton and no corresponding element exists in the row it becomes.
defects.proposedCure: L-7's cure resolves it by construction: once the row IS AdminListItem and the skeleton is AdminListItem with <Skeleton> in its slots, they cannot differ in shape. This finding supplies the measurable reason L-7 is not cosmetic.

defects.defect: One injected ink referent is bound across two different surface rungs in a single file. AdminUsersPanel.vue:232 injects SAFE_ACCENT_KEY — certified against the RESTING rung only — and binds it at :99 (inside <Card tier="resting">, correct) and at :168 (inside <DialogContent surface="glass">, a FLOATING surface). The module's own doc-comment states the contract it breaks: 'the referent is the SURFACE RUNG, never the bare page ambient'.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:299-311 (certifies via surfaceLightnessNow("resting", …)) and its doc-comment at :283-290; the surface-parameterised alternative at :345 (useSafeAccentFn(surface)). Subject bindings: :99 (resting host, AdminPane.vue:2) and :168 (floating host). MEASURED LIVE (read-only evaluate on http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users): --glass-bg-resting alpha 0.65 vs --glass-bg-floating alpha 0.80 over the same ambient — the floating rung composites 15 pp more plate tint. Demo-wide split: 5 SAFE_ACCENT_KEY injection sites vs 6 useSafeAccentFn sites.
defects.mechanism: SAFE_ACCENT_KEY is a convenience singleton co-existing with the surface-parameterised useSafeAccentFn(rung). Any consumer spanning two rungs is GUARANTEED to mis-reference one of them, and nothing can detect it.
defects.reproduction: Structural claim CONFIRMED by file:line plus the measured rung-alpha delta. Contrast consequence is a HYPOTHESIS — reproducing the dialog needs an admin token and a non-empty roster, unavailable in this checkout; direction of error is unfavourable (certified against a darker plate, rendered on a lighter one) but magnitude is unmeasured.
defects.proposedCure: Retire SAFE_ACCENT_KEY as a CONSUMABLE; keep it only as the boot writer's --accent-live source. Every consumer names its rung: useSafeAccentFn("resting") for the row, useSafeAccentFn("floating") for the dialog — so the rung cannot be implicit and the ink-on-tier law becomes structurally unbreakable rather than conventionally observed. Composes with L-9: once the pill is a glass-ui Chip with a tone axis, both the inject and the rung question leave this file.

defects.defect: Per-instance geometry overrides on a design-system primitive: :24, :35, :116, :125 each hand-set `h-7 px-2.5` / `h-7 px-2` plus font-display/text-caption/cursor-pointer on a <Button size="sm">, hand-rebuilding the `xs` rung glass-ui ships.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:24,35,116,125; glass-ui ButtonSize = "xs"|"sm"|"md"|"lg" (dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:5). Fleet figure carried from r2 (22 <Button> sites in 11 files hand-set height in class); not re-measured this pass.
defects.mechanism: Edict 5: style at the design-system root, never per instance. If `xs` is the wrong height for a dock-adjacent toolbar, the token moves in glass-ui — not in eleven demo files.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural.
defects.proposedCure: Use size="xs" and delete the four geometry class fragments. If the rung is genuinely wrong, relay the token change to glass-ui rather than overriding at eleven call sites.

defects.defect: One global `expandedId: Ref<string|null>` (usePaletteActions.ts) is republished on three ports and serves three lists across two disjoint ID namespaces — PalettesPane compares it to `palette.id` (client-minted UUID) while BrowsePane and this panel compare it to `palette.slug` (server slug), which types.ts documents as deliberately disjoint.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:150,178,214 (three republications); demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:87 (=== palette.id) vs demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:97 and demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:144 (=== palette.slug); demo/palettes/types.ts:14-31 documents the namespaces as disjoint ('a remote palette has NO id… identified by slug alone'). Carried from r2; the type-declaration half re-read this pass.
defects.mechanism: Expansion is a property of a list SURFACE, not of the application; one string|null holds either namespace depending on which pane wrote last.
defects.reproduction: HYPOTHESIS (requires an admin session; not executed): expanding a card in #/admin/users leaves the same palette expanded in #/browse, and collapsing it in one collapses it in the other. The UUID/slug collision half is a type-honesty defect rather than a crash risk.
defects.proposedCure: Each list owns its own expansion state, or one keyed map Record<listId, string|null>; the port stops publishing a shared cursor to three unrelated views.

defects.defect: An ambiguous specifier in this component's area, off its closure: demo/palettes/export.ts (a file) coexists with demo/palettes/export/ (a directory of 12 modules) and the single importer writes `from "./export"`, resolving to the FILE. The directory's serializers are reached only by a test — so the byte-exact serializer suite certifies code the application never runs.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/export.ts (132 L: exportAsJSON, exportAsCSSCustomProperties, exportAsTailwindConfig, exportAsSVG, exportAsPNG, downloadExport) vs demo/palettes/export/ (bytes, canonical, css, digest, json, png, reload, rfc8785, serializers, svg, tailwind, types). demo/palettes/usePaletteExport.ts:9 -> `from "./export"`. $ grep -rn 'export/serializers' demo -> demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23 ONLY.
defects.mechanism: Two implementations of one concept plus a name collision between a file and a directory. The test-only reach makes the surviving suite a false proof on this axis's own terms.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural, confirmed by ls + grep. NOT attributable to this component: neither module appears in AdminUsersPanel's closure (the panel renders PaletteCard without wiring @export).
defects.proposedCure: Owned by whichever seat audits usePaletteExport / PaletteCardMenu. Resolve to one home — either promote export/ (add its index.ts, delete export.ts, repoint usePaletteExport) or delete export/ and repoint the byte-exact test at the live path. The current state guarantees the certified code and the shipped code can diverge without any gate noticing.

defects.defect: AdminUsersPanel.vue:186 is the only file in demo/ that imports `Transition` from `vue`; the local binding shadows a compiler built-in that 16 of the 17 <Transition> users rely on implicitly.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:186 — `import { inject, ref, computed, Transition } from "vue"`. $ grep -rl '<Transition' demo --include='*.vue' | wc -l -> 17; the only other vue-side imports in that family are TransitionGroup (3 files). Invisible to lint: vue/no-unused-components and @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars are both disabled (eslint.config.js:18-22).
defects.mechanism: Gratuitous divergence from 16 siblings; identical runtime behaviour, so nothing surfaces it.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the `Transition` symbol from the import.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration. Seat declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the confirmation of an irreversible bulk deletion understates its scope: the dialog said "Prune 1 empty users? … permanently delete 1 user … This cannot be undone", the captured request was `POST /admin/users/prune-empty` with `postData: null` (the client API `pruneEmptyUsers(token)` has NO scope argument), and the result was "Pruned 3 users". 1 promised, 3 executed, reproduced independently in one run (probe-D3f.json).
