defects.defect: The design system already ships five of the primitives this file hand-rolls, and demo/ consumes none of them.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json v7.0.0 exports ./collapsible, ./expandable-container, ./data-table, ./toast, ./separator, ./progress, ./pulse, ./status-dot, ./sortable-list, ./metric. Measured demo consumers: collapsible 0, data-table 0, toast 0, expandable-container 0, separator 0, progress 0, pulse 0, sortable-list 0, status-dot 0, metric 0. This file hand-rolls the disclosure (D-7), the review table (D-10), the result beat (D-16), the row separator (D-5) and the pending indicator (D-13).
defects.mechanism: Design-system boundary crossed downward: consumer re-implements producer primitives.
defects.reproduction: for m in collapsible data-table toast expandable-container separator progress pulse sortable-list status-dot metric; do grep -rl "@mkbabb/glass-ui/$m" demo/ | wc -l; done
defects.proposedCure: Owner edict 4 — adopt the producer primitives for these five roles; where a variant is missing, it is added in glass-ui, not in demo/ui/. Five of the MAJORs above collapse into that one adoption.

defects.defect: Encapsulation inverted (5-member defineExpose driving list state the port should own), an uncleared 3s timer, and a redundant `Transition` import.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 `defineExpose({ removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes })`; the port drives it at useAdminUsers.ts:95,117,132,146. Lines 255-261 hold six confirm refs plus a callback-in-a-ref. Line 308 `setTimeout(…, 3000)` is never cleared. Line 186 imports `Transition` from vue: `grep -rl "<Transition" demo | wc -l` → 19; `grep -rlE 'Transition[ ,}].*from "vue"' demo | wc -l` → 1.
defects.mechanism: Leaf owns list state and an imperative modal driver that belong to the port; two hygiene residues.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static; the timer defect reproduces by triggering two prunes within 3s (the first message truncates) or unmounting within 3s (write to a dead ref).
defects.proposedCure: Move `userPalettes` and the operation-result state to the port that already owns every other list on this route, so the panel renders props (owner edict 1); replace the six confirm refs with one typed confirm descriptor; clear the timer on unmount; drop the `Transition` import.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/` (6-file component folder + 3 composables), driven live against a seeded browse wall
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model ID `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared at spawn, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: C-3 — a single malformed colour string on the PUBLIC browse wall destroys the whole Browse pane for every visitor. Seeded `GET /palettes` with one palette whose `colors[0].css = "oklch()"` plus one innocent neighbour; expanding the card took the article count 2 → 0 and replaced the pane with "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')". `pageErrors` and `consoleErrors` were BOTH empty (an error boundary absorbs the throw), which is why no console-scraping gate could ever catch it. Reachable by any authenticated user: `api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28` is `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` with no colour validation. Path: `PaletteCard.vue:230 safeFirstColor` → `safeCss` → `certifyAccentInk` → `parseCssColor`, which throws instead of returning `{ok:false}` on the empty-args colour-function class (the live π-gate R1). Runner-up, tied: C-1+C-2 — the expanded card's entire per-colour action surface is inert on every device (glass-ui `WatercolorDot` declares `inheritAttrs:false` and forwards only class/style, so `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click` and reka's `PopoverTrigger as-child` are all silently dropped onto an `aria-hidden` span with `pointer-events:none`; and `.floating-panel` is declared nowhere, so the hover popover renders `position:static`, transparent, at `top:900 left:-720` in a 1440×900 frame).
result.negativeProof: n/a — verdict is DEFECTIVE. (Two negatives worth recording: `verbatimModuleSyntax` (edict 8) is satisfied in all six files — every type-only import is `import type` or an inline `type` specifier, checked file by file; and there are no ungated rAF loops, no `defineModel`, no `ValueUnit` construction, no HSV roundtrip and no WebGL in the six files or three composables, so five of the brief's six named local hazards are genuinely absent. The sixth — the `parseCssColor` crash class — is live, and is C-3.)

defects.defect: The swatch is not an interactive element: glass-ui 7.0.0 `WatercolorDot` declares `inheritAttrs:false` and re-applies only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style`, so `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click.stop` — plus everything reka's `PopoverTrigger as-child` grafts on — are silently discarded onto a hardcoded `<span aria-hidden="true" style="pointer-events:none">`. The touch popover therefore never opens, `onSwatchClick`/`onPopoverUpdateTouch` are unreachable code, and the swatches are invisible to assistive tech.
defects.evidence: Producer source `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js`: `inheritAttrs:!1`, props `{color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed}` (no `tag`), render `o("span",{"aria-hidden":"true", …, style:u([f.value,{…,pointerEvents:"none",…}])})`. Consumers: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-20 and :29-36. iPhone-13 emulation (`matchMedia("(hover: hover)")` → false), expanded card, tap swatch centre → `{"rekaPopover":0,"floatingPanel":false,"addBtn":false}`. Desktop toggle-close proof: with the panel open, clicking the swatch left it open (`desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen: true`) — `useHoverPopover.ts:51-54 onSwatchClick` never ran.
defects.mechanism: Silent prop/listener drop across a component boundary — `inheritAttrs:false` with a partial attrs re-application, consumed as if it were a polymorphic `as`/`tag` component. No type or template gate is aimed at unknown props on a producer component.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs — read `touch.popoverOpen`, `touch.triggerDom`, `desktop.panelAfterClickWhileOpen`. Requires an isolated vite with VITE_API_URL set (the :9000 server latches `misconfigured` and never fetches).
defects.proposedCure: Semantics belong to the consumer, not the decoration: `SwatchHoverMenu` renders its own `<button type="button" :aria-label>` and mounts `<WatercolorDot>` inside it as pure decoration — its `aria-hidden` and `pointer-events:none` then become correct by construction. One element, one file, no new producer prop. A polymorphic `tag` belongs in glass-ui (edict 4) only if genuinely wanted; KISS says do not buy back with a producer prop what a wrapping `<button>` gives free.

defects.defect: `.floating-panel` is declared nowhere in the demo or the producer, so the teleported hover popover renders `position: static` — making its carefully computed inline `top`/`left` inert — as an unstyled, transparent, full-viewport-width block at the very end of `<body>`, off-screen.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "floating-panel" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/` → 2 prose hits, 1 consumer (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:42), 0 rule declarations. Live computed style at 1440×900: `{position:"static", zIndex:"auto", background:"rgba(0,0,0,0)", boxShadow:"none", borderRadius:"0px", parent:"BODY", rect:{top:900,left:-720,w:1440,h:40}, inline:"top: 494.656px; left: 258px; transform: translateX(-50%);"}`. Screenshot <scratchpad>/pcard-hover-panel.png shows the expanded card with the cursor on swatch #1 and no popover on screen. Pass-1 archaeology: the rule was `demo/@/styles/floating-panel.css` (`position:fixed; z-index:var(--z-overlay)`), deleted 2026-03-25 in c84504d3 claiming glass-ui provides it — it does not.
defects.mechanism: A demo-local CSS fork was deleted on the assumption the producer absorbed it; the class name survived in the consumer as a phantom. `position:static` silently voids the whole hand-rolled positioning path.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs — read `desktop.panelComputed`; and `grep -rn "floating-panel" demo/ src/ node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/`.
defects.proposedCure: Do NOT re-add a demo-local floating-panel.css (that re-forks what glass-ui was meant to absorb). Retire the hand-rolled Teleport branch and render the reka `Popover` on BOTH pointer classes, driving `:open` from `useHoverPopover` on fine pointers. Deletes `positionPanel`, `floatingStyle`, the `aria-hidden` panel and the `e.currentTarget` defect — one removal, five findings.

defects.defect: One malformed colour string on the public browse wall destroys the entire Browse pane for every visitor. `safeFirstColor` → `certifyAccentInk` → `parseCssColor` throws (rather than returning `{ok:false}`) on the empty-argument colour-function class, and the pane's error boundary swallows the whole wall including innocent neighbouring palettes.
defects.evidence: Four one-palette walls each seeded alongside an innocent "Neighbour", expand the first card: `oklch()` → articles 2 → 0, paneText "This panel hit an unexpected error. Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace') Try again", pageErrors [] consoleErrors []. `""` → 2 → 2 (no crash). `not-a-color` → 2 → 2. `#e11d48` control → 2 → 2. Call site PaletteCard.vue:230 `safeFirstColor = computed(() => safeCss(firstColor.value))`, consumed only by the expanded region (PaletteCard.vue:144 → PaletteCardSwatches.vue:10). Reachability: api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:28 `css: z.string().min(1).max(200)` — no colour validation.
defects.mechanism: A total function is advertised where a partial one ships: `certifyAccentInk` has the correct degenerate (`if (!accent) return css`) but the throw bypasses it. Combined with an error boundary that absorbs the throw, the failure is invisible to every console-scraping gate.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe9.mjs — read the `oklch-empty` row (`articlesBefore` 2, `articlesAfter` 0, `paneText`).
defects.proposedCure: Three layers, all at the root. Library: `parseCssColor` returns `{ok:false}` for the empty-args class (π-gate R1, still live). API: the schema validates a colour, not a 200-char string. Demo: nothing about PaletteCard's structure changes. Additionally (C-3b) `PaletteCard.vue:226` uses `??`, so an empty-string css is not nullish and bypasses the documented `EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH` fallback entirely — use `||` with `.trim()`, and have PaletteColorStrip fall back per-segment to the same named token.

defects.defect: The card's primary action (expand/collapse — the only route to the swatches, the slug and every per-colour affordance) is mouse-only: a `<div role="article">` with `@click`, `cursor-pointer`, no `tabindex`, no `@keydown`, no `aria-expanded`. WCAG 2.1.1 Level A.
defects.evidence: `cardStructure: [{tag:"div", role:"article", tabindex:null, ariaExpanded:null, cursor:"pointer", label:"Palette: Ember Rose"}, …]` (PaletteCard.vue:5-27). 22 real Tab presses across the populated wall: `tabReachedArticle: false` — the sequence reaches the card's descendants ("5 votes, click to vote", "Palette menu") but never the card. `el.focus()` → `{cardFocusable:false, activeTag:"body"}`. Compounding: glass-ui `useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js` returns `onKeydown`/`onKeyup` (with an explicit `e.key==="Enter"||e.key===" "` leg) and `onBlur`; PaletteCard.vue:24 binds all eight handlers to that unfocusable div — three are structurally dead.
defects.mechanism: A disclosure control was implemented as a clickable container. The `role="article"` justification in the header comment (PaletteCard.vue:2-4) is correct for a container that is not itself a control, but this one owns @click, cursor-pointer and a press animation.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe2.mjs — read `tabSequence` / `tabReachedArticle`; node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe3.mjs — read `cardStructure`, `keyboardEnter`.
defects.proposedCure: Put a real `<button aria-expanded>` on the card's own header row (title + colour count), keep `role="article"` on the container, and delete the container `@click`. Fixes 2.1.1, gives `useLiquidPress` a legitimate focusable host, announces the state (C-15), removes the MixSourceSelector wrapper-button hack (C-14), and cures the title dead zone (C-9) for free.

defects.defect: "Rename" from the card menu opens a text input that is immediately focus-stolen by reka's DropdownMenu focus-restore, so the caret never lands in the field and the user's first Enter/Space re-opens the menu. The in-code guard written to prevent exactly this is dead code and its comment is false.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:317 `if (action !== "rename") menuOpen.value = false;` — but `startRenaming()` at :281 opens with `menuOpen.value = false`, so the guard can never change an observable; the comment at :291-292 ("keep the menu open visually until the input takes focus") is contradicted by the code. Measured on /#/palettes, menu → Rename: `menuRename_focusAt150 = {tag:"input", ph:"Palette name..."}` then `menuRename_focusAt800 = {tag:"button", label:"Palette menu"}`, with `menuRename_inputPresent: true` and `menuRename_menuItemsStillInDom: 0`. Control: the title-click entry path keeps focus on the input at both 150 ms and 800 ms.
defects.mechanism: Ordering race between `onMounted → inputRef.focus()` (PaletteRenameInput.vue:53-56) and the dropdown primitive's close-time focus restoration; the guard meant to sequence them is inert.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe8.mjs — compare `menuRename_focusAt150` with `menuRename_focusAt800`.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the dead guard and the false comment; drive the rename open from the menu's own close completion — `@closeAutoFocus.prevent` on `DropdownMenuContent`, focusing the input in that handler. That is the idiomatic reka seam. Not a setTimeout.

defects.defect: `ActionFeedback` is silent to assistive tech, truncates a second message that arrives inside the dismiss window, and never clears its timer on unmount.
defects.evidence: Live: `chipAfterFirstSave = {text:"Saved!", role:null, ariaLive:null}` — no live region on the sole surface reporting four async outcomes (BrowsePane.vue:230,239,249,264). Timing: Save at t=0, Save again at t=2250 ms while the chip was still up → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 613` (promised 2500). Control run with the second Save at t=2523 ms (outside the window) → `secondChipLifetimeMs: 2752`. Cause: ActionFeedback.vue:39-47 watches `props.visible`; PaletteCard.vue:240 writes `feedbackVisible.value = true`, a no-op write when already true, so the watcher never fires and the in-flight timer is neither cleared nor re-armed. Third defect: `let timer` (:37) has no unmount cleanup.
defects.mechanism: State change keyed on a boolean visibility edge rather than on message identity; plus a missing scope disposal.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe7.mjs — read `secondSaveAtMs` and `secondChipLifetimeMs`; flip the intermediate wait to 1750 ms for the outside-window control.
defects.proposedCure: Watch the message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and key the transition on it so a new message is a new node; add `role="status" aria-live="polite"`; register `onScopeDispose(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better: hoist dismissal to the caller and let the chip be pure presentation — that also deletes the `update:visible` round-trip and half of C-8.

defects.defect: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is ignored by the card's expand/collapse itself, not merely by its follow-up scroll: `useHeightTransition` writes hardcoded 350 ms / 250 ms inline `transition` strings with no PRM read, then calls `scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"})` unconditionally.
defects.evidence: Booted with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`: `{prm: true, log:[{style:"height: 111px; opacity: 1; transition: height 350ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 350ms;"}, …]}`. Source: useHeightTransition.ts:7-10 (constants), :30 and :61 (writes), :48 (`scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth", block:"nearest"})`). The global guard demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 cannot help: CSSOM-View consults `scroll-behavior` only when the author passes `behavior:"auto"`, and no stylesheet can override an inline `transition`. Contrast the surrounding discipline: PaletteCard.vue:29 "PRM-zeroed", :62 "PRM-gated", :264 "PRM-instant by construction"; glass-ui's useRAFLoop is called with `respectReducedMotion: !0`.
defects.mechanism: Imperative JS animation bypasses the CSS-layer PRM guard the rest of the component relies on.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs — read `prm` (context is created with `reducedMotion: "reduce"`).
defects.proposedCure: Move the height morph into the `vj-*` transition family this same file already uses for `rename-morph` and `feedback-chip` — custom properties plus a PRM media query. If it must stay JS, read glass-ui's `useReducedMotion` and zero both durations and the scroll behaviour.

defects.defect: `defineExpose({showFeedback})` forces both parent panes to keep instance maps that are never pruned, permanently retaining every unmounted card of the session (and through it the subtree, its press spring, its popover closure and its Palette object).
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })`. BrowsePane.vue:94 and PalettesPane.vue:84 both register `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` into `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})` (BrowsePane.vue:209, PalettesPane.vue:177). Vue calls a function ref with `null` on unmount; the `el &&` guard makes that call a no-op, so no entry is ever deleted. Growth drivers: BrowsePane.vue:140 `loadMoreRemotePalettes()`, every filter change, every sort re-key. The `(el: any)` cast is what hides the `null` from the type checker.
defects.mechanism: An imperative child handle forces every host to build an identity map to reach one method; the unmount signal is then swallowed by the truthiness guard that map registration needs.
defects.reproduction: NONE — retention argument from source (absence of collection cannot be photographed). The three lines are unconditional.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a delete-key fix: make feedback data. Lift `{slug, message, variant}` into the pane and pass it down as `:feedback="feedback?.slug === palette.slug ? feedback : null"`. `defineExpose`, both `cardRefs` maps, both `any` casts and the retention disappear together.

defects.defect: Clicking the palette title — the single most obvious target on every card of the public wall — silently does nothing, because `@click.stop` is a compile-time modifier that stops propagation unconditionally, before the `editableName &&` guard is evaluated.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:53-59 `@click.stop="editableName && startRenaming()"`; BrowsePane.vue:92-117 does not pass `editableName`. Measured on /#/browse: clicking the title → `afterTitleClick_expandedBodies: 0`; clicking card chrome 20 px away → expanded (the `Copy slug` control appears). The span reports `cursor: pointer` there (inherited from the root), so the affordance lies. Cross-check on /#/palettes where `editableName` IS passed: the same span reports `cursor: text` and does start a rename.
defects.mechanism: Vue compiles `.stop` to an unconditional `stopPropagation()` emitted ahead of the handler expression; a falsy guard inside the expression cannot undo it.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe3.mjs — compare `beforeTitleClick` / `afterTitleClick_expandedBodies` against `swatchButtons` (the post-card-click expansion).
defects.proposedCure: Patch: `@click="editableName ? (($event.stopPropagation()), startRenaming()) : undefined"`. Gestalt cure is C-4's — once the disclosure is a real header button, the title is inert text and rename is a named control rather than an undiscoverable click on a label.

defects.defect: `PaletteRenameInput` ships two nameless 17.5×17.5 px icon buttons and a text field with no accessible name — the 4th hand-rolled copy of an icon-trigger recipe the parent file already retired onto the glass-ui atom.
defects.evidence: PaletteRenameInput.vue:18-30 (no aria-label on either button), :11-17 (input has no aria-label, no id/label). Measured with the row open: `renameButtons: [{type:"submit", name:"", w:17.5, h:17.5}, {type:"button", name:"", w:17.5, h:17.5}]`, `renameInput: {ariaLabel:null, id:null, w:275.5, h:23.9}`. WCAG 4.1.2 ×2 and 2.5.8 AA ×3 (17.5×17.5 is 53% of the required 24×24 area). Asymmetry proving oversight: every icon button in sibling PaletteCardSwatches.vue (lines 15, 43, 50, 57) carries an explicit :aria-label under a W5-a11y comment, and PaletteCard.vue:96-104 already consumes the glass-ui atom with the note "S.W5-4: 3rd copy of the hand-rolled icon-trigger recipe dies onto the glass-ui atom; the sm square also cures the ~24px touch target."
defects.mechanism: A component-level a11y sweep and a design-system consolidation both missed one file; `p-0.5` around a `w-3.5 h-3.5` glyph cannot reach 24 px.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe8.mjs — read `renameButtons` and `renameInput`.
defects.proposedCure: Consume `Button icon-only variant="ghost" size="sm"` (already imported in the parent) for both controls and give the field an `aria-label`. Edict 4/5: the atom is the root-level styling seam.

defects.defect: The `Copy slug` button in the expanded card is 16×16 px — the only sub-24 px control present in the expanded state, and therefore the cheapest possible regression test for the vacuous gate.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardSwatches.vue:13-19 (`p-0.5` + `w-3 h-3` icon). Measured on the expanded browse card: `{label:"Copy slug gallery", w:16, h:16}`. WCAG 2.5.8 AA. Not present in the collapsed state, which is why the repo's a11y battery never sees it.
defects.mechanism: Same as C-10: a hand-rolled icon button instead of the ratified glass-ui atom.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe3.mjs — read `swatchButtons` after the card click; or pcard-probe2.mjs `expandedScan.small`.
defects.proposedCure: Same as C-10 — consume the glass-ui icon-only `Button size="sm"`.

defects.defect: The repo's a11y gate is not missing — it exists, it is aimed at exactly this surface, and it passes green over every defect above, because it never expands a card or opens the rename row. Two further blind spots make C-4 and C-9 structurally invisible to it.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-user.spec.ts --project=smoke-admin --reporter=line` → `Running 2 tests using 1 worker / 2 passed (12.1s)`. The spec (:19-44) asserts `nameless === []` AND `undersized === []` over the populated browse wall. My identical battery-shaped scan of the same `main`: collapsed 0 nameless / 0 sub-24; one card expanded 0 / 1 (Copy slug 16×16); rename row open 2 / 3. Blind spots: the `OPERABLE` selector at e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/a11y-battery.ts:66-67 matches only native tags plus a role allow-list, so the `role="article"` click host and the clickable title `<span>` cannot be seen; and `keyboardFacts()` (:222) — the one helper that could catch C-4 — is never called against the card in any spec. Also `grep -rln "PaletteCard" test/` → no matches (zero unit tests).
defects.mechanism: State-blind gate: the battery measures the component's resting frame only, so every defect behind an interaction is out of scope by construction.
defects.reproduction: npx playwright test e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-user.spec.ts --project=smoke-admin --reporter=line  (green, 12.1s). Named green-keeping mutation: delete every aria-label in PaletteCardSwatches.vue, delete role and aria-label from the card root, and shrink every expanded-state control to 1×1 px — both tests stay green.
defects.proposedCure: Give the gate states, not the resting frame: expand a card, open the rename row, open the menu, and re-run the battery at each; add one `keyboardFacts` assertion against whatever owns the expand click. Seeding needs no API — `localStorage["color-palettes"]` is a plain `useStorage` singleton (demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:6).

defects.defect: The decomposition is a distributed god module, not a set of seams: two of the five children state in their own comments that they exist to satisfy a line-count cap, and the state never moved with them. `PaletteCardSwatches` is a 96-line, 8-prop/8-emit pass-through with zero state and zero logic.
defects.evidence: Primary-source admission: PaletteCardMeta.vue:2-4 "T.W5 (PP-8 cap cure, the H.W3 PaletteCardSwatches lift precedent)" and PaletteCard.vue:76-77 "colocated lift (T.W5 PP-8 cap cure)". Parent retains everything: 11 props, 17 emit variants (:200-218), a 20-entry string-keyed dispatch table rebuilt per menu click (:293-313), 4 refs and 4 composables. Every PaletteCardSwatches prop is a member of the parent's `useHoverPopover()` destructure (:246-255) and every emit routes straight back to a handler from that same destructure (:149-156). The seam contract is untyped: `action: [action: string]` (PaletteCardMenu.vue:225) with `if (!fn) return;` (PaletteCard.vue:316) silently swallowing any unknown verb — a rename on either side fails at runtime with no type error and no test.
defects.mechanism: Splitting by file length rather than by state ownership: markup moved, state did not, so each boundary costs 16 declarations and buys no encapsulation.
defects.reproduction: NONE — structural reading with quoted primary-source comments. (PaletteCardMenu, PaletteRenameInput and ActionFeedback ARE real seams: each owns state or a dependency.)
defects.proposedCure: Move `useHoverPopover()` INTO PaletteCardSwatches — 8 props collapse to 4 (colors, isLocal, displaySlug, swatchClass), 8 emits to 3 (popoverAdd, popoverEdit, popoverCopy); the parent's only claim on that state is `onBeforeCollapse` (:277), one line an `@collapse` emit or a child-side `watch(() => expanded)` covers. Type the menu seam as `action: [action: MenuAction]` with a union, which makes the `!fn` branch unreachable and deletable. Fold PaletteCardMeta back into the title row (it is a fragment: four sibling roots, unstyleable as a unit) or give it the vote mutation.

defects.defect: Downstream consumer damage from C-4: `MixSourceSelector` wraps the whole PaletteCard in a native `<button>` to buy back keyboard reach, nesting `role="article"` and two real buttons inside a button — an HTML content-model violation that, because `role=button` is children-presentational, erases the card's own controls from the accessibility tree in the Mix pane.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 — `<!-- W5-a11y: native <button> for keyboard reach + aria-pressed for selection state --> <button v-for="palette in savedPalettes" type="button" :aria-pressed :aria-label …> <PaletteCard :palette :css-color="''" /> </button>`. PaletteCard contributes `role="article"` plus `<button aria-label="Palette menu">` and `<button aria-label="N votes, click to vote">` as descendants. The comment shows the intent was accessibility.
defects.mechanism: A consumer hand-rolled a keyboard affordance the card should have provided; the workaround is structurally invalid.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the a11y-tree collapse (asserted from the ARIA children-presentational rule); the nesting itself is at MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 and PaletteCard.vue:22,83-104.
defects.proposedCure: Fix C-4 (real `<button aria-expanded>` on the card header) and delete the wrapper button, replacing it with a selection control that is a sibling of the card, not its ancestor.

defects.defect: The disclosure never announces its state: no `aria-expanded` anywhere on the card, so even a sighted mouse user on a screen reader gets no signal that content appeared.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:5-27 has no `aria-expanded`; measured `cardStructure[*].ariaExpanded: null` on every card. Nothing else in the subtree signals the state change (the swatch region is `aria-hidden` per C-1).
defects.mechanism: Same root as C-4: a disclosure implemented as a clickable container carries none of the disclosure ARIA contract.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe3.mjs — read `cardStructure`.
defects.proposedCure: Folded into C-4's cure — the header `<button aria-expanded>` carries the state by construction.

defects.defect: `positionPanel(e.currentTarget as Element)` is read from inside a `nextTick` callback, after event dispatch has completed and `currentTarget` has been reset to null — an intermittent, microtask-timing-dependent unhandled TypeError, and unconditionally pointless because the coordinates are inert against `position: static`.
defects.evidence: useHoverPopover.ts:26-31. Pass 1 captured the live throw: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect') at positionPanel (useHoverPopover.ts:18:25)`. My independent corroboration of its intermittency: across every real `mouse.move` hover the inline style WAS written (`top: 494.656px; left: 258px`) and no error appeared — so under genuine hover the microtask checkpoint fires while dispatch is still in flight. The `as Element` cast is what let a null-typed value through the type system.
defects.mechanism: Deferred read of a per-dispatch DOM property, laundered past the type checker by an assertion cast.
defects.reproduction: Intermittent under real hover; deterministic under programmatic dispatch (pass-1 P10). My runs show the passing branch: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe5.mjs → `desktop.panelComputed.inline`.
defects.proposedCure: Capture `e.currentTarget` into a local inside the synchronous handler body; the cast disappears with it. Moot once C-2 adopts a self-positioning popover.

defects.defect: `aria-hidden="true"` on a container that holds three tabbable, named buttons — a WAI-ARIA MUST-NOT that Chromium enforces at runtime.
defects.evidence: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:40-50 sets `aria-hidden="true"` on the hover panel. Measured contents of that panel: three 28×28 buttons with real names — `Add #e11d48 to current palette`, `Edit color #e11d48`, `Copy color #e11d48`. WAI-ARIA 1.2: "Authors MUST NOT use aria-hidden=\"true\" on … an element that contains focusable elements." The panel's own comment names a fallback ("the reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route") that C-1 proves does not exist.
defects.mechanism: Hiding a keyboard-inaccessible surface from AT instead of making it accessible; the hidden subtree still receives focus.
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/pcard-probe4.mjs — read `panel.ariaHidden` and `panel.btns`.
defects.proposedCure: Cured by C-2: one reka `Popover` for both pointer classes manages aria-hidden, focus and dismissal correctly by construction.

defects.defect: `useLeaveTimer` registers no scope disposal, so a card unmounted inside its 250 ms window leaves a live timeout and retains its closure; adjacently, the height transition supplies no `enterCancelled`/`leaveCancelled` hooks and no `:css="false"`, so Vue's CSS end-detection races the JS `done()` and an unfired transitionend would strand the element at `height: 0; opacity: 0`.
defects.evidence: useLeaveTimer.ts:1-17 — `schedule`/`cancel` returned, no `onScopeDispose`. Driver at useHoverPopover.ts:35. useHeightTransition.ts:35-39 and :66-70 attach self-removing transitionend listeners; PaletteCard.vue:131-138 wires only the six happy-path hooks; no `:css="false"` anywhere.
defects.mechanism: Missing lifecycle teardown; JS-only transition hooks used without the flag that tells Vue to stop racing them.
defects.reproduction: NONE for the stranded-element branch — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. The missing `onScopeDispose` is a source fact at useLeaveTimer.ts:1-17.
defects.proposedCure: `onScopeDispose(cancel)` in useLeaveTimer — one line. The transition-cancel hazard is deleted outright by C-7's move to the CSS `vj-*` family.

defects.defect: Idiom drift inside a single folder: `PaletteCard.vue` alone uses `withDefaults(defineProps<…>())` + `props.x` while four of its five siblings use Vue 3.5 reactive props destructure; and `PaletteCardMenu` mixes `@click` and `@select` for one behaviour.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:182-198 vs PaletteCardMenu.vue:206, PaletteCardMeta.vue:61, PaletteRenameInput.vue:39, PaletteColorStrip.vue:31. `expanded?: boolean | undefined` and six siblings restate `| undefined` that `?` already implies. PaletteCardMenu drives eleven items with `@click` (lines 18, 31, 52, 66, 76, 86, 96, 136, 146, 158, 165) and five with `@select` (:113-127), with `@click.prevent` working around the sub-trigger (:108) — `@select` is the primitive's own semantic event, covering keyboard activation and typeahead.
defects.mechanism: Standing edict 7 (idiomatic Vue 3.5) unevenly applied; the reka event contract half-adopted.
defects.reproduction: NONE — source reading, file by file. (Edict 8 `verbatimModuleSyntax` PASSES across all six files: every type-only import is `import type` or an inline `type` specifier.)
defects.proposedCure: Convert PaletteCard to reactive props destructure like its siblings, drop the redundant `| undefined`, and move PaletteCardMenu's eleven `@click` items onto `@select` so the sub-trigger `@click.prevent` workaround can be deleted.

defects.defect: The mega-tranche visual audit has zero coverage of this component: both palette routes were captured with an empty wall, so the REPORT's headline a11y counters cannot see PaletteCard at all.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Declared seat, not inherited. No DEFECT.
result.strongestDefect: N-6 — the application's composition root is an inline `<script type="module">` in demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 with no module home, so the production gh-pages build emits 12,472 bytes of JS across 2 chunks and NO BrowsePane chunk at all. A probe changing only that one thing (composition root moved into a file) emits 1,595,550 bytes across 45 chunks including BrowsePane-bS6gps-Y.js (22,321 B) + BrowsePane-B-2cz1Cw.css (799 B) — 127.9x of the application is missing from the shipped artifact. The boot is simultaneously invisible to typecheck (tsconfig cannot include .html), to eslint, and to the bundler, all for the same reason. Neither prior pass examined the build.
result.negativeProof: The brief's headline charge — a demo import a real consumer could not write — does NOT hold, and this is now proved by three independent passes. BrowsePane.vue's full import list (:179-199, 14 imports) is `vue`, demo-relative paths, and the published subpath `@mkbabb/glass-ui/search`. `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/value.js"' demo/` -> 0 bare-root imports; `grep -rn '@src/|\.\./\.\./src/' demo/` (non-.md) -> 0; all 49 value.js specifiers in demo/ are keys that exist in package.json#exports. The mechanism is structural, not disciplinary: vite.config.ts:38-49 GENERATES the self-alias set from package.json#exports by anchored regex, so an alias cannot drift from the export map nor prefix-match into a subpath, and tsconfig.demo.json carries no @src/* path — a non-published specifier is unauthorable, not merely absent. Additionally sound: verbatimModuleSyntax is honoured (:197 is the only type-only import and is correctly `import type`); the browser/{card,search,dialog} sub-barrel discipline is followed by this file; animations are tokenized not inlined (vj-morph -> demo/styles/animations.css:70-122, pane-scroll-fade -> demo/styles/foundation.css); and the route renders clean in all four Safari matrices (REPORT.md:121,136,151,166 — overflowX 0, main 1, pageErr 0, consoleErr 0). Per MT-F022 the 7/12 Chromium keyboard reachability was NOT born-RED — roving tabindex is correct.

defects.defect: The application's composition root has no module home: demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 is an inline `<script type="module">` containing createApp/use/mount. Under vite@8.0.16 + rolldown its body is dropped at build time, so the production gh-pages artifact contains zero application code, zero application CSS, and no BrowsePane chunk. NEW in pass 3 — neither prior pass examined the build (grep for gh-pages/sideEffects/main.ts/rolldown across both prior reports = 0 hits each).
defects.evidence: demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (inline entry; `ls demo/color-picker/` shows no main.ts). Committed artifact: `ls -la dist/gh-pages/assets/` -> index-Dezn_h7o.js = 698 bytes, no index-*.css, no pane chunks; `head -c 900` of it is only Vite's modulepreload-polyfill IIFE. PROBE A (repo config verbatim, outDir redirected only): 2 JS chunks, 12,472 B total, same content hash index-Dezn_h7o.js, `ls outA/assets | grep -i browse` -> none. PROBE B (+treeshake:{moduleSideEffects:true}): byte-identical to A, so package sideEffects is NOT the mechanism. PROBE C (only delta: the 8 lines transcribed into a real file passed as build.rolldownOptions.input): 45 JS chunks, 1,595,550 B, BrowsePane-bS6gps-Y.js 22,321 B + BrowsePane-B-2cz1Cw.css 799 B. Ratio 127.9x. Configs preserved at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/vite.probe{A,B,C}.mts + probe-entry.ts.
defects.mechanism: wrong module boundary — a module with no file: the composition root lives inside HTML, placing it outside tsconfig (cannot include .html), outside eslint's file set, and outside the bundler's entry analysis. Three enforcement systems miss the same eight lines for one reason.
defects.reproduction: cd /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js && npx vite build --mode gh-pages --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/vite.probeA.mts  ->  outA/assets/index-*.js is 698 bytes, no BrowsePane chunk. Then the same with vite.probeC.mts -> 45 chunks incl. BrowsePane-bS6gps-Y.js. Also directly observable: `ls -la dist/gh-pages/assets/` on the committed build.
defects.proposedCure: Give the composition root a file: demo/color-picker/main.ts holds the eight lines verbatim, index.html carries `<script type="module" src="./main.ts">` and nothing else. Five lines; restores bundler entry analysis, typecheck coverage and lint coverage of the boot simultaneously. Do NOT pursue a bundler workaround — the entry having no module home is the defect. Add a CI gate: build gh-pages and assert the entry chunk exceeds a floor (>50 KB); a 698-byte entry must fail loudly, not deploy quietly.

defects.defect: `"sideEffects": false` is declared package-wide for a package that contains a non-library tree. It is true of src/ and false of demo/ (every SFC <style> is a side-effecting import), and the publish surface has to carve the demo back out by negation globs.
defects.evidence: package.json:12 `"sideEffects": false`; package.json:60-64 `"files": ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages", "!dist/gh-pages/**"]` — two exclusion rules to keep a build target out of the package. demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:5-7 already names the hazard in prose ("the ./demo/** sideEffects mark defeats the named-re-export tree-shake ... BOOKED"). Probe B proves the claim is currently inert, not benign.
defects.mechanism: wrong package boundary — demo/ is a separate package wearing the library's package.json; the boundary is being patched with exclusion globs rather than drawn.
defects.reproduction: NONE — hypothesis about future tree-shaker behaviour. The untrue declaration itself is proved by inspection (package.json:12 vs any demo SFC <style>); probe B proves it does not currently fire.
defects.proposedCure: Split the package: demo/ becomes a private workspace package. The library keeps sideEffects:false truthfully and both !dist/gh-pages negations delete; the demo declares sideEffects:["*.css","*.vue"] and consumes @mkbabb/value.js as a workspace dependency through its real exports map — which also retires the generated self-alias apparatus (vite.config.ts:22-49) and converts "the demo proves the public API" from policy into a fact of module resolution.

Extends pass-1 L-1 with (a) live-resolver proof, (b) semantic byte divergence beyond the known slugifier split, (c) the dogfood inversion: the DEAD path imports the library, the LIVE path does not.

Sole consumer of the contract set: demo/test/export/byte-exact.test.ts:23. Inversion: export/png.ts:11 imports `oklch, toRgba8` from @mkbabb/value.js/color; export.ts:1 imports only ./types and renders PNG by round-tripping its own SVG through a <canvas> (export.ts:84-117). export/serializers.ts:5-9 names its own rival in prose.

defects.defect: Three parallel routes to the design system across 209 import sites, and BrowsePane uses two of them eleven lines apart. Quantifies pass-1 L-3, which established the shims but not their scale or cost.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:180-181 `from "../ui/card"` / `"../ui/button"` (shims -> glass-ui ROOT barrel) vs BrowsePane.vue:195 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/search"` (published subpath). Census: `grep -rn 'from "(\.\./)*ui/[a-z-]*"' demo | wc -l` -> 90; `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/' demo | wc -l` -> 82; `grep -rn 'from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"' demo | wc -l` -> 37. Of 20 shim barrels, 19 re-export the root barrel (only demo/ui/input uses a subpath). Cost: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js = 25,239 B vs card.js = 217 B, button.js = 71 B; glass-ui publishes 68 subpaths and marks sideEffects:["*.css"]. demo/ui/alert/index.ts:3-9 records the directory was converted from real re-implementations to re-exports — one step short of deletion.
defects.mechanism: alias barrels (edict 2) defeating a producer's deliberate subpath split; no rule distinguishes the three conventions because demo/palettes/** has no import governance at all (L-4/N-2).
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'from "\(\.\./\)*ui/[a-z-]*"' demo | wc -l  ->  90 ; ls -la node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/{glass-ui,card,button}.js  ->  25239 / 217 / 71
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely (20 barrels, 90 sites rewritten onto @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath>). Then, once L-4/N-2's globs are re-homed onto the live tree, ban the glass-ui root barrel from demo/** via no-restricted-imports — which makes edict 4 mechanically checkable for the first time.

defects.defect: The five-port dissolution of the usePaletteManager god facade re-formed the facade inside browsePort: 32 members spanning browse data, the actions slice, the admin slice, session identity and three whole un-narrowed sub-composables. BrowsePane consumes all 32.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:157-192 — 32 members. `grep -o "pm\.[a-zA-Z]*" demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue | sort -u | wc -l` -> 30 direct; the remaining two (ensureUser, ensureSession) are consumed transitively via useDialogBrowseActions -> 32/32. Only three files inject BROWSE_PORT_KEY (BrowsePane.vue:182, browser/search/TagEditPopover.vue:47, browser/dialog/VersionHistoryDrawer.vue:115); the other two take one slice each. usePalettePorts.ts:22-30 claims the facade was dissolved.
defects.mechanism: ownership aggregation — a port whose sole full consumer uses every member is the god object renamed; the Pick<> narrowing idiom the codebase already knows (useDialogBrowseActions.ts:26-35) is applied to the helper and not to the pane.
defects.reproduction: grep -o "pm\.[a-zA-Z]*" demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue | sort -u | wc -l  ->  30 ; sed -n '157,192p' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts  ->  32 members
defects.proposedCure: BrowsePane injects three narrow things — a browse port (data + its own actions), a cardActions port (expand/edit/swatch), and the session identity it needs for isOwned/isAdmin. versions/tagEdit/flagged go directly to the drawer, popover and dialog that use them rather than transiting the pane; PaletteCard injects the admin port itself instead of receiving admin verbs as props.

defects.defect: The card-feedback rail is a hand-rolled imperative registry of child component instances, implemented twice (BrowsePane and PalettesPane, keyed differently), and it never releases — every card ever rendered is retained for the pane's lifetime.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"` + :209 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; PalettesPane.vue:84 + :177 are the verbatim twin keyed on palette.id. Four imperative call sites into the child's exposed internals: BrowsePane.vue:230,239,249,264 driving PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })`. Vue invokes function refs with null on unmount; `el && (...)` short-circuits and no `delete` exists in either file. useBrowsePalettes.ts:74 REPLACES remotePalettes on every sort/tier/tag change and :106 APPENDS on paging.
defects.mechanism: wrong direction of dependency — the pane reaches into child instances across the encapsulation boundary; feedback-after-action is a design-system concern (glass-ui publishes ./toast and ./status-dot).
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from code: three sort changes over a 50-row wall retain 150 unmounted PaletteCard instances in cardRefs, since loadRemotePalettes (useBrowsePalettes.ts:74) replaces the array and the null-ref branch is short-circuited at BrowsePane.vue:94. No browser needed.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both registries. Either PaletteCard takes a `feedback?: { message, variant }` prop and owns its own dismissal (the pane just sets a value on the row it already holds), or route action verdicts through glass-ui's toast surface. Both kill the leak, the `any` in the template, and the duplication in one move.

defects.defect: Colour distance has no home. BrowsePane.vue:339-349 and api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-180 hand-roll the same predicate with the same duplicated 0.15 literal; the typed server seam has zero callers and a code comment stands in for the call; and the client filter is scoped to the loaded page, so it reports an empty commons that is not empty.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:344-347 `palettes.filter((p: any) => ... Math.hypot(c.L-L, c.a-a, c.b-b) <= radius)` with `const radius = 0.15` at :343; crud-list.ts:168-179 same predicate as `Math.sqrt(dL*dL+da*da+db*db) <= radius`, `query.colorRadius ?? 0.15`. Dead plumbing: demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-30,50-53 define colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius and `grep -rn "colorL" demo` returns only those two lines plus the comment at BrowsePane.vue:354. Page scope: pm.filteredBrowse derives from remotePalettes, capped at BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts:18). Three homes for OKLab: SearchFilterBar.vue:206 uses value.js via demo/color-session/color-utils.ts:1; api/src/modules/palette/service/oklab.ts:85-95 hand-rolls the matrix (its own header at :16-21 says it should be replaced by value.js wholesale); src/color/anchors.ts:318-326 runs a private squared-XYZ nearest search. The library's published surface exports NO distance function (src/subpaths/color.ts:14-32).
defects.mechanism: a first-class library concept with no home in the library, so three consumers each grew their own; plus a wrong-boundary placement (client-side filter over one keyset page) producing a user-visible wrong answer.
defects.reproduction: With >50 published palettes, run a colour search whose only matches are past the first keyset page: displayedBrowse (BrowsePane.vue:339-349) filters only the 50 loaded rows and PaletteCardGrid renders `:empty` with "No published palettes here yet." (BrowsePane.vue:83-85). The server filter, which searches the whole collection, is never called — grep -rn "colorL" demo returns no call site.
defects.proposedCure: Publish the metric: deltaEOK (and the deltaE2000 sibling) in src/color/operations.ts, exported from src/subpaths/color.ts. api/ consumes it, retiring oklab.ts's hand-rolled matrix and its hex/rgb-only parser limit. BrowsePane deletes displayedBrowse and colorSearchParams entirely and pushes {colorL, colorA, colorB, colorRadius} into currentFilterOpts() in useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-61, where every other filter already lives — the colour filter then pages, sorts and reloads like tier and tags, for free. Make Palette.oklabColors non-optional on the searchable projection so neither implementation can choose silent exclusion.

defects.defect: useDialogBrowseActions is misnamed and mis-homed: it lives in browser/dialog/composables/, its host is a pane, and three of its five members are browse-filter setters over state owned by useBrowsePalettes three directories away.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:199 imports it from "./browser/dialog"; physical home demo/palettes/browser/dialog/composables/useDialogBrowseActions.ts:83-98 (onTierChange/onTagsChange/onClearFilters, each a two-line setter + reload). The state it mutates is owned by useBrowsePalettes.ts:40-41 (tierFilter, selectedTags) and :63 (loadRemotePalettes), which exports the two refs as raw WRITABLE refs at :226-227. Its dialog-only member onRevert is guarded by an optional modalStack dep (:36,:78) that BrowsePane never passes, so it returns immediately while BrowsePane maintains its own revert at :277-284. BrowsePane.vue:329-332 then wraps onClearFilters to also clear pane-local colour search — two 'clear filters' semantics.
defects.mechanism: unique-semantic-ownership failure — the module that owns the filters does not own the invariant 'changing a filter reloads the wall'; any consumer writing pm.tierFilter.value directly desyncs the wall silently.
defects.reproduction: NONE for a runtime failure — the desync is currently unexercised because only the composable writes the refs. The mis-homing and the dead onRevert branch are proved by inspection (useDialogBrowseActions.ts:78 `if (!modalStack) return;` with no modalStack passed at BrowsePane.vue:261-265).
defects.proposedCure: Move onTierChange/onTagsChange/onClearFilters into useBrowsePalettes and stop exporting tierFilter/selectedTags as writable. Fold the colour-search params into the same currentFilterOpts() so one clearFilters clears everything by construction. What remains is onFork — one host-agnostic function, correctly named useForkPalette, homed beside the versions composable that does the work.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, dependency direction, public surface) under demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]` (1M-context variant). Declared for this seat, not inherited. Model receipt written at the head of my pass-3 section in the report.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 (re-confirmed with the confound removed): the "Add current color" CTA and every swatch in the component are inert in the shipped build — glass-ui 7's WatercolorDot is `inheritAttrs:false`, root always `<span>`, hardcoded `aria-hidden="true"` and unconditional `pointer-events:none`, no `tag` prop, no default slot, so `tag="button"` / `:aria-label` / `@click` / `<Plus>` are all silently discarded. Strongest ON-AXIS defect is L-15: this repo's own library publishes the wrong surface (`makeColor`/`SPACE_SCHEMA`/`SPACE_IDS`/`isAnyColor` exist in `src/color/model.ts` and are exported nowhere; no immutable `with*` combinators exist in `src/` at all), which forced the demo to forge a parallel colour model and is the upstream cause of the string-typed colour that makes this whole cone fragile.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND, but these were interrogated and came back clean, measured at HEAD 5c13465d: (1) zero deep library reaches from the demo — `grep -rEn 'from "(\.\./)+src/|@src/' demo` → 0 hits, `grep -rEn 'value\.js/(dist|src)/' demo` → 0 hits; (2) all 39 `@mkbabb/value.js/*` specifiers in demo/ are real `package.json#exports` keys (/color /css /easing /math /quantize) — a real consumer could write every one; (3) `vite.config.ts:30-48` generates the self-alias set FROM the exports map with anchored regexes, so it cannot drift; (4) `verbatimModuleSyntax` compliance is correct at every type-only site in the cone (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:190, useSwatchActions.ts:2-3, SwatchHoverMenu.vue:60); (5) the subject component imports the library not at all, so it makes no false claim about the public API directly. NOTE — a correction recorded in the report: passes 1-2 read negative (1)+(2) as proof the library boundary was sound. It is not. The demo does not reach past the export map because it CANNOT; the map does not publish what it needs, so it built a second copy instead (L-15). A clean import graph concealed a duplicated domain.

defects.defect: Wrong public surface: the library's generic colour model is private, so its only consumer forged a second one. `src/color/model.ts` exports SPACE_SCHEMA (:56-74, 17 spaces x channel names + hueIndex + css flag), SPACE_IDS (:76), makeColor(space,channels,alpha) (:136-142) and isAnyColor (:127-135); `src/color/index.ts` re-exports NONE of them, so `src/subpaths/color.ts` publishes none. No immutable channel combinators exist in src/ at all. demo/color-session/picker-color.ts therefore hand-rolls buildColor (:123-143, a 17-arm switch = makeColor with the generic erased), PICKER_CHANNELS (:52-, a second copy of SPACE_SCHEMA.channels), CSS_PICKER_SPACES (= the css flag), the hue:true marker (= hueIndex), and withAlpha/withChannel/withNormalizedChannel/channelNumber/normalizedChannel (:151-192).

defects.reproduction: `node -e "import('./dist/subpaths/color.js').then(m=>console.log(Object.keys(m).sort().join(', ')))"` from the repo root, then `grep -n 'SPACE_SCHEMA\|makeColor\|isAnyColor' src/color/model.ts src/color/index.ts` — present in model.ts at :56/:136/:127, absent from index.ts and from the built subpath.

defects.defect: The component's primary CTA and every swatch are inert in the shipped build. glass-ui@7.0.0 WatercolorDot is a decorative primitive: `inheritAttrs: !1` (drops every fallthrough attr AND listener), root is always `o("span", ...)` with hardcoded `aria-hidden:"true"`, `pointerEvents:"none"` applied AFTER attrs.style (unoverridable, not variant-gated), props are exactly {color,variant,animate,cycleDuration,range,seed} (no `tag`), and the render children are [svg, ghost-stroke] with no renderSlot. CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 hands it tag="button", :aria-label, @click="addCurrentColor" and a <Plus> child; all four are discarded. SwatchHoverMenu.vue:14-35 repeats it on every saved swatch. Re-confirmed this pass with the L-16 confound removed.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js:79-115. Live DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: both dots inside .dashed-well -> {tag:"SPAN", ariaHidden:"true", hasAriaLabel:false, pe:"none"}; lucideIconsInsideDots:0; elementFromPoint(ghost centre)="DIV.", hitIsGhost:false. Clean discriminator (empty palette, opaque colour): {solidBefore:0, solidAfter:0, store:'{"inputColor":"oklch(0.7 0.15 30)","savedColors":[]}'} after a click dispatched directly on the node. Gates blind: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exit 0 in 9.9s; `npx eslint` on both files clean. Visual: shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png shows the dashed add-slot with no + glyph.
defects.mechanism: ownership inversion at the consumer/design-system boundary — an interactive affordance delegated to a primitive that is decorative by construction
defects.reproduction: In the browser at http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: `localStorage.setItem("color-picker", JSON.stringify({inputColor:"oklch(0.7 0.15 30)", savedColors:[]})); location.reload();` then after settle `const g=document.querySelector('.dashed-well .add-slot-ghost'); g.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click',{bubbles:true,cancelable:true}));` — swatch count stays 0, localStorage savedColors stays []. getComputedStyle(g).pointerEvents === 'none', g.tagName === 'SPAN', g.hasAttribute('aria-label') === false.
defects.proposedCure: Demo side: the swatch becomes a real <button> (or glass-ui Button icon-only) that CONTAINS a WatercolorDot as its fill — the dot stays aria-hidden and pointer-transparent, which is correct for a decoration; the affordance is the app's, the paint is glass-ui's. Producer side (BH/BI relay letter, not a demo patch): glass-ui ships a `./swatch` interactive primitive — a real button hosting the paint, owning `btn-interactive` — or gives WatercolorDot an explicit `interactive` posture. A primitive that silently eats tag/aria-label/onClick/default-slot will reproduce this bug in every consumer.

defects.defect: "Is this colour already in the palette?" is implemented twice with different alpha semantics, and the two run in sequence on one click. useSwatchActions.ts:63 does `savedColorStrings.indexOf(cssColorOpaque)` — an ALPHA-STRIPPED candidate against an ALPHA-BEARING haystack (cssColorOpaque = serializePickerColor(withAlpha(color,1)) at useColorPipeline.ts:104; savedColorStrings = savedColors.map(serializePickerColor) at :166-168, alpha preserved). useColorPipeline.ts:213-217 then does `savedColors.some(c => toCSSColorString(c) === toCSSColorString(model.color))` — alpha-bearing both sides. On alpha-bearing data the first says ABSENT (emit the add) and the second says PRESENT (return without adding): the gesture is a silent no-op.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:63 vs useColorPipeline.ts:213-217; useColorPipeline.ts:104 and :166-168 for the two serializations. Live: seeding localStorage color-picker with {inputColor:"oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)", savedColors:["oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)"]} and reloading yields store `savedColors:["oklch(70% 0.15 30deg / 50%)"]` (alpha survives) and countLabel ["1 color"], while cssColorOpaque is "oklch(70% 0.15 30deg)". Alpha is one gesture away: shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png shows the alpha channel at 82.7%, and ColorPicker.vue:293 commits every swatch edit as toCSSColorString(model.value.color) — the alpha-bearing serialization — back into savedColorStrings via usePaletteActions.ts:99-106.
defects.mechanism: duplicated domain predicate with divergent policy — the direct consequence of colour being string-typed above the library (see L-15)
defects.reproduction: At http://localhost:9000/#/palettes: `localStorage.setItem("color-picker", JSON.stringify({inputColor:"oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)", savedColors:["oklch(0.7 0.15 30 / 0.5)"]})); location.reload();` — after settle the palette shows "1 color" with savedColorStrings[0]==="oklch(70% 0.15 30deg / 50%)" while cssColorOpaque==="oklch(70% 0.15 30deg)", so indexOf returns -1 (add is emitted) and onPaletteAddColor's some() returns true (add is swallowed). Equivalent UI path: add a colour, edit it, move the alpha slider, commit, then press add.
defects.proposedCure: One predicate, one home. Once L-15 lands this is a library question — `colorsEqual(a,b)` beside mixColors in src/color/operations.ts, called by both sites; until then it belongs in demo/color-session/ as the single owner of colour identity. And the policy must be chosen rather than inherited: addColor currently STORES the opaque colour while DEDUPING against the alpha-bearing one, which is an accident of two authors, not a rule.

defects.defect: The module that declares itself the palette-browser feature's "TOP-LEVEL SEAM ... the stable public API ... External consumers reach the feature through THIS seam, never a raw internal .vue file" has zero importers, and the subject component reaches past it in the other direction. Complements pass-1 L-6 (the eslint law that would enforce it lints to undefined): not only is the law dead, the surface it protects has no users.

Zero reach demo/palettes/browser/index.ts (46 lines, 18 of them the seam declaration). Violating edge in the other direction: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:193 imports "../status/ApiOfflineChip.vue" — a raw internal .vue from a DIFFERENT cluster — which demo/palettes/browser/status/index.ts:2-3 documents as a self-granted exception.

defects.reproduction: `grep -rn "palettes/browser" demo | grep -v '^demo/palettes/browser/'` from the repo root; four hits, none targeting index.ts. `npx eslint demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue` is clean despite the raw cross-cluster .vue import at :193.

Either the sub-barrels ARE the contract — delete browser/index.ts, re-target G-DEMO-3b at the real tree (files: ["demo/**/*.{ts,vue}"], pattern **/palettes/browser/**/*.vue with barrels excepted) and fix the one violating edge — or the seam is the contract and the four external consumers move onto it. defects.defect: Two pure aliases with a dead parameter sit exactly at the seam where L-16's divergence hides. demo/color-session/color-model.ts:60-72: `colorToHexString(color)` is a one-line pass-through to pickerColorToHex, and `toCSSColorString(color, _digits = 2)` is a one-line pass-through to serializePickerColor whose `_digits` parameter is declared, defaulted and never read — it advertises precision control and silently ignores it.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-model.ts:60-72. Four call sites of toCSSColorString: ColorPicker.vue:293, useColorUrl.ts:6, useColorPipeline.ts:214, useColorPipeline.ts:216 — none passes a second argument. The alias is why L-16 went unnoticed: useColorPipeline.ts:214,216 compares via `toCSSColorString` while useSwatchActions.ts:63 compares via `cssColorOpaque` built on `serializePickerColor` — the same function under two names, given different alpha inputs.

defects.reproduction: Read demo/color-session/color-model.ts:59-72; the body of toCSSColorString ignores its second parameter entirely. `grep -rn "toCSSColorString" demo` -> 4 call sites, all single-argument.
