LIVE hover (cpe-probe4.mjs): swatch rect y=347.64; panel `{"position":"static","top":"305.641px","inlineStyle":"top: 305.641px; left: 791px;","rect":{"x":0,"y":900,"w":1440,"h":40},"background":"rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)","boxShadow":"none","zIndex":"auto","ariaHidden":"true","buttons":["Edit color …","Copy color …","Remove color …"],"docScrollH":940,"winH":900}`. Screenshot scratchpad/cpe-hover.png shows nothing near the hovered swatch.
defects.mechanism: hand-rolled floating surface whose positioning contract lives entirely in a CSS class that was never authored (or was deleted — cf. the tranche-b precedent commit e7da1b5c "strip phantom floating-panel-item class"); nothing in the toolchain fails when a class name resolves to no rule
defects.reproduction: 1440x900, /#/palettes with seeded colours, hover a swatch, then `getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.floating-panel')).position` → "static" and `.getBoundingClientRect()` → {x:0,y:900,w:1440,h:40}.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: delete the hover branch, useHoverPopover and useLeaveTimer entirely and let the reka-ui Popover that SwatchHoverMenu already imports serve both pointer classes. floating-ui does the positioning (no manual getBoundingClientRect, no phantom class, no scroll drift), reka does focus management and Escape, and the panel becomes keyboard-operable and announced instead of aria-hidden. Removes ~100 lines and three defects at once.

defects.defect: The duplicate-name `Update` affordance irreversibly destroys a stored palette: `duplicateTarget` is a snapshot ref that is never invalidated when the name or the colour buffer changes, and `confirmUpdatePalette` lacks the emptiness guard its sibling `saveCurrentPalette` has.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:248 `if (savedColorStrings.length === 0) return;` (guarded) vs :267-276 `confirmUpdatePalette` (unguarded); no watcher clears `duplicateTarget`. Write path: usePaletteActions.ts:79-82 → usePaletteStore.ts:96-107 `palette.colors = patch.colors` into useStorage. LIVE (cpe-probe9.mjs): `1 store after save: [{"name":"Keeper","colors":3}]` … `3 swatches after emptying: 0` … `3 banner still present? "Start a new palette … \"Keeper\" already exists. Update Cancel"` … `4 store AFTER Update with an empty buffer: [{"name":"Keeper","colors":0}]`. Name-loss variant (cpe-probe5.mjs): after retyping "Totally different", the banner still says "Palette 2" already exists and `S store after Update: [{"name":"Palette 2","n":3}]`.
defects.mechanism: derived state stored as a snapshot ref; the premise that produced it (a name + a non-empty buffer) can change arbitrarily while the affordance stays live and re-reads the CURRENT buffer at click time
defects.reproduction: Save a palette named X; stage colours again; type X + Enter to raise the duplicate banner; remove the staged swatches via the swatch menu; click Update. The stored X now has colors: [] with no undo.
defects.proposedCure: Make it derived, not stored: `const duplicateTarget = computed(() => savedColorStrings.length === 0 ? null : savedPalettes.find(p => p.name.toLowerCase() === trimmedName.value.toLowerCase()) ?? null)` with `trimmedName` also computed, so it self-invalidates on every keystroke and can never outlive its premise; keep only the "user attempted a save" flag as a ref.

defects.defect: The edit target is identified by array index, and the same composable re-indexes that array on removal — so committing an edit after removing an earlier swatch writes past the end and APPENDS a phantom duplicate colour; the edit overlay also silently vanishes, stranding the user in edit mode with no commit/cancel affordance on desktop.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:76-83 emits `colorIndex: index`; :90-94 `filter((_, i) => i !== index)` shifts every later index. Consumer usePaletteActions.ts:99-107: `oldCss = savedColorStrings[colorIndex]` (undefined) → passes the `oldCss === newCss` bail → `updated[colorIndex] = newCss` grows the array. LIVE (cpe-probe7.mjs): `0 savedColors: ["lab(50% 20 -30)","lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"]` → `1 after startEdit(2) — overlays: 1` → `3 after remove(0) — swatches: 2 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)"] overlays: 0` → `4 after Enter-commit — swatches: 3 savedColors: ["lab(70% -40 10)","lab(30% 5 60)","lab(30% 5 60)"]`, `4 count label: 3 colors`.
defects.mechanism: ordinal identity carried across a mutation that redefines the ordinals; both halves of the invariant live in one file and neither enforces it
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 /#/palettes with 3 seeded colours: hover swatch index 2 → Edit; hover swatch index 0 → Remove; press Enter (ColorPicker.vue:377 global keydown → :258 commitEdit). savedColors gains a duplicate third entry, persisted.
defects.proposedCure: Identify the edit target by identity, not ordinal — mint a per-entry id where the buffer is minted (useColorPipeline.savedColors) and key edits on it; resolve any index at the moment of mutation only. Minimum hardening if the ordinal stays: `commitColorEdit` bails when `colorIndex >= savedColorStrings.length`, and the emit that re-indexes the array clears the pending edit target.

defects.defect: `swatchKeys` — 18 lines of Map + counter + cleanup watcher sold as "stable keys for TransitionGroup" — is provably identical to `:key="`${color}::${i}`"` and strictly worse than `:key="i"`: one removal re-keys and remounts every trailing swatch.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:42-59. Proof: the Map is a bijection (color,index)→counter, so the emitted key is an injective relabelling of `${color}::${i}` — identical equalities, identical diff; the pre-flush cleanup watcher additionally deletes pairs whose index moved, so a returning colour gets a FRESH counter. LIVE (cpe-probe4.mjs), wrappers tagged via dataset before removing index 0: `D wrappers after removing index 0: [{"probeTag":"(NEW NODE)","label":"lab(70% -40 10)"},{"probeTag":"(NEW NODE)","label":"lab(30% 5 60)"}]`.
defects.mechanism: the key function depends on the index it is meant to be invariant to; the cleanup watcher then actively destroys the little residual stability the Map would have had
defects.reproduction: Stage 3 colours, tag each `.swatch-row > div.relative` with a dataset marker, remove index 0 via the swatch menu, re-read the markers — both survivors are new DOM nodes.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the Map, the counter and the watcher. If per-entry identity matters (C-5 says it does), mint a real id in the buffer that owns the data and key on that; otherwise one line of string concatenation is the same thing. This is the no-contrivance edict at its purest.

defects.defect: The component's own default palette name collides with an existing palette: the placeholder and the fallback are both `Palette ${savedPaletteCount + 1}` — a cardinality, not a high-water mark — so the component proposes a name, the user accepts it, and the component then refuses it with a duplicate banner naming a string the user never typed.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:127-128 (placeholder) and :249-250 (fallback), checked against the same list at :253-259. LIVE (cpe-probe5.mjs): after saving one palette explicitly named "Palette 2", `S placeholder on 2nd save (default name): "Palette 2"` and pressing Enter on the empty field gives `S well text after default-name save: "Current Palette 3 colors … \"Palette 2\" already exists. Update Cancel"`.
defects.mechanism: name generation derived from list length instead of from the set of names in use
defects.reproduction: Save a palette named exactly "Palette 2"; restage colours; press Enter with the name field empty → duplicate banner for the component's own suggestion.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the default from the existing names: smallest n such that `Palette n` is unused (one while-loop over a Set of lowercased names), expressed as a computed so the placeholder and the fallback cannot disagree.

defects.defect: The save button is icon-only with no accessible name — the component's contribution to the visual REPORT's namelessButtons tally, invisible to the capture because it only renders once the palette is non-empty.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:134-142 (`icon-only`, `<Check>`, no aria-label, no text). LIVE with a colour staged (cpe-probe4.mjs): `B nameless visible buttons: [ …, {"w":32,"h":40,"cls":"button tap-squish focus-ring glass-wash glass-capsule … h-8 w-","inWell":true,"html":"<svg …"} ]`. REPORT.json records namelessButtons:1 for safari-desktop-light /#/palettes, captured with an EMPTY palette so the save row never rendered — the route's true working-state count is 2. e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:39-41 documents the gap in prose and routes around it.
defects.mechanism: icon-only control with the name carried only by the glyph; the audit capture never reaches the state that renders it
defects.reproduction: /#/palettes with a staged colour → enumerate visible buttons with empty aria-label/title/innerText → the 32x40 Check button inside `.dashed-well`.
defects.proposedCure: `aria-label="Save current palette"`. The three sibling swatch-action buttons at :46,49,52 already do this; this is the one that was missed.

defects.defect: Three dead-code sites: an unreachable `:disabled`, an unreachable null-guard created by widening a prop type the store had already narrowed, and a 24-line TooltipProvider block that never renders a tooltip.
defects.evidence: (1) :138 `:disabled="savedColorStrings.length === 0"` sits inside :118 `v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"`. (2) :271 `if (id == null) return;` — usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 narrows to `p is Palette & { id: string }`, but the prop at :201 is widened to `Palette[]`, discarding the proof and re-checking at runtime. (3) :88-111 Tooltip block — LIVE (cpe-probe8.mjs): `3 tooltip after hovering add slot: {"tooltips":0,"tooltipText":[]}` after a 900ms hover.
defects.mechanism: defensive checks retained after their preconditions became structural, plus a tooltip whose trigger attrs are eaten by the C-1 mechanism
defects.reproduction: Hover the add slot for 900ms → `document.querySelectorAll('[role="tooltip"]').length === 0`.
defects.proposedCure: Type the prop as the store types it (`(Palette & { id: string })[]`) so the guard deletes itself; drop the dead `:disabled`; delete the tooltip block (the aria-label it duplicates is the real name, once C-1 makes the control real).

defects.defect: One gesture, two contradictory insert orders, and an alpha-blind dedupe: `addCurrentColor` moves an existing colour to the END while the wiring that services a new colour unshifts to the FRONT; the dedupe compares an alpha-stripped probe against alpha-preserving stored strings.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:62-74 (`reordered.push(...)` → emit apply) vs usePaletteWiring.ts:84-100 (`savedColors.unshift(parsed)`, and existing → unshift to front). Format mismatch: useColorPipeline.ts:104 `cssColorOpaque = serializePickerColor(withAlpha(model.value.color, 1))` vs :166 `savedColorStrings = model.value.savedColors.map(serializePickerColor)` (alpha preserved); commitColorEdit writes `toCSSColorString(model.value.color)` which can carry alpha.
defects.mechanism: two independent dedupe/ordering implementations for one user intent, plus string-identity comparison across two different serialisation policies
defects.reproduction: NONE for the ordering split as a user-visible sequence while C-1 keeps the control dead — code-level contradiction, verified by reading both implementations. The alpha mismatch is likewise reachable only once C-1 is repaired.
defects.proposedCure: The component emits intent (`addColor`) and the buffer's owner applies the ONE ordering rule; delete the reorder branch in addCurrentColor. Compare colours by parsed value, never by serialised string, or normalise both sides through one serializer.

defects.defect: Hygiene in the hover machinery: the leave timer is never cancelled on scope disposal, a media query is subscribed even when the caller supplies canHover, and the panel position is computed once with no scroll/resize reposition.
defects.evidence: useLeaveTimer.ts (17 lines) — no onScopeDispose; onLeave schedules a 250ms callback that outlives unmount and writes a ref in a dead scope. useHoverPopover.ts:11-14 calls `useBreakpoint("(hover: hover)")` unconditionally then discards it when `options.canHover` is provided. useHoverPopover.ts:20-24 writes viewport coords on pointerenter only; no scroll/resize listener, while PalettesPane.vue:2 is `overflow-y-auto`. (glass-ui useBreakpoint DOES dispose — dist/dom.js `c() && u(a)` — so this is waste, not a leak.)
defects.mechanism: a hand-rolled floating primitive re-implementing anchoring and lifetime that a real popover library owns
defects.reproduction: NONE as a user-visible failure while C-3 keeps the panel unpositioned; the timer and subscription facts are read directly from the two files.
defects.proposedCure: Subsumed by the C-3 cure (adopt the reka-ui Popover). If the composable survives at all, add `onScopeDispose(cancel)` and skip the useBreakpoint call when canHover is supplied.

defects.defect: Per-tick work in a row whose contents did not change: 202 DOM mutation records in the swatch row during one 40-step slider drag, with three unchanging saved colours.
defects.evidence: LIVE (cpe-probe6.mjs), MutationObserver on `.swatch-row` (attributes+childList+subtree): `4 swatch-row DOM mutations during a 40-step slider drag: {"row":202,"addSlot":0}` — ~5 per pointer move. Drivers: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:96 `:color="cssColorOpaque"` on the add-slot dot, where glass-ui useWatercolorBlob watches `color` and re-derives 8 random border-radius percentages + the feTurbulence seed per change; and useColorPipeline.ts:166 `savedColorStrings` is a computed over a shallowRef replaced wholesale each tick, so its array identity churns every frame and fires useSwatchActions.ts:54's cleanup watch (fresh Set of N strings + full Map scan) plus the swatchKeys map.
defects.mechanism: a live, high-frequency value bound into a component tree that only needs it at commit time; plus identity-churning derived arrays feeding per-tick watchers
defects.reproduction: 1440x900 /#/palettes with 3 seeded colours → attach the MutationObserver to `.swatch-row` → drag the L slider 40 steps → read the record count.
defects.proposedCure: Seed the add-slot from the already-exported coalesced source (`cssColorOpaqueFrame`, useColorPipeline.ts:279) or from a static seed, and let the C-6 cure delete the per-tick key machinery outright.

defects.defect: An assertive backend annunciator is gated on palette emptiness: `<ApiOfflineChip v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0">` mounts a `role="alert"` live region every time the buffer crosses 0↔1 colours, re-announcing backend state as if it had just changed.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116; ApiOfflineChip.vue:13 `role="alert"` (self-gating already via `v-if="misconfigured"` / `v-else-if="offline"`). LIVE aria snapshot (cpe-probe8.mjs): the chip is the SECOND node in the component's entire accessible tree — `- alert: "dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"`.
defects.mechanism: a status region's lifetime tied to unrelated content state, so mount/unmount churn becomes repeated assertive announcements
defects.reproduction: With the backend unreachable/misconfigured, add then remove the last colour repeatedly on /#/palettes — the alert region is re-created on each 0→1 transition.
defects.proposedCure: Drop the emptiness condition and let the chip self-gate on availability alone, or hoist it to the pane, where backend state actually belongs.

defects.defect: Vacuous/absent gate: no unit test touches the component, the single e2e spec that does is RED on HEAD, CI runs no Playwright at all, and vue-tsc cannot see any of the C-1/C-2 attribute loss.
defects.evidence: `grep -rl "mount(" test/` → nothing; nothing imports CurrentPaletteEditor/useSwatchActions/useHoverPopover/useLeaveTimer. RAN: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts --project=smoke --reporter=line` → `1 failed … Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Error: locator.click … waiting for getByRole('main', { name: 'Color tool panes' }).getByRole('button', { name: /Add current color .* to palette/ }).filter({ visible: true })`. `grep -n "playwright\|e2e" .github/workflows/*.yml` → no output (ci.yml runs lint, vue-tsc x2, build, npm test, packed-surface check). RAN: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → `EXIT=0`.
defects.mechanism: the only behavioural gate asserts a localStorage row appeared, not that the component works — and it is not executed by CI anyway; Vue attribute fallthrough makes the producer-contract violation invisible to the typechecker
defects.reproduction: Run the spec (pasted above). The exact mutation that keeps every gate green even after C-1 is fixed: replace `colorsFromStrings` (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:243-245) with `() => []` — every palette saves EMPTY, and `expect.poll(...palettes?.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1)` still passes. Deleting the whole duplicate-name path, confirmUpdatePalette, and all three swatch actions is likewise green.
defects.proposedCure: Three component tests that each fail on a real defect: (1) mount with savedColorStrings ['a','b'] and assert two role=button elements named /Color swatch/ (fails on C-2); (2) raise the duplicate banner, empty the buffer, click Update, assert NO `updated` emit (fails on C-4); (3) startEdit(1) then remove(0), assert the pending target is cleared (fails on C-5). Then wire Playwright into ci.yml — palette-save.spec.ts has been red on a blocker that no gate reported.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`, the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with. Declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-16 · One click on the pane's own Retry button permanently destroys the pane body — reproduced in Chromium (blank at t=1021 ms) AND WebKit (t=303 ms), clean page, 6-second tail, terminal residue 12 px, no error/empty/skeleton/retry state left. Structurally: `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (BrowsePane.vue:40) drives a three-state machine that can settle faster than its own leave duration, and there is no fourth state to land in — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6 forbids exactly this ("No full-slab remount hole"). Runner-up, and the deeper cause of most other findings: D-01, the `Card` shell is on the field and the entity slip has none, which §3.1 requires exactly inverted.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the following were attacked and held, and three pass-1 findings were killed by measurement. (1) No horizontal overflow anywhere: STATES.json overflowX=0 and clipped=[] for /#/browse in all six matrices incl. rtl-desktop and rtl-mobile; REPORT.md horizontalOverflow bucket empty across 60 captures. (2) Motion is fully tokenized and reduced-motion-correct: animations.css:83-139 uses only --duration-fast/-normal/--spring-snappy/--ease-*; global PRM guard at :177-182; stagger fenced at :43; STATES.json rafPer1500ms=0 under reduced-motion-desktop vs 270 at rest; BrowsePane defines and deletes no keyframes. (3) No layout-forcing transition on the entity card: measured transitionDuration=0s (the "all" I first read is the CSS initial value); motion is compositor-only via useLiquidPress transform. (4) Keyboard focus IS visible on the wall's controls — evidence/D3-chromium-vote-chip-focused.png shows the rendered ring; pass-1's implied absence refuted. (5) Every control is named: REPORT.md namelessButtons for /#/browse = 0 in all four matrices; SearchFilterBar.vue:5 aria-label="Filters" — pass-1 R2.6 KILLED. (6) The search placeholder does NOT overflow at 390 px: Chromium 151.0 vs 236.0 available, WebKit 151.1 vs 235.0 — fits with 36% slack in both engines; pass-1 D-11 KILLED (the shot's clip is a font-swap transient). (7) `.pane-scroll-fade` does implement its fade — PaneHeader.vue:54-57 scroll-timeline + the ::before veil consumer; pass-1 R2.8 KILLED. (8) The dock's 7/12 Tab reachability is roving tabindex and is CORRECT — NOT born-RED, per MT-F022; only the card root's unfocusability was born-RED, on a two-engine `.focus()` no-op proof. (9) verbatimModuleSyntax honoured (BrowsePane.vue:197); no god module, no legacy shim in the file. (10) main landmark count exactly 1, no nested main.

defects.defect: The `Card` shell is on the field and the entity slip has none — the exact inverse of the binding composition. BrowsePane.vue:2 wraps the whole field in `<Card tier="resting" … h-full>`; PaletteCard.vue:5-27 hand-rolls the entity as `<div role="article" class="…cartoon-surface…">` and never imports Card, so not one of the seven props PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.12 fixes for the entity tuple is even expressible.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3.1 verbatim: "every rendered bounded palette entity slip has exactly one Card shell, and the field/empty/inspector have none" and "`Card` … is never the default page primitive". Measured: `grep -rn 'Card tier="resting"' demo/ | wc -l` → 9; demo/DESIGN.md canonizes it as "the picker card AND all 9 pane cards". PaletteCard.vue:12-15 comment: "NOT <Card surface=cartoon>".
defects.mechanism: housing inversion — the design-system primitive attached one level too high
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'Card tier="resting"' demo/ ; read BrowsePane.vue:2 and PaletteCard.vue:5-27
defects.proposedCure: Delete `<Card>` from BrowsePane.vue:2 (the field becomes browse-workspace-chassis region content with no shell); make PaletteCard's root the `<Card>` with §5.12's exact seven-prop tuple. The nine-pane family closes in the same cut.

defects.defect: One click on the pane's own Retry button permanently destroys the pane body. Terminal state in both engines: no error, no empty plate, no skeleton, no recovery — a 12 px residue where the body was.
defects.evidence: probe-D3-retry-focus.mjs, clean page, 6 s tail, 60 ms sampling. Chromium: before {children:1,h:240.5}; t=1021 ms {n:0,h:21.1,txt:""}; t=2342 ms {n:0,h:12}; after6s {children:0,h:12,paneText:"Browse Discover palettes from the community. My Palettes …"}. WebKit: t=303 ms {n:0,h:12}; after6s identical. Screenshot evidence/D3-chromium-after-retry.png. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "No full-slab remount hole, rAF-delayed blank, or dock collapse."

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-D3-retry-focus.mjs chromium (and …webkit); open http://localhost:9000/#/browse, click Retry

defects.defect: The composition is the equal-card matrix §3.1 rules out: measured 50.0 / 50.0 where the law mandates 64–66.7 % protagonist and a 33.3–36 % selected-public-palette inspector. No inspector exists at all.

Coordinate demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:124-131 `browse: { left: "browse", right: "palettes" }`; §4.2 retires "the global Dock PaneSegmentedControl and left/right view state" by name.

defects.reproduction: node …/probe-D-design.mjs chromium — geom-desktop-dark; read demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:124-131

Measured 512/1024 = 50.0 % — 3.3× the ceiling. Frames: evidence/D-chromium-wall-populated.png, evidence/D2-chromium-wall-desktop-dark.png. Owning register row PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-04 ("Empty/equal companion Cards and nested housing → REMOVE … Admin companion 50%→0").

defects.reproduction: node …/probe-D2-states.mjs chromium ; view evidence/D-chromium-wall-populated.png

defects.defect: The palette card is a clickable `role="article"` with no keyboard path to its own activation, in both engines. No `aria-pressed`, no native button spanning the specimen/identity region, and all seven modes §5 forbids on the card body are present.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 verbatim: "A palette card is a bounded entity article, not a clickable `role=article` … One native named `<button type=\"button\">` spans its specimen/identity region … The card body owns no expand, inline rename, action menu, transient result or hover-only swatch-action path." Measured root: {tag:"DIV", role:"article", tabIndex:-1, ariaPressed:null, cursor:"pointer"}. Programmatic focus, BOTH engines: chromium {becameActive:false, hasTabindexAttr:false}; webkit {becameActive:false, hasTabindexAttr:false}. Chromium Tab walk reaches only inner controls ("n votes, click to vote", "Palette menu"), never a seat. The seven modes: expand :97, rename :112-120, menu :83-106, transient feedback :123, hover popover :139-157.
defects.mechanism: activation attached to a non-interactive container role instead of a nested named button seat
defects.reproduction: node …/probe-D3-retry-focus.mjs chromium ; node …/probe-D3-retry-focus.mjs webkit — cardRootFocusable

Keyboard reachability closes as a consequence, not as a tabindex patch. NOTE: the route's 7/12 empty-arm Tab gap is dock roving tabindex and is CORRECT — deliberately not born-RED (MT-F022).

defects.defect: On mobile the palette's name — the card's protagonist — is crushed to 5.6 px of clipped glyph stubs by its own badges. Confirmed in both engines. Even at 1440 the featured card renders "Wall Palett…".
defects.evidence: Measured identity span width, first (Featured) card: chromium 390×844 → 5.6 px, titleClipped true; webkit 390×844 → 5.6 px, titleClipped true; 1440×900 → 128.8 px but visually truncated (evidence/D3-chromium-vote-chip-focused.png). Frame: evidence/D2-chromium-wall-mobile-light.png. Mechanism at PaleteCard.vue:43-79 — every decoration carries `shrink-0` (:64 featured badge, :72 count badge, PaletteCardMeta chips, :82 menu wrapper) while the identity span :54-59 is the sole flexible item, so it absorbs 100 % of the deficit. result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for `demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue`
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; the seat is declared, not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D2-01 — the component is a specimen case asked to be an instrument, and every verb it owns is dead in every modality. glass-ui 7's `WatercolorDot` compiles to `inheritAttrs:false` + `<span aria-hidden="true" pointer-events:none>` with no slot, so `tag="button"`, `aria-label`, `@click` and the `<Plus>` glyph at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 are all discarded. Measured live: all six faces are inert aria-hidden spans; a real WebKit `touchscreen.tap` at 390×844 yields 0 popper wrappers and 0 `Edit color`/`Remove color` nodes anywhere in the document; the desktop hover panel lays out at x0/y900, `position:static`, transparent, `aria-hidden`, one viewport height below the fold. The tabbable inventory of the whole well is [unnamed INPUT, unnamed BUTTON]. Consequence: there is no path in the product that removes a colour from the current palette — the draft is append-only until a nameless commit erases all of it.
result.negativeProof: Not SOUND — but the following were attacked and could not be broken, and one banked pass-1 finding is retracted. (1) MOTION IS CLEAN: the TransitionGroup rides the house `vj-enter` family (animations.css:83-100) on `--duration-normal`/`--ease-decelerate` + `--spring-smooth-duration`/`--spring-smooth`; no ad-hoc timings; the global `prefers-reduced-motion` guard at animations.css:184 neutralises all three families; probe-D5 `p5-reduced` measures `animatedDots: 0` with geometry identical to the normal run; only `opacity`/`transform` animate — nothing layout-forcing. (2) RETRACTION: pass-1 D-8 ("light header ink 3.19:1 FAIL") is NOT CONFIRMED — that figure came from parsing `oklab(0.913299 0.005463 0.013024)` components as sRGB bytes. Resolved through a canvas 2-D context, the header measures 5.08:1 light / 5.97:1 dark — both PASS 4.5:1. (3) No horizontal overflow, no clipping, one `<main>`, zero page errors across 12 scenarios incl. 24 colours at 390px and the 400%-zoom arm (`overflowsParent:false` everywhere). (4) RTL mirrors correctly: direction rtl, row children [625,567,509,451,393,335], commit button moves to the inline start. (5) `demo/ui/{button,input,tooltip,popover}/index.ts` are pure re-exports of @mkbabb/glass-ui — no local fork, edict 4's demo/ui clause satisfied. (6) `verbatimModuleSyntax` clean — :190 is the only type-only import and is `import type`. (7) Vue 3.5 idioms correct — reactive props destructure at :196 plus `toRef(() => …)` at :234-235; no stale defineModel round-trip. (8) No god module — 312 lines with three real composables extracted.

Any face that must render a user colour on the well gets a producer-owned contrast-guarded edge — the same gamut-guarded ≥4.5:1 resolver this repo already applies to the title ramp (utils.css:186-200).

defects.defect: All three of the well's declared boundary devices measure below the 3:1 non-text floor; the two schemes were calibrated to different standards; and the authored hairline is a device-pixel accident.
defects.evidence: utils.css:90-107 declares tone-step + 1.5px dashed edge + 3-layer caster and states at :103 that "the dashed edge ALONE carries the in-progress semantics". probe-D6.json/probe-D7.json: dashed edge composited on the well fill = 1.27:1 light / 1.38:1 dark; well tone-step vs its host plate = 1.13:1 light (rgb distance 24) vs 2.45:1 dark (rgb distance 102) — a 4.25× scheme asymmetry from one token; used border-width = 1px at DPR 1, 1.5px at DPR 2. Casters contradict: well `-2px 2px 0 0, -3px 3px, -4px 4px` (down-left) nested inside Card `8px 8px 0 0` (down-right).
defects.mechanism: M3 — rendered contrast never measured on the real tier; plus PR-05 boundary duplication and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186's ban on casters stacked within casters.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D6.mjs and probe-D7.mjs (scenarios a-orange-1440-dpr1 vs d-orange-1440-dpr2).
defects.proposedCure: One device per boundary, resolved per scheme against the plate the well actually sits on, at ≥3:1, defined where `--well-bg` is defined so fixture and edge move together. Delete the caster and the dashed edge — which also frees the dashed language to mean exactly one thing (D2-09).

defects.defect: The only reachable list mutation — save → clearCurrent → apply([]) — is unannounced, and its exit implodes five swatches onto a single point because the leave rule's containing block is the whole pane Card.
defects.evidence: utils.css:177-179 `.swatch-row > .vj-enter-leave-active { position: absolute }` but `.swatch-row` computes `position: static`, so offsetParent = `DIV.glass-resting card rounded-card`. probe-D8.json tightSamples: leaving x goes [767,813,858,904,950] → [767,786,804,823,842] → [770,787,801,814,828] → [787,790,792,794,797] — all five converge. probe-D8.json frames: wellH 196.70 → 114.11 within 40ms while 5 boxes are still animating (−82.59px in one frame). Live regions before/after: two alerts + one status → one alert; nothing announces success. animations.css:75-77 documents a `vj-celebrate` family literally described as "a ONE-SHOT feedback beat (saved!, error pop)" — unused here.
defects.mechanism: M4 — motion budget inverted: decoration gets the only transition; the structural seam and the semantic event get none, and the leave rule resolves against the wrong containing block.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D8.mjs — seeds 5 colours, names the draft, clicks commit, samples per rAF.
defects.proposedCure: Give `.swatch-row` `position: relative` so the exit belongs to the row; put the well's height change on the same spring as its contents; put the commit result in a durable status the entity owns, with `vj-celebrate` as the optional flourish (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:101).

defects.defect: Three structural `v-if` seams reflow instantly with no transition and no reserve, moving the whole palette library below them.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:18, :116, :117 and :144 are bare `v-if` with no `<Transition>`. probe-D5.json p1-light.zoneTransitions: `.dashed-well` and all four zones compute `transition: "all"` (duration 0s). Measured steps: first colour 114.11 → 196.70 (+82.59px); name collision 196.70 → 242.70 (+46.00px); commit 196.70 → 114.11 (−82.59px).
defects.mechanism: M4 — motion budget inverted; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:68 reserve exists only on the axis where collision exists, and none does.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs (s1 vs s4 well heights: 114.11 vs 196.70) and probe-D8.mjs (frames t0 vs t2+40ms).
defects.proposedCure: Reserve the action region's height, or wrap the three seams in the house morph family so the container and its contents move on one spring.

defects.defect: The failure state is silent, unassociated and unlabelled, and speaks a second confirmation grammar next to the pane's existing destructive Dialog.
defects.evidence: probe-D9.json selfCollide.after: `{role:null, ariaLive:null, inputAria:{invalid:null, describedby:null, labelledby:null, id:""}, hasLabelEl:false, msgType:{family:"Fira Code", size:"16.4px", style:"italic"}, buttons:[{text:"Update",h:36},{text:"Cancel",h:36}]}`. The Input's only accessible name is a placeholder that is simultaneously the default value (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:126-130). The sibling delete-all flow uses a real Dialog with tone="destructive" at PalettesPane.vue:102-122. glass-ui 7 ships LabeledField (invalid/errorLive/error slot) and Alert (announce: off|polite|assertive) — both unused.
defects.mechanism: M2 — state bound to nothing; plus PR-06 (one action owner) and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:100 (one glass-ui action set).
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D9.mjs, scenario selfCollide.
defects.proposedCure: LabeledField owns label + invalid + errorLive + the error slot; the overwrite reuses the existing Dialog. One grammar, one owner.

defects.defect: The default palette name the interface proposes deterministically collides with an existing palette, so accepting the interface's own suggestion lands in its own error state.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:126-130 proposes `'Palette ' + (savedPaletteCount + 1)`; :249-259 rejects any existing name case-insensitively. The proposal counts, the rule names. probe-D9.json selfCollide: store ["Palette 2","Palette 3"] (the user deleted "Palette 1") → `proposed: "Palette 3"` → committing with the field blank yields `"Palette 3" already exists. Update Cancel`.
defects.mechanism: M2 — state bound to nothing: two encodings of one fact (D2-25) that disagree the moment a palette is deleted.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D9.mjs, scenario A.
defects.proposedCure: Derive the default from the existing *names*, not from the count — the first `Palette n` not already taken — and delete the redundant `savedPaletteCount` prop (D2-25).

defects.defect: The dashed WatercolorDot silhouette is spent on an action, colliding with the mark the constitution reserved for absence; four meanings and three mutually inconsistent dashed strokes render in one viewport.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 ratifies the dashed ghost for exactly one job — "one static, aria-hidden EmptyPaletteMark: exactly three WatercolorDots plus the established dashes" (absence). CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95 uses it for action, :37 for transient state, :62 for provenance; EmptyPaletteMark uses it for absence ~200px below in the same frame (shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png). Three dashed strokes in one 462px column: well edge 1px oklab(0.216…/0.12) at 1.27:1; add-slot ghost 2px in the live picker colour at 1.00–2.89:1; EmptyPaletteMark crimson and heavier.
defects.mechanism: M1 — specimen asked to be an instrument; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:70 forbids operable ornaments without names.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png — sites 1 and 4 are pixel-identical in language, 230px apart.
defects.proposedCure: Reserve the dashed ghost for absence. The action becomes a named geometric button (D2-01); the being-edited swatch expresses itself through the selection register on its seat, not by mutating into the symbol for 'empty'.

defects.defect: Three type roles collapse onto one rendered size; the identity line takes the wrong family and weight; the error message is typographically louder than the two controls that resolve it.
defects.evidence: probe-D6.json/probe-D9.json, 1440 light: "Current Palette" (:9 `text-small font-display font-semibold`) → Fraunces 600 @ 16.4px; "5 colors" (:20 `text-mono-small`) → Fira Code 400 @ 16.4px; '"Palette 3" already exists.' (:148) → Fira Code italic @ 16.4px; Update/Cancel (:154,:162) → 14.384px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 fixes control/label as text-small, Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold; :76 mono for value/code/provenance; :74 prose for sentences; :78 closes the matrix with exactly one named exception (P019, Picker) which this surface is not.
defects.mechanism: M5 — type-matrix drift.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D6.mjs / probe-D9.mjs; read the label/count/msgType blocks.
defects.proposedCure: Label → text-small (Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold); count → a genuinely smaller mono rung; the collision sentence → text-prose, upright — it is English, not a CSS literal.

defects.defect: The palette-name field renders at 12.18px on mobile — below the 16px iOS Safari focus-zoom threshold — and the component serves two roles with four rendered sizes.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json: desktop 1440 label/count 16.4px, Input 14.384px; mobile 390 label/count 14px, Input 12.179px. iOS Safari zooms the viewport on focus of a text control under 16px, so focusing the name field pushes the well the user was working in out of view. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:33 forbids a desktop-tight/mobile-airy fork and a breakpoint pile; the file carries four `w-11 h-11 sm:w-12 sm:h-12` forks (:36,:62,:64,:100) and no container query.
defects.mechanism: M5 — type-matrix drift, on a fifth independent scaling axis.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs, scenario s5-five-mobile-390 → `input.style.fontSize`.
defects.proposedCure: Pin the control rung at ≥16px on touch, from the matrix, container-scaled rather than breakpoint-forked.

defects.defect: The specimen row has no reflow law, so the position of the primary action is a function of `palette.length mod container width`; it orphans onto its own row at 390px and at the constitution's 400%-zoom arm.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json s5-five-mobile-390: row 298 × 110.34, wrap, gap 10, dots 44 — add-slot at `{x:46.0, y:395.72}`, row two, alone (5×44 + 5×10 + 44 = 314px into a 298px band). probe-D7.json f-zoom400-360-dpr4: rowChildY `[281,281,281,281,281, 341.2]`. Frame: frames-D4/s5-five-mobile-390.png — the CTA sits alone beside ~250px of nothing and reads as a sixth swatch that failed to load.
defects.mechanism: M6 — no reflow law for the specimen row: the primary action lives inside the data it acts on.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs (s5) and probe-D7.mjs (f).
defects.proposedCure: The add action is an action, not a swatch (D2-01). Move it out of the specimen row into the well's action region beside the commit control, where its position is invariant under length, viewport and zoom.

defects.defect: Every swatch wrapper is a block box hosting an inline-block face, so each hangs 7.17px of line-box slack; `items-center` on the row is a no-op and the authored 10px gap renders as 17.17px below the band.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json s2: every `.swatch-row` child `{display:"block", lineHeight:"27.912px", h:55.17}` hosting a 48px face → 7.17px slack per child, row 55.17 for 48px of ink (+14.9%); gap above the row 10.00px, ink-to-row-bottom 17.17px. Mobile 390: lineHeight 24px, child 50.17 for a 44px face (6.17px), row 110.34 for 98px of ink. Because all six children are equal height, `items-center` at :27 changes nothing, and the band's ink centre sits 3.58px above its geometric centre. The wrapper `<div key="__add__">` at :87 reproduces the same slack.
defects.mechanism: M6 — real rendered relation loses to token intent (PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:73).
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs; read `row.children[*].display / lineHeight / rect.h` against `dots[*].rect.h`.
defects.proposedCure: Make the wrappers `display:flex` (or the faces `display:block`). Then row height equals its ink and the authored gap is the gap that renders.

defects.defect: The commit control is nameless, and it is the only reachable control in the component.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:134-142 — `Button variant="outline" icon-only` whose only child is `<Check>`, with no aria-label. probe-D9.json targets: `{name:"<nameless>", w:32, h:40}`. probe-D4.json s2..s12: `buttons[0].accName: ""` in every populated scenario; `tabNames: ["INPUT:","BUTTON:"]`. audit/visual/REPORT.md:97 counts namelessButtons: 1 on /#/palettes in the empty state, before this button mounts. e2e/smoke/flows/palette-save.spec.ts:39-41 documents the omission verbatim and routes around it.
defects.mechanism: M1 — specimen asked to be an instrument: with every face aria-hidden, the component's entire contribution to the accessibility tree is one unnamed field and one unnamed button.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D9.mjs (targets) or probe-D4.mjs (any populated scenario, `buttons[0].accName`).
defects.proposedCure: Give the commit control a real accessible name at the producer call site. A test that codifies a defect is not coverage — retire the e2e workaround with it.

defects.defect: `.btn-interactive` and `.floating-panel` are phantom classes with no rule anywhere in the running CSSOM; an animation was deleted upstream and only its name was left behind in three templates.
defects.evidence: probe-D5.json p2-hover.during, measured against `document.styleSheets` in the live page: `{floatingPanelRuleExists:false, btnInteractiveRuleExists:false}`. `grep -rl "btn-interactive" node_modules/@mkbabb/` → empty; consumers at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:71,75,78,100 and demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:62,69,78,330. docs/precepts/instructions/LESSONS-LEARNED.md:603 records glass-ui `b0debec` retiring `.btn-interactive` "under a false zero-site verdict". CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:68-74 still describes the scale/press/focus legs the class was supposed to carry; the edit-overlay buttons at :75,:78 and the add slot at :100 now have no hover scale, no press magnitude and no `focus-visible` rule at all.
defects.mechanism: M7 — phantom class atoms: a class name used as a positioning and motion strategy.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D5.mjs (P2) — the two booleans are read from the live stylesheet list, not by grep.
defects.proposedCure: Mint the atom where the house puts ≥3-consumer recipes (demo/styles/utils.css, beside `.dashed-well`/`.swatch-row`) or file it back to glass-ui — but do not leave a name where an animation used to be. Owner edict 6.

defects.defect: The swatch TransitionGroup keys embed the array index, so every survivor after a removal is re-keyed and the `vj-enter-move` FLIP class the shared recipe advertises can never fire.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:45-53 keys on `${color}::${i}`. utils.css:167-172 states the intent: "neighbours reflow on the family move class". Deterministic replay (keyproof-D2-16.mjs): initial [red,green,blue,gold] → keys [0,1,2,3]; remove idx1 → [red,blue,gold] → keys [0,4,5] — both survivors are new nodes, so Vue plays three leaves and two enters. Combined with D2-05's containing-block bug, a mid-list removal renders three absolutely-positioned leaves converging on the pane origin plus two scale-from-zero entries.
defects.mechanism: M4 — motion budget inverted: the identity function defeats the transition the recipe was written for.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/keyproof-D2-16.mjs — exact replay of the source. In-browser arm blocked by D2-01 (no removal path exists) except via the whole-list clear, which is confirmed in D2-05.
defects.proposedCure: Key on a colour identity that survives reordering — mint a stable id per swatch when the colour enters the draft and carry it in the model, not in a `color::index` map derived after the fact. Then `.vj-enter-move` does the reflow the recipe promises and only the removed node leaves.

defects.defect: The 'Add current colour' verb has three outcomes behind one control — append, silently reorder the user's palette, or silently do nothing — and two of them have no representation at all.
defects.evidence: useSwatchActions.ts:62-73: `if (existingIdx !== -1 && length > 1) { …reordered.push(css); emit("apply", reordered); return; }` moves an existing swatch to the end; `if (existingIdx !== -1) return;` does nothing. No disabled state, no 'already in this palette' affordance, no announcement — and the control renders as a glyph-less dashed blob (D2-01), so the user cannot tell which case fired. It is also the component's only reordering, and it is accidental: glass-ui 7 ships `sortable-list` and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:131 specifies the keyboard reorder grammar for "palette colors, operands, stops" down to the 'position of total' announcement — none of which exists here.
defects.mechanism: M1 — specimen asked to be an instrument; VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 forbids states that are not explicit.
defects.reproduction: NONE in-browser — the control that would trigger it is inert (D2-01). Code-derived from useSwatchActions.ts:62-73; labelled a hypothesis for the rendered arm only, not for the code path.
defects.proposedCure: One verb, one outcome. Once the CTA is a real seat (D2-01), give it a disabled/'already present' state with a name, and put reordering on the producer `sortable-list` with the ratified keyboard grammar instead of letting it happen as a side effect of Add.

defects.defect: The edit state is a `hidden lg:flex` desktop-only fork that duplicates two verbs already mounted unconditionally in the Dock.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:58 `class="edit-overlay glass-floating hidden lg:flex"` — below 1024px no from→to specimen, no Save, no Cancel. demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:143-144 mounts `aria-label="Save edit"` and `aria-label="Cancel edit"` with no breakpoint gate. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32-33 (one mobile sequence; no breakpoint pile); PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:57 (PR-13) is the same mechanism on Picker — "specimen and action region both host Copy → REMOVE … total 2 → 1". The overlay is also unreachable in practice: its only entry point is the Edit button inside the dead panel (D2-01).
defects.mechanism: M9 — breakpoint fork duplicating a verb the Dock already owns.
defects.reproduction: Read CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:56-84 against demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:143-144; resize below 1024px.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the overlay. The Dock layer is the ratified action region for the edit journey; the swatch expresses state through its seat's selection register, never a second action set.

defects.defect: A five-zone omnibus with no seat in the ratified Library composition, growing to 392px with no cap, scroll or 'show more'.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json zones, populated 1440: identity+count 436×22.94, `.swatch-row` 436×55.17 (→ 250.69 at 24 colours), `.api-offline-chip` role=alert 255.19×22.59, action row 436×40, plus a second action set on collision 436×36. Well height 196.70 → 392.22 at 24 colours (s12). PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:67 allows one identity, one protagonist and at most ONE persistent action/status region. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:45 fixes Library as owner-state selector / library / selected inspector over the four owner states, and :186 makes those states "explicit, non-interchangeable" — a permanently-mounted draft well is an unratified fifth region.
defects.mechanism: M8 — unregistered composition, zone inflation.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs, scenarios s2 and s12-many24-desktop.
defects.proposedCure: The current palette IS the Device Draft owner state. Re-seat it behind the owner-state selector or in the selected inspector — not as a permanent band that outgrows the library owning the route.

defects.defect: Backend status is gated on an unrelated buffer's length, doubled on screen as two identical role=alert nodes, below the text-contrast floor in both schemes, and addressed to maintainers rather than users.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:116 `<ApiOfflineChip v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0">`. probe-D8.json: live regions go from two `alert: dev misconfigured — run npm run dev` rows plus one status, to one alert, at the exact moment of save — committing the palette silently removes an infrastructure alert. probe-D6.json: chip ink rgb(219,36,36) on bg rgb(231,202,195) @ 11px = 3.18:1 light; rgb(235,71,71) on rgb(86,57,50) @ 11px = 2.73:1 dark — both fail the 4.5:1 floor. The second alert is the always-mounted DockStatusLamp, so AT announces the same alert twice (frames-D4/a-orange-1440-dpr1.png shows both).
defects.mechanism: M3 — rendered contrast never measured; PR-08 requires persistent entity status rather than transient truth.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D6.mjs (chip block) and probe-D8.mjs (liveRegionText before/after save).
defects.proposedCure: One status seat. The dock lamp already owns band chrome. The well carries at most a save-scoped consequence — 'saved on this device only' — unconditionally, in the muted register, at the matrix rung, for users rather than maintainers.

defects.defect: Six per-instance overrides on producer roots: two half-apply and one renders literally nothing.
defects.evidence: probe-D7.json saveBtn: `h-8 w-8 rounded-full` at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:137 renders `{w:32, h:40}` — `w-8` won, `h-8` lost to the producer's `min-height:40px`, so `rounded-full` resolves on a vertical stadium; `border-border/50` on the same element measures `borderWidth: "0px"` — a colour set on a border that has no width. probe-D9.json: `h-6 px-2` at :154,:162 renders 36px. The 40px commit control sits beside a 36px field (btn y 475.36 vs input y 477.36), mis-registering 2px top and bottom. The producer's real ring is a box-shadow recipe the consumer class list cannot see.
defects.mechanism: M10 — per-instance override of a producer root.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D7.mjs (saveBtn) and probe-D9.mjs (selfCollide.after.buttons).
defects.proposedCure: No local sizing on producer Buttons. If a 32px circular icon rung does not exist in glass-ui 7, that is a producer ask (a BJ-inbox letter), not a class list that silently half-applies.

defects.defect: The empty invitation reserves a slab instead of content-hugging, and the same header slot swaps a noun identity for an imperative that cannot be obeyed.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json s1-empty-desktop-light: well 462 × 115.11 for one 48×48 mark and a 19-character label — ink 2,304px² of 53,178px² = 4.3%; `.swatch-row` 436 wide with one child. Mobile 390: 324-wide well with the mark alone at the far left. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186 requires a true empty invitation to content-hug its text/action; :29 caps empty secondary content at a narrow tray; PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:48 (PR-04) rules REMOVE for empty companion Cards and nested housing. The label at :11-16 switches between "Current Palette" (identity) and "Start a new palette" (instruction) in the same type at the same rung, and is not a control.
defects.mechanism: M8 — unregistered composition, zone inflation.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs, scenario s1; read frames-D4/s1-empty-desktop-light.png.
defects.proposedCure: Collapse the empty draft to one named action that hugs its own text — 'Start a palette with #e2571f' — or to absence until the first colour exists.

defects.defect: CSS literals and user-supplied palette names enter RTL prose with no bidi isolation.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:154 — "CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance | render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose." Unisolated at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:107-109 (`Add current color ({{ cssColorOpaque }})`), :46,:49,:52,:101 (aria-labels embedding raw `rgb(226 87 31)`), and :148-150 (`"{{ duplicateTarget.name }}" already exists.` — a user string inside quotes inside a sentence). probe-D5.json p4-rtl confirms the container itself mirrors correctly (direction rtl; row children [625,567,509,451,393,335]; commit button to x 237), so only the isolation is missing.
defects.mechanism: M11 — unbounded / unisolated strings.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe-D5.mjs (P4) with `dir="rtl"` on the document element.
defects.proposedCure: Wrap every CSS literal and every user-supplied name in `<bdi>` (or `dir="ltr"` spans) at these four sites.

defects.defect: The palette name is unbounded at its point of origin — no maxlength, no counter, no truncation contract.
defects.evidence: probe-D4.json s11-long-name: `{valueLen:160, maxLength:-1, scrollW:1645, clientW:394}` — 160 characters accepted into a 394px field and written straight to the store, then rendered as the identity line of every PaletteCard.
defects.mechanism: M11 — unbounded / unisolated strings.
defects.reproduction: node probe-D4.mjs, scenario s11-long-name.
defects.proposedCure: Cap the name where it is authored (a `maxlength` on the LabeledField control of D2-07), so downstream identity lines inherit a contract instead of a problem.

defects.defect: One fact is declared as two props that can disagree.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:196-202 declares both `savedPaletteCount: number` and `savedPalettes: Palette[]`; PalettesPane.vue:44-45 passes `pm.savedPalettes.value.length` and `pm.savedPalettes.value` — the same array. `savedPaletteCount` is `savedPalettes.length` by construction and is read at exactly two sites (:130, :250), both of which could read the array. D2-08 is what happens when the derived fact is the wrong one for the rule that consumes it.
defects.mechanism: M2 — state bound to nothing.
defects.reproduction: Read CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:196-202 against PalettesPane.vue:44-45.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `savedPaletteCount`; derive both the count and the default name from `savedPalettes`.

defects.defect: Four operable targets fall below the 44px floor, three of them outside the viewport.
defects.evidence: probe-D9.json targets: `<nameless>` commit 32 × 40 (inViewport true); `Edit color …` 28 × 28, `Copy color …` 28 × 28, `Remove color … from palette` 28 × 28 (all inViewport false). Matches the audit's family count — audit/visual/REPORT.md:34,49 records smallTapTargets 8 on /#/palettes desktop. PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 — "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities."

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface) under demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. The seat was spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; it is declared, not inherited or defaulted.

defects.defect: The "Prune empty" confirmation dialog names a count computed from a ≤50-row client page while the endpoint it authorises deletes EVERY empty user in the corpus. An irreversible, unrecoverable delete is guarded by a false statement about its own scope.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:59 `const res = await listUsers(token, 50); adminUsers.value = res.data;` (res.total discarded) → demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:33 `:total-users="pm.adminUsers.value.length"` → demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue:241 `const emptyCount = computed(() => users.filter(...).length)` → :289-291 `title: \`Prune ${emptyCount.value} empty users?\`` / "This will permanently delete N users … This cannot be undone." → demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:69-71 `POST /admin/users/prune-empty` with NO body → api/src/modules/admin/service/users.ts:232 `const slugs = await users.findEmptyUserSlugs();` (whole collection, no limit/offset) + :243-246 `sessions.deleteByUserSlugs(slugs); users.deleteMany(slugs)`. Then AdminUsersPanel.vue:303-308 prints the SERVER's count back: `Pruned ${count} users`.
defects.mechanism: Discarded wire contract at a module boundary: PaginatedResponse.total (demo/palettes/types.ts:127) is published by the transport and thrown away by the composable, so the component is handed a page under a name (`totalUsers`) that asserts it is a corpus, and computes a destructive action's blast radius from it. The panel is not wrong to render emptyCount; it is wrong to POSSESS it.
defects.reproduction: CONFIRMED by code path — every link quoted above, all files read this pass. End-to-end browser run requires a roster >50 users with ≥1 empty user beyond row 50; this read-only seat cannot seed the API, so I do not claim to have run it. Deterministic recipe: seed 51+ users with the empty ones sorting past row 50; open #/admin/users with an admin token; click Prune empty; compare the dialog's number to `pruned` in the POST /admin/users/prune-empty response. Nothing in the chain is conditional. Compounding: useAdminUsers.ts:191-193 repairs only page 1 after the global delete and issues no refetch.
defects.proposedCure: The roster composable returns a page-aware value object, never a bare array: `type Roster = {state:"unauthenticated"} | {state:"loading"} | {state:"error";message} | {state:"loaded";rows:User[];total:number;offset:number;limit:number}`. Blast-radius numbers then become unrepresentable from client state. Preferred form: prune takes an explicit slug list, so the confirmation names exactly what it will send — which also makes the operation idempotent and gives the audit log per-slug membership instead of a bare count.

defects.defect: Inverted direction of dependency: the state composable imports the SFC and drives it imperatively through defineExpose. The view owns data (userPalettes, expandedUserSlug) that the composable must reach back in to repair.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:14 `import type { AdminUsersPanel } from "./browser/admin";` · :27 `const adminUsersPanelRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof AdminUsersPanel> | null>(null)` · back-channel mutations at :95 `updatePaletteTier`, :117 `removeUserPalette`, :132 and :146 `clearUserPalettes`, plus demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:123 `admin.adminUsersPanelRef.value?.onPruneDone(pruned)`. Target: AdminUsersPanel.vue:389 `defineExpose({ removeUserPalette, updatePaletteTier, clearUserPalettes, onPruneDone, userPalettes })`; the state it mutates is at :236-238.
defects.mechanism: Ownership inversion — data state living in a view, with a composable reaching across the component boundary via template ref + defineExpose to keep it consistent. Five `?.` call sites silently no-op when the panel is unmounted.
defects.reproduction: Structural, proved by measurement: `npx madge --extensions ts,vue --ts-config tsconfig.json --circular demo/palettes` → "✖ Found 4 circular dependencies!", all four of the form `usePalettePorts.ts > useAdminUsers.ts > browser/admin/index.ts > browser/admin/<Panel>.vue`. Runtime behaviour is unaffected (the edge is `import type`, erased by verbatimModuleSyntax) — this is a type-graph and ownership cycle, not a boot-order bug.
defects.proposedCure: Move expandedUserSlug / userPalettes / loadingUserPalettes / pruning / pruneResult into a `useAdminUserPalettes` composable. The component renders and emits; it never owns. defineExpose, adminUsersPanelRef, the AdminPort member that carries it, and the type import all delete together. Enforce with an absence-of-permission rule: a `.ts` never imports a `.vue`, barrel or not.

defects.defect: The paginated wire contract is discarded wholesale at the composable boundary: total, offset and q are all published by the transport and unreachable from the UI. User 51 cannot be reached, server-side search is never used, and the header count is a page length.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/api/admin-users.ts:21-32 `listUsers(token, limit = 20, offset = 0, q?)` → `PaginatedResponse<User>`; demo/palettes/types.ts:125-130 declares `total`. Caller: useAdminUsers.ts:59 `listUsers(token, 50)` — no offset, no q — and :60 takes `.data` only. Client-side substitutes: `filteredAdminUsers` (useAdminUsers.ts:29-33) filters the 50 fetched rows; `onUserSortChange` (:50-52) sorts the same 50. `grep -rln PaginationBar demo` → AdminAuditPanel.vue, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue only — the concept lives in this exact directory and the largest list (391 L vs 120/153/126/152) does not use it.
defects.mechanism: A transport publishes a richer contract than the layer above consumes; the consumer re-implements the dropped capabilities client-side over a truncated page, so search and sort answer questions about a page while presenting as answers about the corpus.
defects.reproduction: Code path, all lines quoted. Directly observable consequence with >50 users: typing any slug that sorts past row 50 into the admin search renders `· roster clear · No users found.` — indistinguishable from the L-12 unauthenticated plate. Not run end-to-end (roster seeding unavailable to this read-only seat).
defects.proposedCure: Fold pagination into the Roster value object of L-19 and render the PaginationBar the cluster already owns; delete the bare `50` literal. The composable owns {offset, limit, q} and sends q to the server, which deletes filteredAdminUsers' client-side filter outright — one fewer home for "which users match".

defects.defect: One bad import edge produces FOUR measured circular dependencies (barrel amplification), and no gate in this repository can see any of them: no import/no-cycle, no madge, and the boundary lint rules are dead.
defects.evidence: `npx madge --extensions ts,vue --ts-config tsconfig.json --circular demo/palettes` → "Processed 127 files (468ms) … ✖ Found 4 circular dependencies!" — cycles 1-4 are usePalettePorts.ts > useAdminUsers.ts > browser/admin/index.ts > {AdminAuditPanel, AdminFlaggedPanel, AdminTagsPanel, AdminUsersPanel}.vue. Gate absence: `node -e "'madge' in {...deps,...devDeps}"` → false; `grep -n "no-cycle\|import/" eslint.config.js` → no output; package.json scripts = build/typecheck/lint/test/test:e2e only. Dead boundary law: `npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue` → `no-restricted-imports: undefined` (same for useAdminUsers.ts), while demo/color-picker/App.vue has the rule but its ban pattern `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue` uses an alias tsconfig.demo.json:33 records as deleted. `ls -d demo/@` → No such file or directory. Coverage: 16 of 250 demo .ts/.vue files nominally, 0 effectively.
defects.mechanism: Barrel amplification — the single offending edge (useAdminUsers.ts:14) targets a BARREL, and three of that barrel's other members inject ADMIN_PORT_KEY and therefore import usePalettePorts. Three correctly-written panels are dragged into a cycle by a sibling's mistake. A barrel converts one bad edge into N.
defects.reproduction: The madge invocation above, run this pass, output pasted verbatim. `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` both pass on the same tree — module cycles are legal TypeScript and no lint rule expresses the constraint.
defects.proposedCure: Two absences, both of which would have failed this at the introducing commit: (1) one eslint object over demo/**/*.ts banning imports of **/*.vue and component barrels — "a .ts never imports a .vue"; (2) `madge --circular --extensions ts,vue` wired into `npm run lint`. This is the finding that should order the mega-tranche: fixing L-1 without L-24 fixes one instance of a class the repo cannot keep fixed.

defects.defect: The admin console is homed inside the community-browse feature, and its own composition root lives outside the feature its children are inside. The browse seam publishes five admin panels as part of the browse public API.
defects.evidence: Layout: demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue (the root) is a SIBLING of demo/palettes/browser/, while its five panels + AdminListItem + AdminListSkeleton + PaginationBar live in demo/palettes/browser/admin/. AdminPane.vue:79-85 imports its own body from `"../browser/admin"`. demo/palettes/browser/index.ts — header: "the palette-browser mega-feature's TOP-LEVEL SEAM … the stable public API of the palette-browser feature" — lines 28-34 re-export AdminUsersPanel, AdminNamesPanel, AdminAuditPanel, AdminFlaggedPanel, AdminTagsPanel. The only genuine cross edge runs the OTHER way: AdminUsersPanel.vue:201 `import { PaletteCard } from "../card"`.
defects.mechanism: Inverted containment: the tree was arranged to satisfy one leaf import (PaletteCard) rather than the concept boundary. An audit log, a tag taxonomy and account lifecycle have no relationship to browsing community palettes.
defects.reproduction: Structural, verifiable by `ls demo/palettes/admin demo/palettes/browser/admin` and reading browser/index.ts:28-34. Consequence measured: it is the layout that makes useAdminUsers.ts:14's reach into `./browser/admin` read as plausible — re-homing makes that edge obviously absurd, which is what makes the L-1 cure self-enforcing. Note: r3's greenfield lattice leaves the subject at this path — the one place the prior pass accepted the tree's premise.
defects.proposedCure: demo/palettes/admin/ becomes the console's whole home — pane, five panels, AdminListItem, AdminListSkeleton, PaginationBar, plus an index.ts seam. browser/index.ts loses its admin block and returns to being the browse feature. The single real edge (PaletteCard) becomes an explicit, minimal cross-feature reach through browser/card — one named import at one call site, which is exactly what a barrel seam is for.

defects.defect: One cluster runs two opposite wiring conventions; the subject uses all three channels simultaneously (6 props + 7 emits + 2 injects + defineExpose). r3's proposed cure adopts the MINORITY convention and would split the cluster further.
defects.evidence: Measured over the five sibling panels via `grep -c defineProps` / `grep -n "inject("` / `grep -n defineExpose`: AdminAuditPanel 0 props, injects ADMIN_PORT_KEY @:107 · AdminFlaggedPanel 0 props, inject @:149 · AdminTagsPanel 0 props, inject @:122 · AdminNamesPanel 1 defineProps, no inject · AdminUsersPanel 1 defineProps (6 props, :212-220) + inject SAFE_ACCENT_KEY :232 + inject ADMIN_PORT_KEY :234 + defineExpose (5 members) :389. AdminPane.vue renders three children BARE (:61, :64, :67) and the subject with 6 props / 7 emits (:25-41), of which 5 props are pure pm.* reads of a port the child already injects at :234.
defects.mechanism: No single owner of the wiring direction. The pane is simultaneously an adapter (for two children) and a passthrough (for three), so neither convention can be enforced and the subject accreted all of them.
defects.reproduction: The grep table above, run this pass. r3's lattice specifies the subject as a "pure view — zero inject" fed by props, which would yield 3 inject-only / 2 props-only across five sibling panels — the current inconsistency with the ratio changed.
defects.proposedCure: Adopt the MAJORITY: all five panels inject one narrow console port; AdminPane renders them all bare and owns only the sub-view switch and header. The subject then keeps inject and loses all 6 props, all 7 emits and the defineExpose — strictly more deletion than r3's cure, and it converges the cluster. Safe only once L-3's 34-member god-port is split: `AdminUsersPort = { roster, loadRoster, loadUserPalettes, deleteUser, deleteUserPalettes, pruneEmpty }`.

defects.defect: The unauthenticated state costumes as an empty roster. The structural root is port membership: AdminPort has no isAdminAuthenticated — the admin console's own port cannot see admin auth.
defects.evidence: Live probe (Playwright, read-only, http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users): `{adminToken: null}`, body text `"Users 0 … 0 users Prune empty Refresh · ROSTER CLEAR · No users found."`. Code: demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts:55-56 `const token = getAdminToken(); if (!token) return;` — returns before touching loadingUsers OR usersLoadError, so AdminUsersPanel.vue takes :63 (the empty plate) rather than :51 (the error plate). Port membership: isAdminAuthenticated appears in usePalettePorts.ts at :128 (sessionPort) and :184 (browsePort); adminPort spans :194-231 and does not contain it. Falsifies the file's own annotation at :49-50: "the P0 case: error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as an empty roster." Corroborated in WebKit by all four visual captures (shots/*/admin-users.png, read this pass).
defects.mechanism: Wrong port membership — a capability the admin console needs is provided to two other ports and withheld from its own, so the console has no channel to distinguish "not authorized" from "empty". Compounded by per-method precondition guards instead of one boundary gate.
defects.reproduction: Reproduced live this pass: navigate to http://localhost:9000/#/admin/users with no admin token; localStorage['palette-admin-token'] is null; the panel renders the roster-clear empty plate with a live-looking Prune/Refresh toolbar.
defects.proposedCure: Gate the precondition ONCE at the route boundary (auth:"admin" on the five admin views in demo/shell/viewSchema.ts + an AdminGate.vue that renders the unauthenticated plate or its slot), and make the roster composable return the discriminated Roster of L-19 whose "unauthenticated" arm is a distinct renderable state. The per-method `if (!token) return` guards then delete.

defects.defect: Two live routes to the same design system inside one file: Button/Badge through demo/ui/* alias barrels, Dialog through the published @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog subpath — while demo/ui/dialog exports the identical eight symbols.
defects.evidence: AdminUsersPanel.vue:188 `import { Button } from "../../../ui/button"` → demo/ui/button/index.ts is one line: `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. :189 badge, same shape. :190-197 `from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog"`. demo/ui/dialog/index.ts exports Dialog, DialogClose, DialogTrigger, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogContent, DialogFooter — the same eight. All 19 demo/ui/* barrels are pure one-line re-exports (pasted this pass). Route split measured: 90 imports through the alias barrels vs 37 direct to the glass-ui root plus ~70 to its subpaths. glass-ui publishes ./button, ./badge, ./dialog as first-class subpaths; the shims reach the root barrel instead.
defects.mechanism: A migration-era alias layer that survived its migration. Edict 2 (no aliases, no dual paths) and edict 4 (glass-ui is the design system, not demo/ui/) — the layer adds zero value and forfeits the per-component subpath splitting glass-ui publishes 74 export entries to provide.
defects.reproduction: Read the two barrels and the import block; both routes are live in AdminUsersPanel.vue simultaneously (lines 188-189 vs 190-197).
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ (19 files leave the lattice) and import @mkbabb/glass-ui/<subpath> everywhere. One specifier per external package. This also makes glass-ui prop drift (r3's L-4: 51 dead `variant` props across 22 files) visible at the import site instead of hidden behind a local barrel.

defects.defect: ConfirmDialog left glass-ui at the 7.0.0 adoption and the demo re-grew it in two places instead of relaying it back upstream.
defects.evidence: `git show f2c8f565^:demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue | grep -n ConfirmDialog` → `:158 <ConfirmDialog`, `:186 import { ConfirmDialog } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/confirm-dialog"`. glass-ui 7.0.0's exports map has ./dialog and no confirm entry; dist/components/dialog/ contains eight Dialog* files and no Confirm*. Post-fold, two hand-composed re-growths carrying the IDENTICAL comment "(Glass 7: ConfirmDialog folded onto the Dialog family)": AdminUsersPanel.vue:157-181 template + :254-286 controller (7 refs + showConfirm + onConfirm), and PalettesPane.vue:101-121 with its open-state at usePaletteActions.ts:25. Cost here: 372 → 391 lines (+19).
defects.mechanism: A design-system primitive was removed upstream with no replacement composition, and each consumer independently reconstructed it — the same family as the ActionBarLayer/useLayerTransition suspect named in the brief.
defects.reproduction: The git show commands above, run this pass; both re-growths readable in the working tree.
defects.proposedCure: Relay to the glass-ui BH inbox (standing relay edict): request a Dialog-family confirm composition or `useConfirm()` from @mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog — /dialog already ships dialogStageContext, the natural home. Until then, ONE demo-side owner in demo/shared/ui/, not two copies.

defects.defect: The admin row chassis exists five times across the cluster, and only the single unused owner carries the documented mobile fix.
defects.evidence: `grep -n "flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5\|rounded-md border border-card-edge" demo/palettes/browser/admin/*.vue` → AdminListItem.vue:11 (the owner, with `min-w-0`), AdminListSkeleton.vue:9, AdminAuditPanel.vue:62, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:47+50, AdminUsersPanel.vue:68+80. The subject's action column at :106 (`flex items-center gap-1.5 shrink-0`) is character-identical to AdminListItem.vue:20. `grep -rln AdminListItem demo` → AdminNamesPanel.vue (the only importer) and AdminListSkeleton.vue, where the reference is a COMMENT (:4-6, "shaped as the AdminListItem row grammar"). AdminListItem.vue:6-10 documents `min-w-0` as the S.W5-12/F-1 fix for the ~850px track blowout at 390 — absent from all four copies.
defects.mechanism: An atom is being transcribed rather than imported, so a fix applied to the owner never reaches the four copies. The subject renders AdminListSkeleton (a copy) while loading and its own inline copy when loaded — the loading shape and the loaded shape come from two different modules.
defects.reproduction: The grep above, run this pass. HYPOTHESIS (labelled): whether the four copies actually overflow at 390 is unproven — the visual matrix reports overflowX 0 on all four /#/admin/users rows (REPORT.md:128,143,158,173), but every capture is of the EMPTY roster (all four screenshots read this pass), so a populated row was never measured on a phone.
defects.proposedCure: AdminListItem gains an `interactive` variant (role=button, tabindex, aria-expanded, focus ring) and becomes the single row atom; AdminListSkeleton is built FROM AdminListItem with Skeleton slots, so loading and loaded shapes match by construction rather than by comment. The subject's :68-132 collapses to `<AdminListItem interactive>` with three slots.

defects.defect: A 34-member god-port is injected to call exactly one method; three of its members are entire nested composable returns.
defects.evidence: `awk 'NR>=194 && NR<=231' demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts | grep -cE "^\s+[a-zA-Z]+[:,]"` → 34. Members audit / flagged / tags are whole sub-composable returns (useAdminAudit.ts:87-102 alone returns 14), so the reachable surface is ~70+. AdminUsersPanel.vue:234 injects it and uses one member: `pm.loadUserPalettes(slug)` at :361. browsePort measures 32 by the same command. The module's own header (usePalettePorts.ts:21-30) claims RF-15 dissolved 'the old usePaletteManager god facade … into FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports'.
defects.mechanism: The god facade was renamed, not dissolved — one 153-line blob became two 30+-member objects with nested facades inside them. The port boundary carries no information about what any consumer actually needs.
defects.reproduction: The awk/grep counts above, run this pass, against the single use site at :361.
defects.proposedCure: Split by consumer, not by feature area: AdminUsersPort = { roster, loadRoster, loadUserPalettes, deleteUser, deleteUserPalettes, pruneEmpty } — 6 members. The colour-name queue, audit, flagged and tags each get their own port injected by their own panel. Injection keys move to a leaf demo/palettes/keys.ts (the precedent is already in the tree and this very file consumes it correctly at :187).

defects.defect: The demo's three module-boundary lint rules match zero files in the palettes tree, while a barrel in that tree asserts they are enforced standing.
defects.evidence: `npx eslint --print-config demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminUsersPanel.vue` → `no-restricted-imports: undefined`; same for demo/palettes/useAdminUsers.ts. The rule is live only for demo/color-picker/App.vue, where its ban pattern is `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue` — an alias tsconfig.demo.json:33 records as deleted ("No `@styles`/`@components`/…"), and `grep -rn "@components/" demo` returns ONE hit, inside a comment (browser/status/index.ts:5). defects.reproduction: The --print-config invocations above, run this pass; `npx eslint` on the subject, useAdminUsers.ts and usePalettePorts.ts returns clean despite the L-1 boundary crossing.
defects.proposedCure: Re-aim the globs at the live tree (demo/palettes/**, demo/shell/**, demo/workbenches/**, demo/scenes/**), express the ban in the post-W43 relative-path vocabulary, and add the one law L-1 needs: `demo/**/*.ts` may not import `**/*.vue`. Add the missing demo/shared/ui/index.ts seam so the subject's :202 raw .vue reach becomes a barrel reach. Delete the claim from browser/index.ts if the rule is not restored.
