defects.defect: The palette feature's five injection keys are colocated with a 275-line provider that value-imports 16 composables, so importing a CONTRACT drags its entire IMPLEMENTATION cone. This directly amends prior finding L-7's cure, which instructs this component to inject LIBRARY_PORT_KEY / COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts is 275 lines; :271-275 declare SESSION_PORT_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, BROWSE_PORT_KEY, ADMIN_PORT_KEY, COLOR_TARGET_PORT_KEY in the same module as providePalettePorts, which value-imports 16 composables (usePaletteStore, useBrowsePalettes, useAdminUsers, useAdminAudit, useAdminFlagged, useAdminTags, useVersionHistory, useTagEdit, useSlugMigration, useColorNameQueue, usePaletteActions, useFilteredList + 3 auth). Measured transitive relative-import walk, value (non-type-only) edges only: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts → 26 modules / 2,971 LoC; demo/color-session/keys.ts → 1 module / 27 LoC. (Full graph incl. type-only edges: 92/9,482 vs 18/2,035 — keys.ts's cone is entirely type-only and erases at build.) Five shell/dock modules already pay the bill for one Symbol: Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14.
defects.mechanism: An injection key is a contract; a provider is an implementation. Colocating them makes every consumer of the contract depend on the whole implementation cone. The repo already contains the correct idiom and this very component already uses it — demo/color-session/keys.ts is keys-and-types only (every import an `import type`), and CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:173 + useSwatchActions.ts:4 each reach it for 27 lines. The palettes feature does the opposite of its sibling.
defects.reproduction: wc -l demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts → 275; sed -n '1,19p' shows 16 value imports + one `import type { ViewId }`; python transitive walk (value edges only) → 26 modules / 2971 LoC vs 1 / 27 for demo/color-session/keys.ts; grep -rn 'palettes/usePalettePorts' demo/shell → 5 files importing SESSION_PORT_KEY.
defects.proposedCure: Split demo/palettes/ports.ts (the five InjectionKey symbols + the port interfaces, `import type` only, ~60 lines) from demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts (the provider). Consumers import the former; only the app root imports the latter. Mechanical file split, zero behaviour delta, identical in shape to demo/color-session/keys.ts — and it makes prior L-7's cure (inject instead of prop-drill 4 props / 8 emits) free rather than expensive.

defects.defect: `TooltipProvider` — a scope primitive that belongs once at the app root — is mounted per call-site, four times, with three different delay values and none at the root.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "<TooltipProvider" demo --include='*.vue'` → 4: demo/scenes/about/ColorNutritionLabel.vue:97 (delay-duration="100"), demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:23 ("300"), demo/shell/dock/ColorInput.vue:30 ("200"), demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:88 ("200"). `grep -rn "TooltipProvider" demo/color-picker/App.vue demo/shell/*.vue` → no output (zero at app root). In this component the provider is opened INSIDE the TransitionGroup, wrapping a single trigger.
defects.mechanism: reka-ui's TooltipProvider shares open/close and skip-delay state across the tooltips beneath it; four isolated providers means that grouping never spans them (moving between tooltips in different providers re-incurs the full delay). More structurally, 'how long before a tooltip appears' is a house motion decision that has become a per-instance magic number — edict 5 (style at the root component level, never per-instance overrides) applied to timing.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "<TooltipProvider" demo --include='*.vue' (4 hits, 3 distinct delay-duration values); grep -rn "TooltipProvider" demo/color-picker/App.vue demo/shell/*.vue (no root provider).
defects.proposedCure: One <TooltipProvider> at the app root with the house delay expressed as a token; delete the four local providers. If a surface genuinely needs a different delay, that is a NAMED register in glass-ui, not a magic number at a call site.

defects.defect: demo/palettes and demo/shell are mutually dependent: the palette feature's port CONTRACT is parameterised by the shell's view vocabulary, while five shell/dock modules import the feature's session port. Neither tree can be lifted, tested or reasoned about alone.
defects.evidence: Feature→shell: demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:19 `import type { ViewId } from "../shell/useViewManager";` — and PalettePortsDeps (:33-41) declares `currentView: Ref<ViewId>` and `switchView: (id: ViewId) => void`. Shell→feature: demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:70,71,76 (lazy panes — legitimate composition) plus demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:18, DockViewSelect.vue:8, layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:5, menus/MobileMenuDropdown.vue:13, menus/ProfileSection.vue:14 all importing SESSION_PORT_KEY.
defects.mechanism: The shell→feature edge is legitimate composition (a router mounts panes; a dock reads a session port). The feature→shell edge is not: the palette feature cannot state its own port contract without naming the shell's routes. The type-only import erases at runtime so this is not a load-time cycle, but it is a genuine cycle in the dependency lattice.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'shell/' demo/palettes --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → 1 hit (usePalettePorts.ts:19). grep -rn 'palettes/' demo/shell --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → 8 hits, 5 of them SESSION_PORT_KEY.
defects.proposedCure: Invert the edge: the ports declare a FEATURE-owned vocabulary — `onNavigate: (intent: "library" | "browse") => void` — and the app root (which already owns both trees) adapts intents to ViewId. The feature stops knowing the shell exists; the shell keeps knowing the feature does. One direction, which is the point of a lattice.

defects.defect: `EditTarget.paletteId: string` flattens two disjoint kinds — the in-memory draft buffer and a saved palette's local store key — into one string, discriminated by a `"__current__"` sentinel living in a third file, in a namespace shared by construction with `__extracted__`-prefixed temp ids.
defects.evidence: demo/color-session/color-model.ts:19-23 `export interface EditTarget { paletteId: string; colorIndex: number; originalCss: string; }`. demo/palettes/constants.ts:9 `export const CURRENT_PALETTE_ID = "__current__";`. Two consumers branch on it: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useSwatchActions.ts:26 `et.paletteId === CURRENT_PALETTE_ID && et.colorIndex === index` and demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:100 `if (paletteId === CURRENT_PALETTE_ID) { …write the draft buffer… }`. demo/palettes/types.ts:15-27 documents Palette.id as `crypto.randomUUID()` OR a `gen-`/`mix-`/`__extracted__` temp prefix — the same underscore-sentinel shape, one namespace.
defects.mechanism: A domain distinction with no type — the same disease as prior L-16 one level up. Nothing prevents a future temp prefix from colliding and nothing tells a new consumer the branch exists; constants.ts's doc comment is the only record and it is in neither consumer's file.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn "CURRENT_PALETTE_ID|__current__" demo src test e2e → 6 sites, 2 of them branching predicates in different modules; read demo/color-session/color-model.ts:19-23 for the flattened type.
defects.proposedCure: `type EditTarget = { kind: "draft"; colorIndex: number; originalCss: string } | { kind: "saved"; paletteId: string; colorIndex: number; originalCss: string }`. The sentinel and demo/palettes/constants.ts both delete themselves and both branches become exhaustive rather than remembered.

It is an internal inconsistency, not a missing feature: Mix bounds a rack whose limit is taste; the palette editor does not bound one whose limit is contract.

result.strongestDefect: L5-1 — `usePalettePorts.ts` claims (lines 22-31) to have dissolved a god facade into "FIVE narrow, feature-owned ports" where "no consumer injects a member outside the port it named". It in fact creates ONE `searchQuery` ref (`:54`) and aliases it into three ports (`:141`, `:183`, `:224`) and three sub-composables (`:65,68,69`) plus `useFilteredList` (`:112`). Route `#/browse` renders BrowsePane and PalettesPane side by side, so the two visible search fields are one cell: typing "zzq-probe" into "Search the commons..." puts "zzq-probe" into "Search your palettes..." — confirmed live, both directions, plus direct runtime `===` identity across the provide chain with a negative control. The invariant in the banner is satisfied textually and violated referentially, which is exactly how a renamed god module passes its own review.
result.negativeProof: N/A — verdict is DEFECTIVE. However, two sub-axes came back SOUND with positive proof and are recorded in the report so the cures for other findings do not disturb them: (1) the demo→library public-surface discipline is clean — `grep -rn 'from "\.\./\.\./src/…' demo/` returns empty (no demo file reaches `src/`), and every value.js specifier written in demo/ (`color, css, easing, math, quantize`) is a proper subset of `package.json#exports`; the single bare `@mkbabb/value.js` occurrence is prose in a comment at `demo/shared/utils.ts:12`. `vite.config.ts:37-50` generates the self-alias set FROM the exports map with anchored `^…$` regexes, so a specifier the demo can write is one a real npm consumer can write — BrowsePane's proof of the public API is honest. (2) The palette-browser barrel seam is respected in fact: grep for raw `.vue` reaches into `browser/` from outside returns empty and `npx eslint demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue` exits clean — though the guard meant to enforce it is inert (deferred to pass-1 L-4).

defects.defect: The five injected "narrow ports" hand out ONE shared mutable `searchQuery` ref. Three ports (browse, library, admin) expose the same object; five corpora (remote wall client filter, remote wall SERVER query, the user's localStorage-backed saved palettes, the admin user table, the colour-name moderation queue) are driven by one cell. Route #/browse renders both consuming panes simultaneously, so the two visible search fields are one text box.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:54 `const searchQuery = ref("")`; aliased at :65,:68,:69,:112,:141,:183,:224. Banner claiming the opposite at :22-31. PROOF 1 (runtime identity, probe-L5/port-identity-output.json): {"searchQuery_browse_is_library": true, "searchQuery_browse_is_admin": true, "control_remotePalettes_vs_savedPalettes": false} — the false control proves the probe discriminates. PROOF 2 (live typing): `AFTER typing 'zzq-probe' into COMMONS field: commons.value= "zzq-probe"  mine.value = "zzq-probe"  SHARED-REF DEFECT: true`. Frame: probe-L5/L5-shared-searchquery.png shows the string legible in both fields. Reverse direction confirmed: probe-local-search-network.mjs types only into the local field, reports `commons field now reads: "sunset"`.
defects.mechanism: A port that publishes a shared mutable primitive is not a port — it is the god blob with five names. "Search" is not one concept; it is five queries against five corpora. The claimed invariant is satisfied textually and violated referentially, which is invisible in an import graph and only observable in runtime object identity.
defects.reproduction: `node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-L5/probe-shared-search.mjs` against the dev server on :9000. Also `node .../probe-L5/probe-port-identity.mjs`. Both confirmed. NOTE the network half of the blast radius (local search firing a commons refetch via useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-60) is a LABELLED HYPOTHESIS on this host: probe-local-search-network.mjs measured 0 palette calls because the dev page sits in the designed `misconfigured` latch, which availability.ts:49-50 documents as short-circuiting "(no request was issued)".
defects.proposedCure: Delete `searchQuery` from `providePalettePorts` entirely. Each corpus mints and owns its query: useBrowsePalettes owns `query`; useFilteredList(savedPalettes, query, …) takes a library-owned one; useAdminUsers and useColorNameQueue likewise. Each port exposes its own `query: Ref<string>`. `searchPlaceholder` and its `switch` (:104-110) die with it — the placeholder is already a prop each pane passes (BrowsePane.vue:13, PalettesPane.vue:37). Net −1 shared cell, −1 computed, −1 switch, −5 aliases; five independent queries; the banner's invariant becomes true.

defects.defect: Three ports share one `expandedId` ref (and one `toggleExpand`), read against two deliberately disjoint keyspaces: BrowsePane keys by remote `slug`, PalettesPane keys the same object by the client-minted local UUID `id`. Both walls render together on #/browse, so a single-valued "which card is open" register is contested by two exclusive readers.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:144-145 (library), :177-178 (browse), :226-227 (admin) — all three are the same `actions.*`. BrowsePane.vue:97 `pm.expandedId.value === palette.slug` / :102 `pm.toggleExpand(palette.slug)` vs PalettesPane.vue:88 `=== palette.id` / :90 `toggleExpand(palette.id)`. types.ts:14-27 (K-PALID id-honesty) establishes the domains cannot intersect: a remote palette has NO `id`; `id` is `crypto.randomUUID()` present iff `isLocal`. Runtime identity: probe-L5/port-identity-output.json {"expandedId_browse_is_library": true, "expandedId_browse_is_admin": true, "toggleExpand_browse_is_library": true}.
defects.mechanism: A per-wall UI register hoisted into shared state because it sat next to the other palette actions in usePaletteActions, not because the concept is shared. One ref, two exclusive key domains, two simultaneously-rendered readers.
defects.reproduction: Reference identity CONFIRMED via probe-L5/probe-port-identity.mjs. The user-visible collapse (expanding a commons card closing an open My Palettes card) is a LABELLED HYPOTHESIS — sound by construction but not yet observed, because the commons wall cannot populate on a loopback host under the misconfigured latch. Observing it needs VITE_API_URL pointed at a reachable commons plus >=1 saved local palette.
defects.proposedCure: `expandedId` belongs to `PaletteCardGrid` — the component that IS a wall. Give the grid a `shallowRef<string|null>` exposed as `v-model:expanded` (or via slot props). Delete it from usePaletteActions and from all three ports. Two walls, two registers, zero coordination, and the slug-vs-id question stops being a global concern.

defects.defect: The `cardRefs` registry never prunes, retaining a live ComponentPublicInstance for every slug ever rendered. Extends pass-1 L-12, which asserted the leak but did not prove the mechanism — and the obvious reading ("Vue nulls the ref on unmount, so the entry clears") is wrong in a way easy to miss on review.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:209 `const cardRefs = reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; :94 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)"`. Vue DOES notify on unmount — node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 in `setRef`: `const value = isUnmount ? null : refValue;` — and the `el &&` guard short-circuits on exactly that call, so the notification is received and DISCARDED. Growth drivers: useBrowsePalettes.ts:63+ replaces the row set wholesale on every sort/tier/tag change; BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 at :18 appends 50 per page. Duplicated apparatus at PalettesPane.vue:169,88,178-181.
defects.mechanism: Inverted data flow plus a discarded lifecycle signal. Verdict state ("Saved!", "Deleted", a fork error) is data that flows down, but is modelled as a sideways imperative method call (PaletteCard.vue:244 `defineExpose({ showFeedback })`), which is why the pane must hand-roll an instance registry at all — and the registry's cleanup path is silently swallowed by its own null guard.
defects.reproduction: Static mechanism, CONFIRMED from Vue's shipped source at runtime-core.cjs.js:1763 read against BrowsePane.vue:94. Deterministic: any unmount of a PaletteCard leaves its cardRefs entry in place.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `cardRefs`, `defineExpose` (PaletteCard.vue:244) and both panes' registries. One `feedback?: { message: string; variant: "success" | "error" } | null` prop on PaletteCard, driven by a single `shallowRef<{slug,message,variant}|null>` on the wall — shallowRef being the correct primitive per edict 7. Self-pruning, declarative, and the "feedback" concept lands inside PaletteCard's own contract instead of two panes' bookkeeping.

defects.defect: `request<T>` is a generic type ASSERTION, not a decoder — `res.json()` widened to `Promise<T>` with zero runtime checking — so every function in demo/palettes/api/ (8 modules) claims a shape it never verifies. This is the root cause of pass-1 L-16's masking `Object.values` shim in BrowsePane, and it means pass-4 N-10's types-only cure cannot close the boundary.
defects.evidence: Chain: demo/platform/transport/client.ts:101,130 `export async function request<T>(path, init?): Promise<T> { … return res.json(); }` → demo/palettes/api/colors.ts:14 `export function getTags(): Promise<Tag[]> { return request("/colors/tags"); }` → demo/palettes/useTagEdit.ts:31,42 `const allTags = ref<Tag[]>([])` / `allTags.value = await getTags()` → BrowsePane.vue:215-220 `Array.isArray(tags) ? tags : Object.values(tags)` with an 8-line apology at :210-214 describing a RUNTIME payload shape no type can forbid. Pass-4 N-10 § Cure explicitly reasons "it is types only, so it costs nothing at runtime" — a `.d.ts` erases, so the shim would survive it. The api tree already ships the authority: zod schemas at api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:89-91 and siblings.
defects.mechanism: A wire boundary policed by assertion rather than validation. Ownership (which pass 4 correctly identified) is necessary but not sufficient: naming the same shape on both sides does not make the wire carry it. The shim is therefore structurally required at the leaf, which is why pass 1 could only rank it INFO — at the leaf it looks like defensive noise; at the seam it is a hole with ~40 call sites.
defects.reproduction: Static trace, CONFIRMED end to end at the four cited file:line sites. The observable symptom is the repeated Vue "Expected Array, got Object" prop warning that BrowsePane.vue:210-214 was written to suppress.
defects.proposedCure: Ownership from N-10 PLUS validation at the boundary: `request<T>(path, decode: (u: unknown) => T, init?)`. `getTags` becomes `request("/colors/tags", decodeTags)`. Derive the decoders from the same zod schemas that already validate inbound requests in api/, making the contract single-homed in the strong sense (one definition, two directions) rather than the weak one (one type, asserted twice). `availableTags` collapses to `pm.tagEdit.allTags`; the shim and its apology both die; a wire-shape change becomes a loud typed error at the seam instead of a prop warning at a leaf.

defects.defect: Structural synthesis, not a separate site: L5-1, L5-2 and pass-1 L-10 are one fault — every "port" publishes WRITABLE state, so no owner can hold any invariant. Pass 4 diagnosed the coarse version (whole sub-composables smuggled across, its L-7); this is the fine version, and it is what makes the coarse one look harmless.
defects.evidence: searchQuery — raw Ref<string> written by 3 panes + 3 composables (usePalettePorts.ts:141,183,224). expandedId — raw Ref<string|null> written by 2 panes across 2 keyspaces (:144,177,226). remotePalettes — raw Ref<Palette[]> with 9 hand-rolled slug-index mutations across 6 modules (pass-1 L-10), two of them inside the view itself at BrowsePane.vue:281-283 and :314-318. Port surface published raw at usePalettePorts.ts:158.
defects.mechanism: A property bag over assignable cells cannot enforce anything: not "the query belongs to this corpus", not "one card is open per wall", not "the row set is consistent with the cursor". A view assigning `pm.remotePalettes.value[idx] = …` is the view mutating the store's internals — the wrong direction of dependency, made representable by the port shape itself.
defects.reproduction: Composite of the CONFIRMED reproductions for L5-1 (runtime identity + live typing) and L5-2 (runtime identity), plus pass-1 L-10's census. Not an independent site.
defects.proposedCure: One rule dissolves all three: ports expose `Readonly<Ref<T>>` plus named commands, never a writable cell. `browsePort` becomes `{ rows: Readonly<Ref<Palette[]>>, query: Ref<string> /* its own */, setColorTarget(), setSort(), setTier(), setTags(), loadMore(), upsertBySlug(), patchBySlug() }`. All nine index-splices collapse into upsertBySlug and the compiler enforces it rather than a comment. Lift probe-L5/probe-port-identity.mjs into the suite as a standing test asserting no two port objects share a ref identity.

defects.defect: The OKLab colour-distance predicate is computed with `Math.hypot` on the client and `Math.sqrt(dL*dL+da*da+db*db)` on the server — two different functions for one concept, with the radius constant 0.15 hard-coded on both sides.
defects.evidence: BrowsePane.vue:343,347 `const radius = 0.15` / `Math.hypot(c.L - L, c.a - a, c.b - b) <= radius` vs api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:167,176-178 `const radius = query.colorRadius ?? 0.15` / `Math.sqrt(dL*dL + da*da + db*db) <= radius`. Measured over 3e6 random OKLab deltas in [-0.2,0.2]^3: `hypot !== sqrt: 1122317 of 3000000 (37.4%); max |delta| = 1.11e-16; radius-0.15 predicate DISAGREEMENTS: 0`.
defects.mechanism: Fingerprint of the two-home problem already filed as pass-1 L-8 / pass-4 N-13 — the same concept implemented twice from scratch rather than once and shared.
defects.reproduction: `node -e` Monte Carlo, 3e6 samples, output pasted above. Numerically real, behaviourally inert today.
defects.proposedCure: Not a defect to fix on its own — it dissolves when pass-1 L-8's cure lands (one deltaE-OK home, the pane passing colorL/A/B/Radius through the seam that already exists at demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-29,50-52). Recorded because the server exposes a tunable colorRadius the client hard-codes: the day one is tuned they diverge for real.

defects.defect: The Safari visual matrix captured only the designed `misconfigured` error state of this route in all four matrices, so the component's success surface is entirely uncaptured and four open reproductions across the audit cannot be closed from it.
defects.evidence: audit/visual/shots/{safari-desktop,safari-mobile}-{light,dark}/browse.png all show "The commons is unreachable. / Failed to load palettes". Per-capture rows REPORT.md:121,136,151,166 read text=280 desktop / 124 mobile, overflowX=0, pageErr=0, consoleErr=0, smallTapTargets=4 — but they describe an error card, not the wall. Cause is environmental and by design: availability.ts:29-36 (loopback origin + unset VITE_API_URL -> loud `misconfigured` state) and client.ts:36-43; the "DEV MISCONFIGURED — RUN `npm run dev`" chip is visible in probe-L5/L5-shared-searchquery.png. `curl localhost:9000/colors/palettes?limit=2` returns index.html (no proxy).
defects.mechanism: Evidence gap, not a component defect. The capture harness ran against a host in the designed misconfiguration state, so every state gated behind a populated wall went unobserved.
defects.reproduction: Read the four PNGs and the four REPORT rows; confirm the latch via availability.ts:49-50 which documents that no request is issued.
defects.proposedCure: Re-run the visual matrix with VITE_API_URL set to a reachable commons. That single change closes four open reproductions at once: the skeleton->content vj-morph, the load-more affordance, pass-1 L-8's filter/hasMore contradiction, and this pass's L5-2 collapse. Until then no conclusion about the wall may be drawn from browse.png.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (BrowsePane.vue)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — claude-opus-5[1m], declared at the seat, not inherited
result.strongestDefect: D4-01 — the Browse wall's primary interaction (expand a palette) is a state machine with no state and no seat: clicking a card grows it 100→211 px (1440) / 125→228 px (iPhone 14) while the element reports aria-expanded: null, aria-pressed: null, tabIndex: -1 on BOTH Chromium and WebKit. Prior passes proved the card is unreachable by keyboard; this proves that even a successful pointer expansion produces no machine-readable state at all, so adding tabindex="0" closes the prior finding and leaves this one fully open. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 mandates a native <button aria-pressed> seat AND forbids in-card expansion; both halves fail.

defects.defect: The expand affordance is a state machine with no state and no seat. `:expanded` is a render prop and `@click` is bound to a <div role="article">; the card grows on click but emits no aria-expanded, aria-pressed, aria-controls, role=button, tabindex or keydown. The component was modelled as a display surface that responds to clicks, never as a disclosure control.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:97,102 (`:expanded="pm.expandedId.value === palette.slug"`, `@click="pm.toggleExpand(palette.slug)"`); demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:5-26,185. Measured (probe/p4-D-iphone14-expand.mjs, WebKit): iPhone 14 cardH 125 → click → {h:228, expandedAttr:null, pressed:null}; 1440x900 cardH 100 → click → {h:211, expandedAttr:null, pressed:null}. artTabIndex = [-1,-1,-1,-1,-1] in Chromium AND WebKit. Revealed payload read from live DOM: "Sunset Commons | 5 | 1 | warm | sunset | 7 | user-1" — the collapsed row plus one token.
defects.mechanism: entity card modelled as presentation, not as a control — no seat exists to carry activation/selection/disclosure state
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-iphone14-expand.mjs (LAN origin http://192.168.1.166:9000 + Playwright route stub of api.color.babb.dev); or manually: open #/browse against a reachable API, click a card, inspect the [role="article"] element attributes.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition, not a patch: make the article root a noninteractive container (drop @click and cursor-pointer) and introduce the one native <button type="button" aria-pressed> seat VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 already specifies, spanning specimen+identity. Move the in-card expansion payload (owner, slug, duplicate swatches) into the §3.1 selected-palette inspector the route is supposed to have and currently donates to My Palettes. This single move closes D4-01, D4-03, D4-05 and the prior passes' D-11/D-13, because the identity becomes a button label rather than the only shrinkable flex item.

defects.defect: The specimen loses area to its own chrome. The colour strip — the reason a person opens a colour commons — is a fixed h-10 at every viewport while the metadata rail grows with wrapping, so the narrower the device the smaller the specimen's share. Five persistent status/action regions (count chip, fork count, tag chips, vote button, ··· menu) where PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.2 allows one.
defects.evidence: Measured on devices["iPhone 14"] (the exact profile audit/visual/capture.mjs:57 uses): cardH=125, stripH=40 → specimen 32.0% / chrome 68.0%. Desktop 1440: cardH=100, stripH=40 → 40%/60%. Source: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:9 (`flex h-10 w-full`). Frame: evidence/D-p4-wall-iphone14.png
defects.mechanism: fixed-height specimen band + elastic metadata rail — the support region is the only one allowed to grow
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-iphone14-expand.mjs — read `cardH` and `stripH` from the JSON output.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of the D4-01 transposition: once specimen+identity are one named seat and the surplus metadata discloses in the inspector, the strip is the card's protagonist by construction rather than a 40px band above a six-species rail. Do not patch this with a taller h-12 strip — that preserves the inverted relation at a larger size.

defects.defect: `show-slug` is inert on the wall, and is an action when it does fire. The prop is passed to every card on the commons but is consumed only inside `v-if="expanded"`, and what it renders is a named clipboard button, not provenance text.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:101 passes `show-slug`; demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:140-143 gates it behind `v-if="expanded"` (`:display-slug="showSlug ? displaySlug : undefined"`). Measured on the settled populated wall: `slugShown: false` (document.body.innerText.includes("sunset-commons")). Expanded subtree read: {t:"button", ti:0, al:"Copy slug user-1"}.
defects.mechanism: a prop gated behind an unreachable, unexpressible disclosure — dead plumbing at the call site
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-iphone14-expand.mjs → `slugShown: false`; then node probe/p4-D-filtered-empty.mjs → the expanded subtree reports the Copy slug button.
defects.proposedCure: Either render provenance as a real wall-level text-mono-small line per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 ("value, code, or provenance"), or delete the prop at BrowsePane.vue:101 and the branch at PaletteCard.vue:143. It cannot remain as a prop whose only effect is a clipboard action behind a stateless disclosure (owner edict 2: no dead paths).

defects.defect: The wall's vertical rhythm is a function of string length. Card height is data-dependent, so the column alternates heights depending on whether a palette name happened to wrap.
defects.evidence: Measured at 390px (evidence/D-p4-wall-measurements.json, populated-mob): arts heights = [125, 125, 100, 100, 100] with a constant 12px gap (BrowsePane.vue:46 `gap-3`). Two cards are 125px because their names wrapped to two clipped lines. Frame: evidence/D-p4-wall-mobile-390.png
defects.mechanism: content noise reaching layout — the metadata rail reserves a second line on an axis where the specimen has no collision
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-wall.mjs — read `populated-mob.geo.arts` heights.
defects.proposedCure: Resolves with D4-01/D4-02: once the identity is a button label with its own measure and the surplus chrome moves to the inspector, the row has one wrap-free identity line and a fixed specimen band, so height is container-scaled per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 7 rather than string-scaled.

defects.defect: The card's only keyboard-reachable control is mis-named: the vote chip's accessible name is "1 votes, click to vote" — an ungrammatical plural, an imperative used as a name, and no palette identity anywhere in it. Because the card seat is missing (D4-01), this chip is the card's de-facto accessible representative and is unfit for the job.
defects.evidence: Live subtree read (probe/p4-D-filtered-empty.mjs): {t:"button", ti:0, al:"1 votes, click to vote"}. Chromium tab walk (probe/p4-D-wall.mjs): BUTTON "7 votes, click to vote" → BUTTON "Palette menu" → BUTTON "14 votes, click to vote" → … — ten interchangeable names for ten distinct palettes. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires explicit role, accessible name, state/value.
defects.mechanism: accessible name generated from a count with no plural rule and no object; the identity lives on a non-control parent that is never announced as the button's context
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-wall.mjs — read the `keyboard-chromium.walk` array.
defects.proposedCure: Name the toggle by its object and expose its state, not its instruction: aria-pressed on a toggle named for the palette (e.g. "Vote for Sunset Commons", pressed=true|false) with the count as associated text. The plural rule follows for free once the count leaves the name.

defects.defect: Six ScrollTimeline animations run under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce on #/browse. `pane-title-shrink` is a defensible position-mapped scrub, but `pane-desc-shrink` drives opacity 1→0 plus translateY, so under PRM scrolling the Browse wall makes the pane description disappear. This NARROWS a negative proof pass 2 banked ("Motion is tokenized and reduced-motion-correct").
defects.evidence: Measured (probe/p4-D-wall.mjs, WebKit context reducedMotion:"reduce", t+4000ms): document.getAnimations() → 6 entries, all playState "running", all timeline ScrollTimeline — pane-header-veil ×2, pane-title-shrink ×2, pane-desc-shrink ×2. Matches STATES.json reduced-motion-desktop #/browse row (animatedCount: 6, rafPer1500ms: 0). Source: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:177 gates on @supports (animation-timeline: scroll()) and nothing else; :148-151 states the design position; :214-223 is the opacity keyframe. Contra VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state." Prior claim: challenge-D-design-pass2.md:667.
defects.mechanism: scroll-driven scrub exempted from PRM wholesale, including an opacity-to-zero arm that is not merely position-mapped geometry
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe/p4-D-wall.mjs — read the `reduced-motion` probe row.
defects.proposedCure: TIGHTEN the opacity arm only, at the owner (PaneHeader.vue), not a wholesale PRM gate: under prefers-reduced-motion resolve pane-desc-shrink to its stable end state (description present, opacity 1) and leave the transform scrub intact. BrowsePane is only the consumer (BrowsePane.vue:3) — do not patch it here.

defects.defect: The pane hands its search field to the design system and then fights it: `.search-seated` is an unlayered per-instance override chosen specifically to beat glass-ui's @layer components recipe by layer order, live in three consumers, and it stacks a third cartoon caster on a plate that already stacks two.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:12 (`class="search-seated"`); demo/styles/utils.css:125-137 — the file states the mechanism: "unlayered, so it wins over the @layer components recipe by layer order", and :137 adds `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-sm)`. Booked swap is variant="seated" (ASK-D) at utils.css:129-131. Measured: `node -p "require('@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json').version"` → 7.0.0; `grep -rn "seated" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/*.d.ts *.css` → no match. Three consumers: BrowsePane.vue:12, PalettesPane.vue:35, AdminPane.vue:14. Contra owner edicts 4 and 5.
defects.mechanism: a documented, booked interim carry that did not retire when its producer major landed — now a cascade-layer exploit in three files
defects.reproduction: NONE for a rendered failure — this is a source/versioning fact. Verified by the two commands pasted above (glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no `seated` token or variant).
defects.proposedCure: Not a consumer patch. Land the already-booked glass-ui ASK-D `variant="seated"` on SearchBar (with the ASK-B font seam and ASK-C cap seam) and delete .search-seated from utils.css and its three call sites in one cut. Pass 3's §6.B reaches the same producer ask from the labelling side; this is the same ask from the material side.

result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative proof is owed for the whole. defects.defect: The browse search composes two mutually incompatible predicates and hands over between them at 2 characters, so typing the second character of a word empties the commons and renders the "the commons is empty, go publish one" invitation.
defects.evidence: Client predicate: demo/palettes/useFilteredList.ts:8-12 (untrimmed, any length) + demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:43-45 (`p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q)`), rendered at BrowsePane.vue:340 (its only consumer in the tree). Server predicate: useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-61 (`q.trim()`, sent only when `length >= 2`) → api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:95-96 (`f.$text = {$search: q}`) → api/src/platform/db/db.ts:57-60 (`createIndex({name:"text"})` — WORD/stem matching on `name` only). Measured live (probe-C3/probe-c3-live-proxy.mjs, real production commons, 10 public palettes incl. `Ocean Depths`): typed `o` → request `/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest` (no q) → 3 cards; `oc` → `…&q=oc` → 0 cards + "No published palettes here yet."; `oce` → 0; `ocea` → 0; `ocean` → `…&q=ocean` → 1 card; cleared → 10 cards. Server side confirmed independently: `curl "https://api.color.babb.dev/palettes?limit=50&sort=newest&q=oc"` → 0 rows; `…&q=ocean` → 1 row ['Ocean Depths']. Trim divergence measured: `' o'` → server sends NO q (trims to 1 char) → 10 rows returned → client filters `name.includes(" o")` → 0 cards + true-empty invitation.
defects.mechanism: Two engines answering one question, composed in series. A length threshold SWAPS which engine answers, and the two engines disagree about what a match is (substring vs whole-word/stem, name+slug vs name-only, untrimmed vs trimmed). The composition is an intersection of disagreeing predicates, and the intersection is usually empty.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-C3/probe-c3-live-proxy.mjs — the `perKeystroke` array is printed unconditionally. Manually: type `oc` into "Search the commons…" against any reachable backend. Frame: probe-C3/c3-cliff-at-oc.png.
defects.proposedCure: One predicate, one place. EITHER the server owns search — delete `filteredBrowse` outright, render `remotePalettes` directly, and replace `$text` with a prefix-capable matcher (anchored name+slug regex or an Atlas autocomplete index), because `$text` structurally cannot answer a type-ahead — OR the client owns it and `q` never goes on the wire. What cannot stand is a length threshold that swaps engines. Same fix as C-6/P-4: the colour seam wants to move server-side by the same move.

defects.defect: Slug search is explicitly offered by the code and is dead in the product: it works at exactly one character and nowhere else.

defects.mechanism: Same as P-2 — two engines in series where the upstream one cannot see a field the downstream one filters on. Copying a slug the pane itself displays and pasting it into the pane's own search box returns the empty-commons invitation.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/BrowsePane/probe-C3/probe-c3-slug-and-retry.mjs — the `slugSearch` array is printed unconditionally.

defects.defect: NEW — the always-mounted add slot binds the UNCOALESCED live colour, so every colour change re-randomises its border-radius silhouette AND re-seeds its `feTurbulence`, forcing an SVG filter re-rasterisation the producer's own doc says never happens.
defects.evidence: CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:96 `:color="cssColorOpaque"`; demo/color-picker/App.vue:271 `provide(CSS_COLOR_KEY, cssColorOpaque)` — the RAW signal, not `cssColorOpaqueFrame`. Producer bundle: `useWatercolorBlob` with animate=false installs `watch(colorSource, c => borderRadius.value = radiiToCSS(randomRadii(mulberry32(hashString(c+seed)),lo,hi)))`, and setup computes `seed = hashString(color+seed)%256` bound to `<feTurbulence seed>`. Producer header states 'the SVG <filter> rasterizes ONCE + caches … and NEVER re-rasterizes per frame'. Measured over one 60-move slider drag (probe/probe-P4-a.mjs): `{"styleMutations":34,"turbSeedMutations":17,"distinctBorderRadii":7,"distinctTurbSeeds":11}`; fleet-wide (probe/probe-P4-b.mjs, 7 dots, dragMs 5613): `{"styleMutations":267,"seedMutations":68}`. demo/color-session/useAtmosphereFrameCoalesce.ts:1-30 exists verbatim because heavy derives 'would otherwise fire SYNCHRONOUSLY on EVERY cssColorOpaque change, i.e. 60x/s under a slider drag -> the ~20fps / 31-of-44-janked collapse' and instructs consumers to read the RETURNED signal 'never the synchronous cssColorOpaque'.
defects.mechanism: F-h: hot-signal consumption that bypasses the repo's own rAF coalescer, making an SVG filter graph a function of a 60 Hz signal.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/CurrentPaletteEditor/probe/probe-P4-a.mjs (add slot); node .../probe-P4-b.mjs (fleet).
defects.proposedCure: Bind `cssColorOpaqueFrame` (already built, already exported, already provided to the atmosphere) instead of `cssColorOpaque` — or, better, make the seed independent of colour (C4-1's cure) so the silhouette and filter stop being a function of the live signal at all. Only the swatch background needs frame-accurate colour, and a background-colour change is a compositor op, not a filter rebuild.

defects.defect: NEW (producer relay) — `hashString(color+seed) % 256` collides across exactly the palette a colour tool contains: pure R, G and B all map to filter seed 173, defeating glass-ui's documented 'no twelve-clones' per-instance uniqueness promise.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/prng-2uS6J_A1.js implements djb2 (`t=(t<<5)+t+charCodeAt|0`); WatercolorDot truncates with `%256`, and 33^8 == 1 (mod 256) so the low byte depends only on chars weighted by position mod 8. Computed: rgb(255 0 0)=527826861 (%256=173), rgb(0 255 0)=4041908397 (173), rgb(0 0 255)=3938648493 (173), rgb(255 255 0)=3676147897 (185), rgb(0 255 255)=3591819961 (185), rgb(255 0 255)=3572887993 (185), #ff0000=2134180884 (20), #00ff00=4253796628 (20). Observed live in one rendered row (probe/probe-P4-c.mjs, 4 saved colours): turbSeed 173, 173, 173, 185. Producer doc: 'The filter seed is per-instance off hashString(color + seed) so each dot's wet edge is uniquely displaced (no twelve-clones).'
defects.mechanism: F-i: a truncated hash defeats a per-instance-uniqueness promise. borderRadius still differs because it consumes the full 32-bit hash; only the filter seed is truncated.
defects.reproduction: node --input-type=module -e "import {hashString} from '/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js'; for (const c of ['rgb(255 0 0)','rgb(0 255 0)','rgb(0 0 255)']) console.log(c, hashString(c), hashString(c)%256)"  — and node docs/.../probe/probe-P4-c.mjs for the rendered row.
defects.proposedCure: Producer-side, via the standing glass-ui BH-inbox relay — mix before truncating (e.g. `h ^= h>>>16; seed = h & 0xff`) or widen the attribute domain. Do NOT patch this in demo/.

result.strongestDefect: L3-1 — the published package's runtime `dependencies` are the demo's dependencies. Every other finding is internal to a demo that ships to one URL; L3-1's blast radius is every consumer of @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0. It inverts the dependency direction at the only boundary the outside world can observe, and npm itself prints the resulting cycle (value.js -> glass-ui -> value.js) alongside vue@3.5.35, reka-ui@2.9.9 and tailwindcss@4.3.0 in the `npm ls --omit=dev` tree of a framework-free colour library. It is also the cheapest to cure (two fields move to devDependencies) and the easiest to keep cured (assert `dependencies === {}`), which is the profile of a defect that survives only because nobody has read the manifest from a consumer's side.

This is the mirror of C-2 — C-2 is "the search ignores what you typed", C-19 is "the indicator ignores what you searched" — and both fall out of the same missing single source of truth.

defects.defect: `@submit.prevent="onSlugSwitch"` on `<SearchBar tag="form">` never binds to the form. glass-ui 7's SearchBar declares `inheritAttrs:false` and spreads `$attrs` (minus class) onto its inner `<input type="search">`, so the submit listener sits on a node that can never receive a submit event. Submitting the login form calls nothing and, because `.prevent` never runs, performs a native GET submission of a form with no `action` — per the HTML spec the action defaults to the document URL, so the SPA does a full navigation and the typed slug is discarded.
defects.evidence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js — SearchBar setup: `inheritAttrs: !1` … `o = g(() => { let {class:e, ...t} = P(); return t })` … `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search"}, o.value, {...}))`. Measured (probes/c3-slugbar.probe.test.ts PROBE G/G2, real SFC + real glass-ui): `[G] handler calls after FORM submit: 0` · `[G] handler calls after INPUT-targeted submit: 1` · `[G2] handler calls after clicking submit: 0` · `[G2] jsdom errors (navigation attempts): ['Error: Not implemented: HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit']` (jsdom's stand-in for a real navigation).
defects.mechanism: attribute-fallthrough misrouting — a listener authored for a component's root lands on a descendant because the vendor sets inheritAttrs:false; the modifier (.prevent) is lost with it
defects.reproduction: npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/c3-vitest.config.ts — PROBE G and PROBE G2 print the call counts above.
defects.proposedCure: The component must own a real `<form @submit.prevent>` and place `SearchBar` inside it as a field (tag="div"); OR glass-ui grows a `submit` emit on SearchBar — the design-system-side home for a form-shaped control. Not a `@keydown.enter` patch, which would leave the button path broken.

defects.defect: The component is an orphan: it is rendered on zero routes and has zero value-position importers. A failed login is silent in the live app.

Delete the SFC + slug/index.ts + browser/index.ts:44 + the unbound ref and type-only import in useSlugMigration.ts (a 3-file change that cannot break a consumer, since nothing imports the seam — see C-29), then repair the LIVE surface's error path, which is currently unreachable for a reason unguessable from either file.

defects.defect: Any input that is not exactly four lowercase hyphenated words is silently reclassified as an ADMIN TOKEN and emitted with isAdmin=true. The parent then executes `deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value)` — i.e. a single typo in your own slug logs you out of your identity and stores junk as an admin credential, with no error and no confirmation.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:205 `const isAdmin = !looksLikeSlug(normalized);` → :213 `emit("switchSlug", isAdmin ? normalizeTokenInput(raw) : normalized, isAdmin)`. demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51-57 `if (isAdmin) { deps.clearUserSlug(); deps.adminLogin(value); setActiveTab("saved"); return; }`. Measured (PROBE D, 6/6): 'azure-drifting-teal'→[…,true]; 'azure drifting teal fox'→[…,true]; 'azure-drifting-teal-fox-extra'→[…,true]; 'azure_drifting_teal_fox'→[…,true]; 'azure-drifting-teal-fox2'→[…,true]; 'azure--drifting-teal-fox'→[…,true].
defects.mechanism: binary negation used as a classifier — 'not shape A' is treated as 'therefore credential B', with no third (invalid) outcome and no confirmation before a destructive session mutation
defects.reproduction: PROBE D in probes/c3-slugbar.probe.test.ts (parameterised over the six near-miss strings).
defects.proposedCure: Three-way outcome: slug | adminToken | invalid. adminToken reachable only via the explicit `ADMIN_TOKEN=` sentinel normalizeTokenInput already parses, or a separate affordance; everything else is invalid and renders an error WITHOUT touching session state.

defects.defect: NEW (pass 3). A rejection from the async parent handler escapes the component entirely and lands on the global error channel as an unhandledRejection plus a Vue warn — it is not merely undisplayed. `emit()` returns void, the component's try/catch has already completed synchronously, and Vue routes the listener's rejected promise to app.config.errorHandler (absent) → console noise on every failed login.
defects.evidence: PROBE B, parent listener `async () => { throw new Error("404 Slug not found") }`: `[B] rendered error text: null` · `[B] unhandled rejections captured: [ 'Error: 404 Slug not found' ]` · stderr `[Vue warn]: Unhandled error during execution of component event handler at <PaletteSlugBar …>`. Live listener is `async function onSlugSwitch` at demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51.
defects.mechanism: fire-and-forget emit across an async boundary — the event contract is synchronous while its only implementation is asynchronous, so failures cannot be caught locally and are promoted to global
defects.reproduction: PROBE B in probes/c3-slugbar.probe.test.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Make the contract honest about being async: either the parent owns pending/error state and the component becomes presentational (pending/error as props), or the event carries a completion handle `switchSlug: [slug, isAdmin, done: (err?) => void]`. Do NOT bolt a `.catch()` onto the emit site — that hides the failure one level lower.

defects.defect: NEW (pass 3). Bounding proof for C-5: the predicate `looksLikeSlug` is a TOTAL SOUND ACCEPTOR of the real slug space — all 268,435,456 slugs the API can mint pass it, and no word list entry contains a hyphen or non-[a-z] char. Therefore the defect is exactly and only the unconditional negation at line 205, not the regex. defects.defect: The 50ms `setTimeout` that defers entering edit mode is uncancelled across unmount (it fires into a destroyed instance), and the focus call it schedules is double-optional-chained — `searchBarRef.value?.inputRef?.focus()` — so when the ref is null (which it always is: <Transition mode="out-in"> has not yet mounted the enter branch) the miss is swallowed with no throw, no warn, no observable trace. That silent swallow is why the focus bug survived.
defects.evidence: PaletteSlugBar.vue:176-181. Measured (PROBE E): `[E] pending timers at unmount: 1 · after unmount: 1 · timers after advance: 0` — the timer survives unmount and then runs. CSS corroboration for the focus race: demo/styles/animations.css:111-116 `.vj-morph-leave-active { transition: opacity var(--duration-fast) …, transform var(--duration-fast) …}` — out-in mounts the enter branch only after that leave, while nextTick resolves on the current microtask. The live sibling demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:16-23 has the same shape and works, because it enters edit mode synchronously with no transition to race.
defects.mechanism: an unowned timer plus a masking optional chain (edict 2): a guard that converts an always-wrong case into a no-op instead of a failure
defects.reproduction: PROBE E (timer). The focus miss itself is NOT reproducible in jsdom — VTU stubs <Transition>, so the harness's enterEditMode succeeds; the live measurement is pass 1's insertedAtMs: 276. Labelled accordingly: mechanism proven by reading + CSS arithmetic, timing proven by pass 1.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the timer and the chain together — bind focus to the branch's own lifecycle (@after-enter on the Transition, or autofocus on the field) and let a genuinely-absent ref fail loudly.

result.strongestDefect: C-2 — `@submit.prevent` binds to glass-ui SearchBar's inner `<input>` instead of the `<form>` (inheritAttrs:false spreads $attrs onto the field), so the login form's handler is never called (measured: 0 calls on form submit vs 1 on an input-targeted submit) and, with `.prevent` lost, activating it performs a native form submission — a full document navigation in the SPA. The component's single reason to exist does not work, and would not work the moment anyone mounted it. Ranked above the orphan finding (C-1) only because C-1's disposition is a decision (delete vs. re-mount) while C-2 is an unambiguous implementation defect that must be repaired in either branch — and its mechanism (silent attribute-fallthrough misrouting past a vendor's inheritAttrs:false) is a class the rest of the demo consumer surface shares.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field carries the negatives established so the next pass need not re-spend the probes. Hazards named in the brief, each CHECKED and ABSENT here: no defineModel anywhere in the component (ref + defineExpose only), so the stale-read round-trip class does not apply; no colour math at all — cssColorOpaque goes straight to :style — so oklch→HSV hue drift and stableHue are N/A; no ValueUnit construction, so the nesting-accumulation class is N/A; no slider, so the reka pointer-capture leak is N/A; zero requestAnimationFrame and no per-frame or per-keystroke work whatsoever (the only work is on submit), so the PRM-RAF epidemic does not touch this file; no canvas/WebGL; nothing parses CSS, so the live parseCssColor crash class is not reachable. Measured negatives: (a) NO ReDoS — /^[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+-[a-z]+$/ against 50,000-char adversarial inputs runs in 0.072ms (no dashes) and 0.007ms (alternating dashes); (b) the compiled prop `userSlug: { type: [String, null], required: true }` is safe — Vue 3.5.35 guards it at runtime-core.cjs.js:5094 `if (ctor === null)`; (c) the props-destructure shadowing at line 205 (`const isAdmin` shadowing the `isAdmin` prop) COMPILES CORRECTLY — the SFC compiler keeps the local and rewrites only genuine prop reads to __props.*, verified in the compiled output (independently reproduces pass 2's C-25); (d) `border-muted-foreground` (line 65) is a valid utility — `--color-muted-foreground` is registered in glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/bridges.css; (e) no CSS-injection surface via cssColorOpaque — Vue's object :style writes through el.style; (f) most consequentially, `looksLikeSlug` is a TOTAL SOUND ACCEPTOR of the API's entire mintable slug space — all 268,435,456 combinations of the four 128-word lists in api/src/modules/session/slugWords.ts pass, with zero failures and no non-[a-z] token in any list, which kills the tempting over-claim that the classifier also rejects legitimate slugs and bounds C-5's cure to the negation alone.

result.strongestDefect: LP3-1 — the swatch's `focus-ring` never paints. Every precondition is satisfied (glass-ui's `.focus-ring:focus-visible` rule IS loaded, `--focus-ring-shadow` resolves to a real two-layer ring, and the element measurably matches `:focus-visible`), yet the computed box-shadow contains only the three `shadow-cartoon-sm` layers and `outline-style` is `none`. A keyboard user reaches the control and receives nothing. The mechanism is structural, not a typo: glass-ui publishes its focus affordance as a `box-shadow` class, on a design system whose entire material language (`shadow-cartoon-*`, `glass-wash`, `glass-capsule`) is also `box-shadow` — the two cannot coexist, `box-shadow` replaces rather than composes, and cascade layers (`components` < `utilities`) decide it before specificity is consulted. Nothing in types, eslint, vue-tsc or a screenshot can observe the collision. The repo has already diagnosed and cured this exact death twice in prose — `demo/styles/utils.css:140-144` ("Compose, never replace: the unlayered base box-shadow would otherwise silently beat the layered ring") and `demo/styles/focus-ring.css:9-15` (the U-F25 lesson) — and still shipped a ringless control, because a cure that lives in a comment is not an invariant.

defects.defect: The login form cannot submit. `@submit.prevent` is bound to glass-ui 7's `SearchBar`, which is `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads all non-`class` attrs onto its inner `<input type="search">` rather than onto the `tag="form"` root. An `<input>` never fires `submit`, so the `<form>` carries no submit listener and nothing calls `preventDefault()` — the browser performs an unprevented native GET submission that reloads the SPA and discards the typed credential. Prior run identified the cause but could only argue the consequence 'from the HTML spec rather than a probe' (jsdom died at `requestSubmit`); this run reproduced the navigation in a real browser.
defects.evidence: CAUSE, compiled producer read directly: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/search.js` — `inheritAttrs: !1`; `o = computed(() => { let {class: e, ...t} = useAttrs(); return t })` is spread into `b("input", w({ref_key:"inputRef", ref:s, type:"search"}, o.value, {...}))` while the root `j(e.tag)` receives only `class` and `data-surface`. CONSEQUENCE, WebKit, two arms (probes/psb-submit2.mjs): arm A listener-on-FORM -> `{handlerRuns:1, formStillPresent:true}`, navigations `[]`. arm B listener-on-INPUT -> `{handlerRuns:"gone (page navigated)", formStillPresent:false, url:"http://localhost:9000/?#/palettes?..."}`, 3 recorded main-frame navigations. The interposed `?` is the native GET-submission signature. Binding site: demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:5-15.
defects.mechanism: producer-contract misuse — SearchBar is a field, not a form host, but accepts `tag="form"` without objecting, so the consumer's `@submit` silently relocates to the inner input. Typecheck cannot see it: `onSubmit` is a legal fall-through attr. Landed in the glass-7 adoption commit f2c8f565.
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaletteSlugBar/probes/psb-submit2.mjs (dev server live at :9000). Two arms print handlerRuns + recorded navigations.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural, not a patch: the component is deleted (D-1), so at the value.js altitude the cure is that the Account Dialog owns a real `<form @submit.prevent>` around a real `<input autocomplete=…>`, exactly as the live sibling demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:76-79 already does. Separately, a glass-ui BH/BI relay item: `SearchBar` must either refuse `tag="form"` or route non-input listeners to its root — every future consumer hits this silently.

VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1 requires 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance' to render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose; the pill has no isolation. index.html currently pins dir="ltr" document-wide, which is why nothing is visibly wrong today — but that attribute's own source comment describes it as the RTL seam, deliberately established so dir="rtl" flips the document. The moment it does, an un-isolated hyphen-segmented slug reorders against surrounding prose.
defects.evidence: MEASURED (probes/psb-probe.mjs and psb-probe3.mjs): pill computed style -> `{ unicodeBidi: "normal", direction: "ltr" }`. `unicode-bidi: normal` is the absence of isolation. Recipe: demo/styles/foundation.css:585-587 `.slug-pill { @apply text-mono-small font-bold px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full border; }` — no isolation property. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §6.1 direction-jurisdictions table, row 4.
defects.mechanism: bidi isolation — a latent RTL defect held harmless only by a document-level dir pin that the repo explicitly intends to flip.
defects.reproduction: node probes/psb-probe3.mjs — read `pillUnicodeBidi`. Hypothesis label: the reorder consequence under dir="rtl" is not photographed (no /palettes RTL capture exists and the component does not render); the missing property is measured, the downstream reorder is mechanism.
defects.proposedCure: Isolation belongs in the shared `.slug-pill` recipe at foundation.css:585-587 — once, for all five call sites — not at each consumer. Same shape as D-15: the recipe is the root, and the root is where direction law must live.

Subtraction precedes explanation.'

defects.defect: The three-dot menu trigger is a 22x22 CSS px operable target — below WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum, before considering the 44px comfort floor. Built as `p-1` around a 14px glyph.

The same 22x22 recurs on the live dock's `DockControl compact` seats (probe DOCK block: 'Switch to slug' 22x22, 'Generate new slug' 22x22, 'Cancel' 22x22), so this is a family, not an isolated site — consistent with the visual audit's smallTapTargets column, nonzero on all 60 captures (REPORT.md:31-92). defects.reproduction: node probes/psb-probe.mjs — `dots` and `DOCK` blocks.
defects.proposedCure: PR-12's stated cure, at the root: an invisible seat geometry that preserves the 24px target floor while the visible glyph keeps its optical rung — applied in glass-ui's control primitives so every DockControl/icon-button inherits it, rather than padding each consumer.

defects.defect: The account menu is a `Popover` filled with four hand-rolled `<button>` rows, in a repo where glass-ui's `DropdownMenu` is the design system's menu and is already consumed for this exact surface by the live sibling. The hand-roll forfeits roving focus, the producer's typeahead engine, `disabled`, and cancellable `select`; and it declares `aria-haspopup="dialog"` for something that is semantically a menu.
defects.evidence: Site: PaletteSlugBar.vue:81-120 — `<Popover>` + `<PopoverContent>` containing four `<button class="flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 …">` rows; trigger at :84 carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. Producer surface available: demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts re-exports DropdownMenu/Trigger/Content/Item/Separator/Label straight from @mkbabb/glass-ui; DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts declares `disabled`, `textValue` ('Text used by the menu's typeahead engine'), and a cancellable `select` emit. Live counterexample: ProfileSection.vue:53-91 implements the same four commands with DropdownMenu/DropdownMenuItem.
defects.mechanism: design-system boundary — reaching past glass-ui to hand-assemble a primitive it already provides. Owner edict 4.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static. Read PaletteSlugBar.vue:81-120 against ProfileSection.vue:53-91 and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/*/DropdownMenuItem.vue.d.ts.
defects.proposedCure: Consume DropdownMenu in the Account Dialog, as ProfileSection already does. The general rule this violates is that a component-type name that already exists must be reused, not re-implemented — the hand-roll is how a11y semantics (roving focus, typeahead, disabled) get silently dropped.

defects.defect: Legacy error-branching retained on a code path that cannot produce it. `onSlugSwitch` wraps a synchronous `emit` in try/catch and branches on `msg.includes("409"|"404"|"429")` — the exact substring pattern that useSlugMigration.ts:78-82 documents, in a source comment, as already found broken and replaced with typed `ApiProblem.status` branching, because the server titles never contain those digits.
defects.evidence: Site: PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225, branches at :218-221. The in-repo correction it ignores: useSlugMigration.ts:78-82 — 'S.W2 W2-6: branch on the typed ApiProblem.status, not .message substrings — the server titles ("Already logged in as this user", "User not found", "Rate limit exceeded") never contain "409"/"404"/"429", so those branches matched nothing and the authored copy below never showed.' The `try` body at :204-215 contains only synchronous work terminating in `emit("switchSlug", …)`, which cannot throw an HTTP-shaped error, so the catch is doubly dead.
defects.mechanism: legacy dual path — a superseded idiom left in place beside its own documented fix. Owner edict 2 (no legacy code, no dual paths, no masking fallbacks).
defects.reproduction: NONE — static. Read PaletteSlugBar.vue:198-225 against useSlugMigration.ts:78-88.
defects.proposedCure: Deleted with the file. The durable cure is that error classification lives once, typed, in the auth owner (ApiProblem.status), and the view renders whatever the port hands it — a view must never re-derive an error taxonomy by string sniffing.

defects.defect: Dead public surface across every channel the component exposes: a prop that is never read, an emit that is never emitted, and — NEW this run — one of three exposed members that has zero call sites, while a second is callable only through a ref that is permanently null. Plus an empty scoped style block.
defects.evidence: `hasSavedPalettes` (:150) — 2 occurrences in the file (type + destructure), never referenced in template or script. `copy: []` emit (:155) — declared, `grep -c 'emit("copy")'` and `emit('copy')` both 0; onCopySlug (:168-170) writes the clipboard directly instead. NEW — `resetEditMode`: `grep -rn resetEditMode --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git .` returns exactly 2 hits, both in this file (:231 definition, :236 defineExpose), zero call sites anywhere. `setError` is reachable only via slugBarRef, which is permanently null (see D-1). Scoped `<style>` at :239-243 contains a `@reference` and a comment and no rules. Also: `useTemplateRef` count 0 — :166 uses `ref<InstanceType<typeof SearchBar>|null>(null)` where the live sibling SlugEditLayer.vue:14 correctly uses `useTemplateRef` (owner edict 7); and the local `const isAdmin` at :205 shadows the destructured reactive prop `isAdmin`.
defects.mechanism: dead public surface — an API contract asserted in types and never exercised by any consumer, so nothing ever falsified it.
defects.reproduction: NONE — static. The three greps quoted above.
defects.proposedCure: Deleted with the file. The generalisable gate: a component whose props/emits/exposes have zero consumers is not 'flexible', it is unmounted — the repo needs a check that fails on 'exported, typechecks, renders nowhere', which is exactly what let a BLOCKER-severity broken login path survive a glass-7 migration, a 60-shot Safari matrix and two prior audits.

defects.defect: Motion and type are both declared in channels the system does not read. Six controls declare `active:scale-95`/`active:scale-[0.98]` while their `transition-property` list contains no `transform`, so the press scale snaps instead of animating; a 50ms magic `setTimeout` sequences the component's own state against another component's close animation; and the Login control renders Fira Code at weight 700 where the closed type matrix assigns controls Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold.
defects.evidence: MOTION — MEASURED (probes/psb-probe.mjs): login `transitionProperty: "color, background-color, border-color, outline-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke, --tw-gradient-*"`, `transitionDuration: "0.2s"` — no `transform` in the list, while the class at :73 declares `active:scale-95`. Same shape at :84, :91, :98, :106, :113. Magic delay: :176 `setTimeout(() => { slugEditMode.value = true; … }, 50)` with the comment 'Delay to let the Popover fully close' — an untokenized constant racing a token-driven exit. TYPE — MEASURED: login `{ fontFamily: "Fira Code", fontWeight: "700", fontSize: "16.4px" }`. Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 type-jurisdiction table — 'control or label, including dropdown options | text-small | Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold'; Fira Code is reserved for 'value, code, or provenance'. §6 requires spatial continuity to use 'one producer-owned glass-ui spring register'.
defects.mechanism: ad-hoc motion + closed-type-matrix violation — intentions stated in classes the cascade does not act on. (Note: the scale animates `transform`, which is compositor-only, so this is NOT a layout-thrash defect — the defect is that it never animates at all.)
defects.reproduction: node probes/psb-probe.mjs — `login`/`dots` blocks, fields transitionProperty, fontFamily, fontWeight.
defects.proposedCure: Motion belongs to the producer's spring register, not to per-consumer `active:scale` + `transition-colors` pairs that silently disagree; the 50ms delay is a sequencing bug that disappears once one component owns the open/close state instead of two racing each other. Type: the control consumes the `text-small` rung from the matrix — the mono family is for the slug value, never for the button that opens it.

result.strongestDefect: D-2 — the login form cannot submit. `@submit.prevent` is bound to glass-ui 7's `SearchBar`, which is `inheritAttrs: false` and spreads every non-`class` attr onto its inner `<input type="search">` while the `tag="form"` root receives only `class` and `data-surface`. An `<input>` never fires `submit`, so the `<form>` has no submit listener and nothing prevents the default action. Prior runs proved the cause but could only argue the consequence from the HTML spec, because jsdom threw on `requestSubmit`; this run reproduced it in WebKit against the live app with a two-arm probe: listener-on-FORM gives `handlerRuns: 1` and zero navigations, listener-on-INPUT gives `handlerRuns: "gone (page navigated)"`, a URL mutated to `http://localhost:9000/?#/palettes?...` (the `?` being the native GET-submission signature), 3 recorded main-frame navigations, and the DOM destroyed. PLAUSIBLE → CONFIRMED: pressing Enter reloads the SPA and discards the typed credential, and there is no path by which `onSlugSwitch` ever runs.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so this field records the two would-be findings this run KILLED by measurement — both are traps I walked into from a code read, and both would have shipped as confident false positives. (1) N-1 — the `vj-morph` swap does NOT jump. `<Transition mode="out-in">` at :4 swaps a pill branch against a Login-button branch of visibly different size, which normally produces a collapse-and-grow; measured in the live cascade (probes/psb-probe.mjs) both branch roots are h=36.00 (pill 28.94, login 32.94 inside them) and `branchDeltaPx = 0.00` — the `min-h-9` on the bar root absorbs both. Bar height is stable across the swap. (2) N-2 — `focus-visible:outline-none` does NOT kill the forced-colors focus outline. Specificity reasoning predicts a defect: Tailwind's `.focus-visible\:outline-none:focus-visible` is (0,2,0) and foundation.css:700-721's WHCM affordance is a zero-specificity `:where(a[href], button, [role="button"], …):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight }` at (0,1,0), so the component should win and blank the outline — and since `ring-*` is a box-shadow, which does not paint in forced colors, focus would vanish entirely. Measured instead in Chromium `forcedColors: "active"` (probes/psb-probe2.mjs): dots, login and menurow all report `outline: "solid 2px rgba(5, 0, 73, 0.8)"` with `boxShadow: "none"` — the root rule wins on all three species, because it is UNLAYERED and unlayered declarations beat every `@layer` regardless of specificity, while `outline-none` lives in `@layer utilities`. Not a defect, and genuinely good foundation design: it holds against consumers that opt out by hand. Also verified sound and not filed: `prefers-reduced-motion` is neutralized globally at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`), satisfying VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:144; the `active:scale-*` presses animate `transform`, which is compositor-only and forces no layout (their real defect is D-10, that `transition-property` omits `transform` so the scale never animates at all — an ad-hoc-motion finding, not a layout-thrash one); and the audit's horizontalOverflow is 0 on every `/palettes` capture, to which this component contributes nothing because it renders nothing.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law) for demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue — PASS 3
