defects.mechanism: the invariant is applied as a decoration on two items rather than as a property of the doomed-action class
defects.reproduction: Serve the dev server over its LAN host with all api.color.babb.dev requests aborted (evidence/pass-2/pcm-p2-h.mjs), then open a card menu: Publish disables and annotates; every other network action remains enabled.
defects.proposedCure: Falls out of C2-8's extracted item table: a declarative `needsNetwork: true` per item, read against the seam-derived `degraded` from C2-4. Both defects close by construction rather than by adding six more `:disabled` bindings.

defects.defect: The same enum→boolean collapse as C2-5 recurs in the admin section: `tier` is 3-state, but an `archived` palette is labelled "Feature" and featuring it silently un-archives.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:159-161 (`palette.tier !== 'featured'` / `tier === 'featured' ? 'Unfeature' : 'Feature'`); demo/palettes/types.ts:42 `tier?: "standard"|"featured"|"archived"`. Verified NOT a toggle bug: useAdminUsers.ts:82-90 does send `palette.tier !== "featured"`, so featured↔standard round-trips correctly — only the third state is mislabelled.
defects.mechanism: identical to C2-5 — a 3-valued curation enum rendered through a two-branch ternary, so the third member aliases onto one of the other two
defects.reproduction: NONE executed — hypothesis. An `archived` remote palette served to an admin session would render "Feature"; the same LAN-host + page.route() stub used for C2-5 (evidence/pass-2/pcm-p2-g.mjs) would exercise it by adding a `tier: "archived"` row and an admin token.
defects.proposedCure: Cure the family, not the instances: both this and C2-5 are enum-shaped state rendered as a toggle. The extracted item table (C2-8) should take the enum and emit an explicit (label, annotation, transition) triple per member, which makes the third state impossible to drop.

defects.defect: The "K-INV5 small-caps register" is two copy-pasted per-instance inline styles plus a duplicated five-class recipe — a per-instance override of a glass-ui primitive (edict 5) for a register that has no name (edict 4).
defects.evidence: PaletteCardMenu.vue:35-39 and :56-59 both carry `class="ml-auto fira-code text-mono-caption opacity-55 tracking-wide" style="font-variant: small-caps"`. Adjacent per-instance sizing of glass-ui primitives: `class="w-48 text-small"` at :7, arbitrary value `max-w-[180px]` at :9.
defects.mechanism: a design register described in a comment but never given a component or a token, so it is re-typed at each use site
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — read PaletteCardMenu.vue:35-39 against :56-59; the two spans are byte-identical apart from their content.
defects.proposedCure: One glass-ui item-annotation variant (a `data-annotation` slot on the existing DropdownMenuItem, or `<DropdownMenuItemAnnotation>`), consumed twice here and available to every future degraded-state affordance. That is also the right home for C2-9's aria-hidden.

defects.defect: Pressing the menu trigger animates the whole card's press spring — the card visibly squashes when the user is opening a menu, not activating the card.
defects.evidence: PaletteCard.vue:24 `v-bind="press.handlers"` on the card root; the handler set from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js is onPointerdown/up/cancel/leave/enter/keydown/keyup/blur; the wrapper at PaletteCard.vue:82 stops `click` only. Measured (probe pcm-p2-a.mjs): before `{"pressT":"0.0000","scale":"none"}`, during pointerdown on the trigger `{"inlineStyle":"--card-press-t: 0.8360; --flex-vel: 0.8360; scale: 1.0079 0.9592;"}`.
defects.mechanism: an event fence built for one event type (`@click.stop`) around a control whose affordance is driven by a different event type (pointerdown)
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with a seeded palette; `page.mouse.down()` on the `Palette menu` button and read `getComputedStyle(card).scale` → `1.0079 0.9592`. Probed and found sound: the press does NOT stick — after mouseup with the menu open, `pressT` returns to 0.0000.
defects.proposedCure: `@pointerdown.stop` alongside the existing `@click.stop`, or better, scope the press handlers so nested interactive descendants are excluded — the wrapper is already a hand-rolled fence around one specific event and should fence the whole affordance.

defects.defect: The owner-facing `Delete` menu item is unconfirmed and irreversible, while the admin `Delete (admin)` item on the same menu is gated by a confirmation dialog.
defects.evidence: LIVE (probe pcm-p2-e.mjs): `::E1_menuOpen {menus:1, articles:8}` → click Delete → `::E2_afterDelete {articles:7}` `::E2_storeN 7` with `::E2_afterDelete overlays: []` and no dialog at any point. Contrast AdminUsersPanel.vue:158-165, which mounts a Dialog/ConfirmDialog for adminDelete. No undo path exists; ActionFeedback is not shown either.
defects.mechanism: two standards of care for the same destructive verb in one menu, with the irreversible one unguarded
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with 8 seeded local palettes; open a card menu; click Delete. localStorage["color-palettes"].palettes drops 8→7 immediately with no confirmation and no feedback.
defects.proposedCure: One confirmation policy per destructive action class, declared in the item table (C2-8) rather than in each host — `destructive: true` implies confirm, so the owner and admin paths cannot diverge.

defects.defect: The reka modal lock is applied to `<body>` while the app's real scroll container is an inner div, so the page is made pointer-inert and aria-hidden while remaining freely scrollable under an open menu — all of the cost, none of the intent.
defects.evidence: Measured (probes pcm-p2-a/c/f.mjs): on open `{"bodyPE":"none","bodyInlinePE":"none","bodyOverflow":"hidden","ariaHidden":"true"}` and `elementAtCardMenuCorner: {"tag":"HTML"}`; but `::scrollInfo {"docHasVScroll":false, candidates:[{tag:"DIV", cls:"glass-resting card …", scrollH:3680, clientH:686, overflowY:"auto"}]}`. Scrolling that div under an open menu: `::scrollAttempt {"before":0,"after":320,"moved":true}`; the menu stays anchored (`delta` constant 40.4 px) and there is no layout shift (`::SHIFT` all zeros, `bodyPadRight 0px`).
defects.mechanism: reka's `modal: true` default is never considered by this component; its scroll lock targets an element the app does not scroll
defects.reproduction: Seed 30 palettes at /#/palettes; open a card menu; set the inner scroller's scrollTop +320 — it moves, while document.body carries overflow:hidden and pointer-events:none.
defects.proposedCure: Decide the modality deliberately. A dropdown on a card inside a scrolling list is a strong candidate for `:modal="false"`, which drops the app-wide aria-hidden and pointer-inertness that currently buy nothing.

defects.defect: The 8-matrix Safari visual audit captured zero PaletteCards, so this component contributes nothing to the REPORT's tap-target and nameless-button counts and the sweep proves nothing about it either way.
defects.evidence: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.json: /#/palettes bodyTextLength 237 (desktop) / 169 (mobile), /#/browse 280 / 124; smallTapTargets on every row are PaletteSlugBar ("Switch to slug", "Generate new slug", "Cancel", 22-23 px) and ComponentSliders channel spans only; no `Palette menu` button in any of the 8 captures; every /#/browse row carries the console warning "Failed to load remote palettes: SyntaxError: The string did not match the expected pattern."
defects.mechanism: the sweep ran against an empty local store and a dead API, so both hosting routes rendered their empty/failed states
defects.reproduction: NONE needed — read the eight matching rows in REPORT.json. My own measurements fill the gap: trigger 36×36 (desktop) / 54×54 (mobile), items 178×44, submenu items ~326×44, all ≥24 px; trigger `aria-label="Palette menu"`; content role=menu with aria-labelledby → the trigger.
defects.proposedCure: Seed the visual matrix with local palettes (and a stubbed browse feed via the LAN-host technique in the report) so the card and its menu are actually on screen; otherwise the sweep's silence will keep reading as a pass.

result.strongestDefect: C2-1 — 22 menu-item instances, including the destructive `Delete`, are wired to nothing at 3 of the 5 host sites. Reproduced with a matched control on the same build in the same run: `Delete` on /#/mix leaves the store at 8/8 (no feedback, no dialog, menu closes as if it worked), while the identical click on /#/palettes takes it 8 → 7; Export → JSON downloads `probe-palette-0.json` on /#/palettes and nothing on /#/mix. The cause is not a slip in this file's logic but a hole in its contract — `action: [action: string]` (PaletteCardMenu.vue:224-227) plus `if (!fn) return` (PaletteCard.vue:316) plus seventeen separate host-side `@`-bindings means correctness is a property of files this component never sees, checked by nothing. It outranks C2-2 (one dead feature on one input modality) because it is a destructive verb that silently no-ops on a route reachable in two clicks, and because it is the general case of the pass-1 seat's MINOR C-5, whose mirror-image symptom (a dead `copyAll` handler) they rated as cosmetic.
result.negativeProof: Verdict is DEFECTIVE, so no negative is claimed for the component as a whole. The following sub-claims WERE probed with the same effort and came back sound, and should not be re-litigated: (1) no stuck press — after mouseup with the menu open, `pressT 0.0000`, `scale none`; (2) no leaked modal layer — after Delete, Escape, Rename and a route change, `overlays: []`, `body.style.pointerEvents` and `overflow` both restored, trigger clickable again; (3) no layout shift from the scroll lock — all deltas 0, `bodyPadRight 0px`; (4) closed menus cost nothing — 30 cards → 1058 total DOM nodes, 0 menuitems, 0 menus (portalled + presence-gated); (5) Feature/Unfeature is a real toggle — useAdminUsers.ts:82-90 sends `palette.tier !== "featured"`; (6) no leaked rAF, listeners, observers or timers in this file — the sub-trigger's timer is reka's and is cleared in its own onUnmounted, so zero PRM-RAF contribution; (7) none of the six known local hazards are present — no defineModel, no oklch/HSV roundtrip, no ValueUnit wrapping, no slider pointer-capture, no WebGL, no parsing; (8) edict 8 (verbatimModuleSyntax) PASSES — both type-only imports at :177/:178 are `import type`; (9) edict 4 PASSES structurally — all 14 primitives re-exported from @mkbabb/glass-ui via demo/ui/dropdown-menu/index.ts, zero local forks (the styling half fails, see C2-12); (10) edict 1 PASSES — 228 lines, one job, two computeds; (11) zero page errors attributable to this component across all nine probe runs; (12) disabled items are genuinely inert under a tripped latch — `aria-disabled="true"`, `data-disabled=""`, `pointer-events: none`; (13) focus restoration on dismiss is correct — Escape returns focus to the trigger (and it is precisely this correct behaviour that causes C2-6); (14) `useApiClient()` throws without a provider, but `provideApiClient()` at App.vue:219 stands above all five host sites, so it is sound in the app — that throw is why the component cannot be mounted in isolation, which is a contributing cause of C2-8.

result.axis: D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, design-system boundary, proportion/seat law)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`. Declared seat, matches the spawn declaration; not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the FIRST drag-to-reorder of every session permutes the entire library and the corruption persists to localStorage. Asked to move row 1 to slot 3 of 5, the component writes `P3,P4,P2,P5,P1` instead of `P2,P3,P1,P4,P5`: all five rows move and the dragged row lands at the opposite end from the drop slot. Reproduced 3/3 in fresh WebKit contexts. Drags 2..n in the same session are correct, which is precisely why it shipped — any manual test that drags twice sees a correct result. Cause: `PalettesPane.vue:183` passes `pm.filteredSaved.value` (a plain array) instead of the ref, and because `useFilteredList.ts:9` returns `items.value` unchanged for an empty query, that array IS the object the `savedPalettes` computed caches; vueuse's un-overridden `defaultOptions.onUpdate` splices an element out of it synchronously and SortableJS fires `update` before `end`, so `onEnd` maps N−1 ids and `reorderPalettes` appends the two orphans at the tail.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the next seat does not re-spend the probes — eleven attacks that did NOT break: (1) zero horizontal overflow at 1440/720/390/320, under RTL, at 2x type scale, with a 76-char name and at 40 palettes; REPORT.json agrees `overflowX: 0` in all four Safari matrices. (2) RTL mirrors correctly — pane x 729->199, the `justify-end` delete row moves to the logical end x 1188->224, handles x 768->656, no LTR leakage. (3) The count-badge a11y construction works: `aria-hidden` Badge + `sr-only` companion gives the heading the accessible name "My Palettes (5 saved)", not "My Palettes5". (4) Vertical rhythm is exact — search->editor->delete-row->grid gaps measure 12,12,12 px in both schemes at every viewport. (5) No design-system fork: `demo/ui/{card,button,badge}/index.ts` are one-line glass-ui re-exports. (6) Zero page errors and zero console errors on `/#/palettes` in all four tracked Safari matrices. (7) The empty invitation's mark is §7-compliant — exactly three WatercolorDots plus dashes, `aria-hidden="true"`, static. (8) The LIGHT ramp does meet its declared floor (5.77:1 vs a 3:1 large-text floor) and `My` is genuinely neutral (C 0.0061 light / 0.0063 dark), so §2's neutral-`My` clause holds. (9) Long names truncate with an ellipsis rather than overflowing at 1440/390/320. (10) Reorder DOES persist across reload (`P2,P3,P4,P5,P1` -> `P2,P3,P4,P5,P1`) — the superseded pass's "lost on reload" claim is a Playwright `addInitScript` re-seed artifact and is retracted. (11) The 200%-zoom breakpoint fires: at 720x450 CSS the two-card split correctly collapses to one pane.

defects.defect: The first drag-to-reorder of every session permutes the entire library and the scramble persists to localStorage. Drags 2..n are correct, hiding the defect from any two-drag manual test.
defects.evidence: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183-197; useFilteredList.ts:9; node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:14-15,32-35,78-88; node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js:2002-2028; usePaletteStore.ts:153-167. Measured (scratchpad/drag2.mjs, 3/3 fresh WebKit contexts): `store before: P1,P2,P3,P4,P5` / `store after : P3,P4,P2,P5,P1` / `(intended: P2,P3,P1,P4,P5)`. Same session: `drag#1 *** WRONG ***`, `drag#2 OK`, `drag#3 OK`.
defects.mechanism: `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, …)` passes a plain array, not the ref. `useFilteredList` returns `items.value` unchanged for an empty query, so that array IS the object the `savedPalettes` computed caches. vueuse's `defaultOptions.onUpdate` is spread BEFORE caller options and the caller supplies only `onEnd`, so the default survives; `moveArrayElement` takes the no-copy branch (`isRef` false) and `array.splice(from,1)` runs synchronously with the re-insert deferred to nextTick. SortableJS dispatches update->sort->end, so `onEnd` then maps N-1 ids; `reorderPalettes` places those and appends the two orphans at the tail. Traced by hand to `[P3,P4,P2,P5,P1]` — the exact measured value.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/drag2.mjs — seed 5 palettes into localStorage key `color-palettes`, load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes, drag row 1's `.drag-handle` onto row 3's centre, read the store. Deterministic 3/3 in fresh contexts.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the useSortable/SortableJS dependency. Reorder is a model operation on an ordinal and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2 already specifies it as one (Space grabs, Up/Down move, Home/End, Space drops, Escape cancels, announce `position of total`). Emit `move(id, delta)` against the store's own order — never a filtered projection, never a captured array. Kills D-1, D-1b and D-9 together and removes a library.

defects.defect: Reordering while a search filter is active silently rewrites the positions of palettes the user cannot see.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:190-195 maps only `pm.filteredSaved.value` ids; usePaletteStore.ts:163-165 appends everything not in the id list. Measured: `store before: P1,P2,P3,zebra one,zebra two` -> query 'zebra' -> swap the 2 visible rows -> `store after : zebra two,zebra one,P1,P2,P3`.
defects.mechanism: `onEnd` builds the id list from the filtered projection; `reorderPalettes` treats that partial list as the head of the new order and appends the unmatched remainder, so any filtered reorder hoists every match to the top of the library and demotes every non-match.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/drag2.mjs (TEST4) — seed 3 palettes plus 2 named 'zebra …', type 'zebra' in the search field, drag the first visible row onto the second, read the store.
defects.proposedCure: Same as D-1: the reorder verb must address the store's order, and a filtered view must either disable reorder or map the moved ordinal back through the projection before writing.

defects.defect: The pastel-rainbow identity — one of exactly two sanctioned colour-bearing text sites in the product — is chromatically dead in dark mode; it renders as white with an imperceptible tint.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §2 verbatim: 'Both coordinates render in light and dark.' Measured live root tokens: LIGHT `--palettes-ramp-title-{0,1,2}` C = 0.188343 / 0.188343 / 0.124795 (mean 0.16716); DARK C = 0.033662 / 0.021053 / 0.023120 (mean 0.02594) — dark is 15.5% of light, a 6.44x collapse. Ramp arc dE(OKLab) first->last: 0.2071 light vs 0.0374 dark (5.5x less). Pixel-sampled from the tracked Safari captures: light mean C 0.1649, dark mean C 0.0227, versus neutral `My` ink C 0.0061/0.0063. Contrast measured against the sampled dark plate rgb(94,72,65): shipped ink 7.47:1 against a declared RAMP_LARGE_TEXT_CONTRAST_FLOOR of 3 — a 2.49x overshoot.
defects.mechanism: `certifyAccentInk`'s cusp walk does not stop AT the floor; it runs to the end of its reach, landing at OKLCH L 0.958 where the sRGB gamut cusp permits almost no chroma at any hue. The entire chroma budget is spent buying contrast nobody asked for. Not a gamut limit: oklch(0.72 0.150 329.8) -> rgb(216,127,209) measures 3.19:1 in gamut, and oklch(0.75 0.140 9.8) -> rgb(248,134,154) measures 3.57:1 — C ~0.14-0.15 at the declared floor, ~6x the shipped dark chroma.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with colorScheme dark and read `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--palettes-ramp-title-0..2')`. Or open docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-dark/palettes.png and compare with the light capture; scratchpad/ramp-chroma.py reproduces the pixel numbers.
defects.proposedCure: Make the walk stop at the floor by bisection instead of running to reach, and hold chroma at the cusp for the L actually chosen. The dark arm then lands in the pastel band the resolver's own doc promises, at the same chroma register as light.

defects.defect: The per-site 'floor split' machinery — a second resolver invocation, three extra root tokens and a per-instance inline :style override with duplicated OKLCH literals — moves the rendered title by dE(OKLab) 0.0138 on one of three stops in light, and by exactly zero in dark.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:171-175. Measured light: `--palettes-ramp-title-0/1` are byte-identical to `--palettes-ramp-0/1` (dE 0); stop 2 differs by dE(OKLab) 0.0138 — below the OKLab JND. Measured dark: all three title tokens byte-identical to the menu tokens (dE 0).
defects.mechanism: Two full `resolvePalettesRamp` calls at two floors (3 vs 4.5) converge on the same output because the walk overshoots both floors to the same reach limit; the per-instance override therefore aliases tokens onto themselves.
defects.reproduction: Read `--palettes-ramp-{0,1,2}` and `--palettes-ramp-title-{0,1,2}` from the live root in both schemes and diff them.
defects.proposedCure: Delete `rampTitleVars` and the whole `--palettes-ramp-title-*` family. With a floor-stopping walk (D-2's cure) the two sites differ by the honest amount their two floors imply, expressed once in `useViewAccents` and consumed through the one `.palettes-ramp-text` recipe — one resolver, three tokens, zero per-instance style.

defects.defect: The desktop composition is an exact 50.00/50.00 split with an unrelated Picker occupying the Library inspector's slot, and the route is a page wearing a Card.
defects.evidence: Measured live at 1440x900: picker card x=199 512x684.7, palettes card x=729 512x684.7 — protagonist share 512/1024 = 50.00%. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 1 requires 61.8-66.7%; §3.1's Library row requires a field at 64-66.7% plus a 'selected action/history inspector' at 33.3-36% and says 'Browse cannot stand in for Library'. §3 law 2: 'It never receives half the viewport.' PROPORTION-AUDIT §4 PR-04 already rules this exact family REMOVE. REPORT.json records `canvas: 2` on the route. PalettesPane.vue:2 opens `<Card tier="resting" class="… overflow-y-auto … h-full">`; §3.1 says Card 'is never the default page primitive'.
defects.mechanism: The route was composed as a single Card rather than as the owner workspace chassis, so the second 50% had to be backfilled with whatever instrument was adjacent, and the ratified inspector region has nowhere to exist.
defects.reproduction: Load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 1440x900 and read the bounding rects of the two `.pane-scroll-fade` cards; also visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the Card root. Compose the route as the §3.1 owner workspace chassis: owner-state selector, palette field at 64-66.7%, selected-palette inspector at 33.3-36% that collapses when nothing is selected. This one move also supplies the seat D-4 lacks and the home D-7 needs.

defects.defect: The palette card is a pointer-only `role="article"` div with no focusable seat, no aria-pressed, and byte-identical rest and hover styles. Expansion is unreachable by keyboard in every engine; in Safari the entire library is unreachable.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 verbatim: 'not a clickable role=article … One native named <button type="button"> spans its specimen/identity region'. Measured: tag DIV, role article, tabindex null, aria-pressed null, aria-selected null, cursor pointer. Card heights: before [100,100,100]; after POINTER click [172.17,100,100]; after 6xTab+Enter [100,100,100]. Chromium pane tab order: search -> 'Delete all saved palettes' -> 'Palette menu' x3 — no palette. WebKit default tab set: the pane's only stop is the search input. Hover probe: rest === hover is `true` (byte-identical computed backgroundColor/boxShadow/outlineWidth/transform/opacity/filter).
defects.mechanism: With no inspector to select into (D-3), no seat owns selection, so activation was attached to the article root via a bare @click and never given a control element, a focus state or a hover state.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/tab.mjs (WebKit) and scratchpad/tabc.mjs (Chromium); node scratchpad/pp3.mjs for the rest-vs-hover comparison and the pointer-click height delta.
defects.proposedCure: Implement the §3.1 tuple exactly: a noninteractive article root plus one native `<button type="button" aria-pressed>` spanning specimen+identity that owns activation, visible selection and focus and drives the restored inspector.

defects.defect: `role="list"` owns `role="article"` children — structurally invalid ARIA; assistive tech reports an empty list wrapping loose articles.
defects.evidence: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets role="list"; every child PaletteCard root carries role="article" (measured on all rendered cards). ARIA 1.2 declares `listitem` a required owned element of `list`.
defects.mechanism: The grid was given a list role for landmark reasons while the child kept an article role for entity reasons; neither side reconciled the owned-element requirement.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with seeded palettes and inspect `document.querySelector('.palette-card-grid').getAttribute('role')` against the children's roles.
defects.proposedCure: Children become `role="listitem"` wrapping the article, or the list role is dropped and the grid becomes a plain container once the button seat supplies the semantics.

defects.defect: The no-search-results state renders the empty-LIBRARY invitation: 'No saved palettes yet.' plus 'Add colors above, then save the set.', while the badge in the same header reads 5. The statement is false and the recovery advice is wrong.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:75-81 — `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` with one hard-coded copy set. Reproduced live with 5 seeded palettes and query 'zzzqqq' (screenshot scratchpad/F.png): header Badge '5', sr-only '(5 saved)', body '· EMPTY PLATE ·' / 'No saved palettes yet.' / 'Add colors above, then save the set.' — 200px apart in one 512px card. The delete-all trigger also survives (its v-if keys on savedPalettes.length, line 62), so at zero visible results the only two focusable controls are the search box and 'Delete all saved palettes'.
defects.mechanism: The component conflates 'the collection is empty' with 'the projection is empty'; one copy set describes two semantically opposite states.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/pp2.mjs 3 (case F) — seed 5 palettes, fill the search field with 'zzzqqq', screenshot and read the empty region's text.
defects.proposedCure: Give PaletteCardGrid a `filtered` empty arm: 'No palettes match "…".' with a Clear search action. EmptyState already ships the second-variant machinery (role=alert, detail slot, action slot) that the grid never forwards. Route the changed-result count through the owning status region per §5.1.

defects.defect: The empty region is a polite live region that announces a false statement mid-typing whenever a filter drops results to zero.
defects.evidence: EmptyState.vue:29 — `role="status"` (implicit aria-live=polite) on the invitation. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7: 'never a routine live region: ordinary text uses aria-live="off"'.
defects.mechanism: Every >=1 -> 0 results transition mounts the status region, and its content is the empty-library copy of D-5.
defects.reproduction: With 5 seeded palettes, type into the search field until results reach zero with a screen reader active; the announced string is '· empty plate · No saved palettes yet. Add colors above, then save the set.'
defects.proposedCure: aria-live off on the invitation; a single owned status region reports the changed result count once, per §5.1's in-route-filter row.

defects.defect: Export failure is `console.warn`-only — the exact construct the palette contract forbids by name.
defects.evidence: usePaletteExport.ts:22 `catch (e) { console.warn("Export failed:", e); }`, mounted at PalettesPane.vue:211 and wired at PalettesPane.vue:96. PALETTE-CONTRACT.md Appendix W51 line 172, verbatim: 'A serializer either yields the bytes below or a visible terminal/retryable operation state—never a partial download or `console.warn`-only result.' PROPORTION-AUDIT §4 PR-08 rules the family ADD-AFFORDANCE.
defects.mechanism: The export action was wired without a return channel, so the pane has no value to render and the composable swallows the throw.
defects.reproduction: Trigger a PNG export that throws (e.g. quota) via the card's export menu; nothing appears in the UI. Source-level: the catch block has no UI path.
defects.proposedCure: `onExport` returns a typed result; the restored inspector renders the durable operation state Appendix W51 §8 already specifies (captured | ready | retryable-failure | terminal-failure | handoff-initiated with a closed failureCode union). No new component, no toast.

defects.defect: The Library port has no operation-state surface at all — no pending, no error, no durable result — so publish runs live-triggered with no feedback, its only truth is a transient in-card flourish, one outcome path is discarded, and corrupt storage renders as an empty library.
defects.evidence: usePalettePorts.ts:145-161 — sixteen members, none a pending/error/status flag; the adjacent browsePort exposes browsing/browseError/loadingMore/sortLoading. PalettesPane.vue:199-209 awaits a network publish with the trigger live (no disabled, no aria-busy). Line 206 `card.showFeedback(...)` is the only result, against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 'never carries the only truth'. Lines 202-204 `if (id == null) return;` discards the outcome and is dead code (savedPalettes is typed `Palette & { id: string }`, usePaletteStore.ts:50-53). usePaletteStore.ts:24-31 returns defaultStore on a corrupt parse, which VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 names as the first forbidden rendering of a storage fault.
defects.mechanism: With no inspector (D-3) there is no surface that could hold entity-scoped state, so the port was never given the vocabulary and every outcome had to be transient or dropped.
defects.reproduction: Source-level for all four sub-cases; the publish path additionally: click Publish on a saved palette and observe that the trigger stays enabled for the whole round trip and that a failure leaves no visible trace.
defects.proposedCure: Add `pending: Set<id>`, `error: Map<id, OperationError>` and a durable `lastResult` to libraryPort and render them in the inspector; delete the unreachable id guard; give corrupt storage the §7 recovery article instead of `return defaultStore`.

defects.defect: The pane declares glass but paints none — 66-75% opaque with `backdrop-filter: none` over a live animated chromatic ground — and the 462px column carries five shadow recipes with two opposed horizontal light directions, including three cartoon casters per palette card inside a card that is itself a caster.
defects.evidence: Measured: light `background-color: oklab(0.928273 0.005506 0.013193 / 0.664)`, dark `oklab(0.395241 0.009680 0.016528 / 0.7536)`, both `backdrop-filter: none`. Shadows — pane `8px 8px 0` (down-right); `.search-seated` `-2px 2px 0`; editor `-2px 2px 0`; delete-all `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.4)`; each palette card `-3px 3px 0, -5px 5px 0, -7px 7px 0` (down-left). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §2 'Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well'; §7 'not cartoon casters stacked within casters'; §3.1 fixes `shadow=false` for every Library entity Card; PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-05 rules caster shadows REMOVE.
defects.mechanism: `tier="resting"` is declared but resolves to no blur, so the surface is a tinted film; and each nested species brought its own shadow recipe without any pane-level light-source law.
defects.reproduction: Read computed `backgroundColor`/`backdropFilter`/`boxShadow` on `.pane-scroll-fade` and on any `[role=article]` at /#/palettes; the opposed directions are visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/palettes.png.
defects.proposedCure: One light source for the whole route, declared once. Entity cards take the §3.1 tuple (`shadow=false`); the pane either earns blur by being real glass or becomes an opaque well. Retiring the Card root (D-3's cure) removes the outer caster entirely.

defects.defect: The reorder handle is an unnamed, unfocusable 16x16 bare `<svg>`, and the §5.2 keyboard reorder grammar is entirely absent.
defects.evidence: Measured: tag svg, rect 16x16, aria-label null, role null, tabindex null, no <title>, and `.focus()` leaves `document.activeElement === handle` false. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5: 'An optional reorder handle remains a separate named control.' PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 5: 'operable ornaments without names are forbidden.' §5.2's vertical-list reorder row (Space grabs, Up/Down move, Home/End, Space drops, Escape cancels, announce `position of total`) has no implementation.
defects.mechanism: Reorder was delegated wholesale to SortableJS via a `handle: '.drag-handle'` selector, so the affordance is a CSS hook rather than a control.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/tab.mjs — the handle probe prints `{tag:"svg", focused:false, tabindex:null, aria:null, role:null, title:null}`.
defects.proposedCure: A named `<button>` reorder control per row emitting `move(id, delta)`, implementing §5.2's grab/move/drop/cancel/announce contract; pointer drag layers over the same verb. Shared with D-1's cure.

defects.defect: The library is a fixed-height inner scroller at every viewport, so the document never scrolls — at 200% zoom 61% of the content is hidden inside a nested scroller on a page that cannot scroll.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:2 `h-full overflow-y-auto`. Measured `scrollHeight - clientHeight`: 1440x900/5 palettes 113px; 1440x900/40 palettes 4033px; 390x844 154px; 320x720 278px; 720x450 (= 200% browser zoom on 1440x900) 533px hidden inside a 512x338 plate with `document scroll = 0`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 6: 'Mobile uses one document-scrolling stage'.
defects.mechanism: The Card-as-page decision forces the route body to be a fixed-height plate, so its content must scroll internally; the sticky PaneHeader then sticks inside that inner scroller rather than the page. No virtualization or pagination exists, so 40 palettes put 40 cards and 68 focusables in the DOM.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/pp2.mjs 6 (40 palettes, 320px) and scratchpad/pp3.mjs (720x450) — read `pane.scrollHeight - pane.clientHeight` and `documentElement.scrollHeight - clientHeight`.
defects.proposedCure: Retire the Card root (D-3's cure) so the route body is a page region and the document scrolls; add pagination or windowing above a threshold count.

defects.defect: There is no owner-state selector; the four non-interchangeable owner states the constitution names are collapsed into one undifferentiated list, so there is no Trash and therefore no undo behind the bulk delete.
defects.evidence: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7: 'Device Drafts, unpublished Server Workspaces, Published lineages, and Trash are explicit, non-interchangeable owner states.' §3.1 puts the 'owner-state selector' first in the Library mobile sequence. PalettesPane renders one `PaletteCardGrid` over `pm.filteredSaved` with no state tabs; measured DOM at 40 palettes shows a single flat list.
defects.mechanism: The composition was built around a single local `savedPalettes` array, so no state axis exists to select on.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes with any number of palettes; no owner-state control is present in the DOM.
defects.proposedCure: Introduce the four owner states as a P092 SegmentedTabs owner-state selector over a state-partitioned store, restoring Trash as the undo destination for D-16.

defects.defect: The route has zero H1; the Library identity is an `<h3>` at 41.888px, ranked peer to a numeric readout that is also an `<h3>`.
defects.evidence: REPORT.json records `"h1": 0` for /#/palettes in all four Safari matrices; live probe confirms. Full heading outline: `H3 "92.0%,88.8,20.0"` (the Picker readout) and `H3 "My Palettes"` (Fraunces 41.888px, weight 400) — rendered by PaneHeader.vue:28. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1: 'Each route has one H1'; §5.1 makes the H1 the focus target for every in-app route change; PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 11: 'A display-sized readout is not therefore a document heading.'
defects.mechanism: PaneHeader emits an h3 because it was designed as a card header, not a route heading; with the Card-as-page decision there is nothing above it to be the h1.
defects.reproduction: Load /#/palettes and evaluate `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length` — returns 0 in every matrix.
defects.proposedCure: The shell owns one stable `<main>` and one `<h1>` per route (already the §4.1/§5.1 design); PaneHeader's title becomes that h1 for the Library route, restoring both the outline and the §5.1 focus target.

defects.defect: The library search field has no accessible name and is 22px tall on both mobile widths.
defects.evidence: Measured: `aria-label` null, `aria-labelledby` null, `id` empty (so no `<label for>` can exist), only a placeholder. Heights: 24.6px at 1440, 22px at 390 and at 320 — under the 24px target floor. PalettesPane.vue:33-37. Producer gap worth relaying: glass-ui 7.0.0 SearchBar exposes {modelValue, placeholder, icon, tag, size, surface, variant} — no label/aria-label/id prop, and a fall-through aria-label lands on the wrapper, not the input.
defects.mechanism: The consumer supplies no name and the producer exposes no slot for one, so the field ships named only by a placeholder that disappears on input.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/pp2.mjs 1 — the `search` object prints `{aria: null, labelledby: null, id: ""}` with `rect.h` 24.6 / 22.
defects.proposedCure: Add a `label`/`id` prop to glass-ui's SearchBar (BH relay) and supply 'Search your palettes' as the accessible name; raise the field to the control-size rung that clears 24px at every viewport.

defects.defect: `.search-seated` is a hand-rolled per-instance class replicated at three sites, self-labelled 'interim', that duplicates an axis glass-ui already exposes.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:35 `class="search-seated"`; identical application with the identical 'interim, booked onto the P3 seated rung / ASK-D' comment at BrowsePane.vue:12 and admin/AdminPane.vue:14. Recipe at utils.css:132-138 (`--well-bg` fill, `backdrop-filter: none`, 1.5px `--card-edge`, `--shadow-cartoon-sm`). glass-ui 7.0.0 SearchBar accepts `surface?: Surface` with `SURFACES = ["glass","veil","opaque"]` (_shared/axes.d.ts).
defects.mechanism: A producer variant was booked but never landed, so three consumers carry a local class that overrides the producer root.
defects.reproduction: grep -rn 'search-seated' demo/ returns the three consumer sites plus the utils.css definition.
defects.proposedCure: Land the seated register as a glass-ui SearchBar `surface`/`variant` value and delete the class from all three consumers (owner edicts 4 and 5).

defects.defect: The only motion this component authors is a bare `animation: 150` numeric literal with no token, no producer motion axis, and no prefers-reduced-motion branch; ghost styling is a Tailwind utility string smuggled into a behaviour config.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:185-186 `animation: 150, ghostClass: "opacity-30"`. `grep -rn 'animation-slide' demo src` returns nothing — the named token register does not exist in this tree. glass-ui 7.0.0 exposes `MOTIONS = ["full","reduced","off"]` (_shared/axes.d.ts), bypassed. The PRM run (scratchpad/pp2.mjs 4) produced geometry identical to the non-PRM run and there is no PRM branch in the file. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: 'Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry.'
defects.mechanism: SortableJS's `animation` is a JS-driven transform loop that CSS media queries cannot reach, so the reduced-motion contract is structurally unreachable from where the value is set.
defects.reproduction: Run with `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` and drag a row — the 150ms transform animation still plays; no code path consults the query.
defects.proposedCure: Removing SortableJS (D-1's cure) removes the untokenized animation with it; the replacement reorder uses the producer motion axis and CSS transitions that PRM can gate.

defects.defect: Delete all is an orphan glyph owning a 94%-empty layout band, renders as a filled circular chip rather than the 'quiet ghost' its own comment claims, and is the first control a keyboard user reaches after the search field with no Trash to undo it.
defects.evidence: Measured: row rect x=754 w=462, button rect x=1188 w=28 h=28 — 434 of 462px (94%) empty. Computed `background-color: oklab(0.414856 … / 0.6304)`, `border-radius: 9999px`, `box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.4), …`. Chromium pane tab position +1. Source comment PalettesPane.vue:56-61 states the '{n} palettes' line was excised because 'it existed only to left-balance this button' and that the trigger was 'DEMOTED … to a quiet ghost'. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 8: 'Real rendered relation wins over token intent.'
defects.mechanism: The counterweight was removed and the button kept, leaving a right-aligned singleton in a full-width flex row; and `variant="ghost"` still resolves to a plated chip at this size, so the recorded intent and the rendered object disagree.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/fine.mjs — prints the row and button rects plus the computed background/shadow in both schemes; scratchpad/tabc.mjs prints the tab position.
defects.proposedCure: Move the bulk action into the restored inspector's action region or an overflow menu, after per-entity actions in tab order, with Trash (D-11) as the undo destination.

defects.defect: Three dead imports.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:128 imports `watch`, `onMounted`, `nextTick`. `for s in watch onMounted nextTick; do grep -c "\b$s\b" demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue; done` returns 1, 1, 1 — each occurs only in the import statement.
defects.mechanism: Left behind by earlier refactors; no lint rule catches unused named imports in this SFC configuration.
defects.reproduction: Run the grep above.
defects.proposedCure: Delete them.

defects.defect: Pre-3.5 template-ref idioms, two escapes from the type system, and a component-instance record that is never pruned.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:177 `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})`; :180 `ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)`; :181 `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement`; :84 `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.id] = el)"`. `cardRefs` is written on mount and never deleted on unmount.
defects.mechanism: The `$el` cast exists only because a component ref was used where an element ref was needed; the callback ref writes into a reactive map with no matching cleanup.
defects.reproduction: Source-level; the retention is observable by deleting palettes and inspecting `cardRefs` key count.
defects.proposedCure: `useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>` on the grid root removes the `$el` cast and both `any`s; register/unregister card refs in a mounted/unmounted pair, or drop the record once feedback moves to the inspector (D-7).

defects.defect: The count badge and the pane title do not share an optical centre.
defects.evidence: Measured: title y=141.0 h=45.1 centre 163.5; badge y=160.1 h=26.0 centre 173.1 — a 9.6px disagreement, 37% of the badge's own height. A 16.4px Fira Code pill baseline-aligned against a 41.888px Fraunces display glyph.
defects.mechanism: Default inline/baseline alignment inside the h3 flex line, which is conventional for inline badges but not for a count pill beside a display identity.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/fine.mjs — prints both rects and centres in both schemes.
defects.proposedCure: Optically centre the badge against the title's x-height, or move the count into the identity line's own type rung.

defects.defect: The current-palette editor asserts two contradictory materials at once: a dashed placeholder outline and a cast physical shadow.
defects.evidence: Measured: `border: dashed 1px` together with `box-shadow: -2px 2px 0 …`. Visible in every capture and in scratchpad/C.png, D.png.
defects.mechanism: The ghost/dashed treatment was applied for its 'not yet real' reading while the surface also inherited the pane's caster shadow species.
defects.reproduction: Read computed `borderStyle` and `boxShadow` on the 'Start a new palette' container at /#/palettes.
defects.proposedCure: Pick one register: a dashed invitation with no shadow, or a real plate with no dashes.

defects.defect: Two import idioms for one design system, twenty lines apart.
defects.evidence: PalettesPane.vue:129-131 imports Card/Button/Badge via `../ui/*` (verified one-line glass-ui re-exports, demo/ui/card/index.ts), while :141-149 imports Dialog* and SearchBar from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/dialog` and `@mkbabb/glass-ui/search` directly.
defects.mechanism: Two conventions coexist; neither is wrong in isolation but the file uses both.
defects.reproduction: Read PalettesPane.vue:127-152.
defects.proposedCure: Pick one path per producer surface and apply it repo-wide.

defects.defect: The empty-state copy this pane supplies lands two of its three lines outside the closed type matrix, and the placeholder message renders bolder than the pane's own identity.
defects.evidence: Measured computed styles for PalettesPane.vue:78-80's copy: '· empty plate ·' Fira Code 14.384px uppercase ls 2.589px (defensible under the mono-caption carve-out); 'No saved palettes yet.' Fraunces weight 700 at 25.888px; 'Add colors above, then save the set.' Fira Code 16.4px. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4 maps prose/help to `text-prose`, Plus Jakarta Sans, and reserves mono for 'value, code, or provenance' and Fraunces for display/identity; the matrix 'is closed across all eighteen compositions'. The pane title itself renders at weight 400, so the placeholder is bolder than the protagonist (§3 law 8).
defects.mechanism: EmptyState hard-maps its three slots to mono-caption / font-display / mono-small regardless of content class; PalettesPane feeds prose into the mono slots.
defects.reproduction: node scratchpad/pp2.mjs 1 — the `emptyBits` array prints fontSize/fontFamily/fontWeight/letterSpacing for each line.
defects.proposedCure: Map the hint and message slots to `text-prose` (Plus Jakarta Sans) in EmptyState and keep mono only for the caption eyebrow; drop the 700 weight so the invitation stays subordinate to the identity.
